findings.title: Every bid recommendation ignores my remaining budget and my remaining roster slots
findings.rootCause: theoreticalMaxBid is a function of preDraft, aggression, budget advantage, inflation and phase multiplier only; myWinningBid caps it against the richest RIVAL's effective budget. Neither reads myRemaining, mySlotsRemaining, or my own effectiveBudget. The class of number the page calls "Win at" is a competitor-ceiling estimate, not a feasible bid.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:717-731 — `const theoreticalMaxBid = Math.floor(preDraft * (1 + aggression * (budgetAdvantage - 1)) * combinedInflation * phaseMultiplier);` then `const myWinningBid = Math.max(0, Math.min(theoreticalMaxBid, winByCompetitor));` where `winByCompetitor = Math.max(1, competitorCeiling + 1)` and competitorCeiling is `topCompetitorMax`, computed at :479-485 by scanning only `if (i === myTeamIdx) continue;`. Reproduced: after spending all $417 across all 6 slots (myRemaining = 0, mySlotsRemaining = 0, my effectiveBudget = 0), the board still reports Kenyon Sadiq at Max Bid $90 / WIN AT $69, and Caleb Downs at Max Bid $76 / WIN AT $69.
findings.userImpact: The single number the module docstring designates as the headline figure (line 385: "The UI should surface myWinningBid as the headline figure") is unimplementable by the user it is shown to. A user with $12 left is told to bid $69. This is a recommender that does not optimize under, or even respect, the constraint it exists to manage.

findings.area: Draft / auction decision engine — frontend/lib/draft-logic.js, pick-stack.js, auction-power.js, app/draft/page.jsx, app/idptc-rookies/page.jsx, backend /api/dra
findings.title: "Next Best Targets" is a preDraft sort wearing an EV model's clothes
findings.rootCause: surplus = max(0, inflatedFair − myWinningBid). But myWinningBid = min(fair × k, C) where k = (1 + aggression×(BA−1)) × phaseMultiplier is a per-board constant and C = topCompetitorMax + 1 is a league-wide scalar. When k > 1 the max() is zero for everything below the cap; when k < 1 surplus = fair × (1−k), proportional to fair. In both regimes the ranking is a monotone function of preDraft.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1949-1957. Reproduced with the shipped defaults: at draft open nextBestTargets returns exactly 5 rows and `JSON.stringify(returned names) === JSON.stringify(top-5 by preDraft)` evaluates true. After forcing BA to 0, it returns 13 rows in the order Fernando Mendoza, Makai Lemon, Carnell Tate, Jordyn Tyson, Sonny Styles, Caleb Downs … — identical to the undrafted preDraft-descending order. The scarcityBoost term is capped at 10 × 0.3 = 3, versus surplus values in the tens.
findings.userImpact: A panel headed "Next Best Targets" with the subtitle "EV = (fair − winBid) × tag weight + scarcity boost" tells the user nothing the #-column ordering does not already tell them, while implying a value calculation happened. At draft open it shows 5 of 72 players because everything else scores exactly 0.

findings.title: Vendor "Market" dollars are inflated by row count, so KTC overrates literally every rookie it covers
findings.rootCause: _vendor_dollars_for_rookies calls _rookie_dollars_from_values with total=1200 over only the rookies that vendor prices. The Hill formula always distributes the full $1200 across whatever list it receives, so a vendor covering 42 of 72 rookies has its whole column scaled up by roughly 72/42 in aggregate.
findings.evidence: server.py:7058-7068. The comment at 7063-7065 claims a pad that the code does not perform: `# Pad to top_n so the formula stays calibrated against the same / # 72-row Hill curve the picks use.` followed immediately by `values = [r[key] for r in eligible]` and `dollars = _rookie_dollars_from_values(values, total)`. Measured on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json: 42 KTC-eligible rookies in the top-72 pool; Σ KTC dollars = 1200 vs Σ our dollars over the same 42 names = 1016, a 1.181x bias. Row-count-only effect holding values fixed: rank-1 = $134.5 at n=72, $146.5 at n=30, $160.0 at n=20.
findings.userImpact: All 42 KTC-covered rookies register as "KTC overrates us" and feed the "Good to nominate" panel; 25 of them would not after removing the bias. Symmetrically, ZERO rookies qualify for "Best value on the board" (0/42 on the KTC leg, 0/21 on the IDP-only leg), so that panel renders entirely from its backfill branch. The "Market" column on the rookie board carries the same bias.

findings.area: Draft / auction decision engine — frontend/lib/draft-logic.js, pick-stack.js, auction-power.js, app/draft/page.jsx, app/idptc-rookies/page.jsx, backend /api/dra
findings.title: Inflation diverges hyperbolically at the end of every draft, producing absurd late-draft prices
findings.rootCause: inflation = remainingLeague / max(1, totalBudget − soldPreDraft). The denominator is (team budgets) minus (board dollars) — two different accounting scales that happen to both total $1200 only in the synced case. As the pool is drafted, soldPreDraft → totalBudget and the denominator → 0.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:550-551 — `const expectedPoolRemaining = Math.max(1, totalBudget - soldPreDraft); const inflation = remainingLeague / expectedPoolRemaining;`. Reproduced with a pool summing to exactly $1200 and every pick hammering at 75% of fair: inflation reads 58.20 at pick 67, 96.33 at 69, 144.00 at 70, 287.00 at 71 — the last $1 rookie shows Fair $287 / Enforce $229. Reproduced with the shipped DEFAULT_ROOKIES pool (which sums to $1211, not $1200) and everyone paying 60% of fair: at pick 68 the raw denominator is −7, clamps to 1, and inflation = 475, rendering four $1 rookies at Fair $285 / Enforce $228 / Max Bid $1169.
findings.userImpact: The board becomes actively dangerous exactly at the moment it matters most — the endgame with money still on the table. A user following the Enforce column would bid $229 on a $1 dart. With the default seed pool the failure starts around pick 63 of 72.

findings.title: Sleeper-derived draft capital fabricates 52% of the board on live data — and the 503 guard added to prevent exactly this does not fire
findings.rootCause: build_sleeper_derived builds picks for current_season AND current_season+1, but the canonical contract carries slot-level rows only for the current class. Every next-season pick falls through _pick_value_from_contract to a hardcoded flat table. The endpoint's 503 guard fires only when there is NO contract at all.
findings.evidence: src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:96-99 — `# Fallback: flat per-round value.  Round 1 ≈ 7000, Round 2 ≈ 4000, / flat = {1: 7000.0, 2: 4000.0, 3: 2000.0, 4: 1200.0, 5: 700.0, 6: 300.0}` reached from the loop at :175 `for season in (current_season, current_season + 1):`. Guard at server.py:8154 — `if not is_default_league and not latest_contract_data:`. Verified against exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json: 2026 Pick R.SS rows exist; 2027 Pick R.SS rows do not (only '2027 Early 1st' … '2027 Late 6th'). Σ real 2026 values (rounds 1-4) = 156,703 vs Σ fabricated 2027 = 170,400 → the fabricated half takes $625 of the $1,200. A fabricated 2027 first (7000) is priced above a real 2026 pick 1.06 (4945).
findings.userImpact: Every non-default league's draft-capital board — its per-team dollar totals, its bar chart, the budgets the /draft dashboard auto-loads, and the pick-stack values feeding /trade verdicts — is more than half invented, with no field distinguishing the invented rows. CLAUDE.md states this class of failure is "fixed"; it is not.

findings.title: Sleeper-derived path assigns draft slots by roster_id, so pick VALUES follow roster numbering rather than standings
findings.rootCause: The picks loop uses `original_rid = slot` as a stand-in, then prices each pick by that slot. The set of picks per owner is correct (Sleeper's traded_picks is keyed on the original owner's roster_id) but the slot each roster is credited with — and therefore its dollar value — is arbitrary.
findings.evidence: src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:177-181 — `for slot in range(1, actual_num_teams + 1): / original_rid = slot  # stand-in: slot N = original owner roster N / current_rid = traded_map.get((season, round_n, original_rid), original_rid) / ... / value = _pick_value_from_contract(contract, season, round_n, slot)`. The comment at :170-173 asserts "we assume reverse standings — which for this view is fine (ordering is not the point, value + ownership is)" — but value IS slot-dependent, so ordering is precisely the point.
findings.userImpact: In any non-default league, roster_id 1 is permanently credited with the 1.01 dollar value and roster_id 12 with the 1.12 value, irrespective of actual standings. Per-team auction totals — the numbers /draft auto-loads as team budgets — are wrong by construction.

findings.title: "Best value on the board" renders backfill rows as green underrate signals with a double-negative percentage
findings.rootCause: The backfill branch emits rows whose gap is ≤ 0 (the vendor values the player HIGHER than we do), and the renderer unconditionally prefixes a minus sign and applies the green "underrates" styling.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:2185-2186 — `const gap = ourDollar - vendorDollar; const gapPct = vendorDollar > 0 ? gap / vendorDollar : 0;` with no sign guard; rendered at frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:2659-2669 — `style={{ background: "rgba(74, 222, 128, 0.18)", color: "var(--green, #4ade80)" }} title={\`${vendorLabel} underrates by ${Math.round(gapPct * 100)}% ...\`}> −{Math.round(gapPct * 100)}%`. With live data producing zero qualifying rows, every rendered row takes this path: e.g. Jeremiyah Love at ours $132.0 vs KTC $140.0 renders the badge "−-6%" with the tooltip "KTC underrates by -6%".
findings.userImpact: A panel titled "Best value on the board" presents players the market prices ABOVE our board as green bargains, with a literally malformed "−-6%" badge. The signal is inverted for 100% of what a user currently sees.

findings.title: Per-team pick counts are clamped to 6, so a team that trades for extra picks is modelled as if it had not
findings.rootCause: mergeDraftCapitalTeams clamps the feed-derived slot count with `Math.min(feedSlots, DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS)`, contradicting its own docstring three lines above.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1409-1413 — `const initialSlots = picksArray ? Number.isFinite(feedSlots) ? Math.min(feedSlots, DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS) : 0 : Math.min(priorSlots, DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS);` against the docstring at :1399-1402: "When the picks array is present, the slot count is authoritative." DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS = 6 (:53).
findings.userImpact: Slot count feeds effectiveBudgetFor (:294-299), so a team owning 9 picks reserves $5 instead of $8 and its effective budget is overstated — inflating topCompetitorMax and therefore every user-facing "Win at". For the USER's own team it is worse: after 6 picks slotsRemaining hits 0, slotPressure hits 1 (max phase multiplier) and my own effectiveBudget reads $0 while I still hold picks. The Sleeper-derived fallback returns ~8 picks per team (two seasons × 4 rounds), so every non-default league hits this on every load.

findings.title: nominationCandidates' own docstring describes a different, unimplemented algorithm
findings.rootCause: The function was rewritten to a vendor-gap ranker; the original docstring block was left above the new body comment.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1985-2001 documents `expected_price(p) = p.inflatedFair`, `affordable(p) = min(expected_price, topCompetitorMax)`, `tag_weight: avoid → 1.8 / neutral → 1.0 / target → 0`, `risk_of_winning(p)`, and `score(p) = affordable × tag_weight × (1 − risk_factor)`. The body at :2034-2058 computes none of these: there is no risk factor, no 1.8 avoid weight, and the score is `(1 - phasePct) * vendorDollar + phasePct * gapPct * 100`. `drain` is computed at :2059-2061 and never rendered anywhere.
findings.userImpact: Anyone reading the module to understand or modify the nomination logic — including a future agent — will reason about a scoring model that does not exist. Avoid-tagged players get no preference at all despite the documented 1.8x weight.

findings.title: The roster-needs strip claims positional shortages are factored into target priority; nothing reads them
findings.rootCause: computeRosterBreakdown's output is threaded into a chip renderer only. No scoring function takes a position argument.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:4810 — `positions below threshold, factored into target priority`. `needSet` is created at :3688-3691 and grep shows exactly two other uses: passing it into RookieBoard (:4933) and rendering a chip (:1408-1415, `{p.pos && needSet?.has(p.pos) && (NEED)}`). Neither nextBestTargets (draft-logic.js:1941-1976), playerRecommendation (:1839-1921), nominationCandidates (:2005-2088), bestValueOnBoard (:2118-2209) nor the bid math (:706-779) accepts or reads a position.
findings.userImpact: A user is told their roster gaps are influencing the recommendations. They are not. There is no positional need weighting anywhere in the draft engine.

findings.title: DEFAULT_POSITION_MINS is invented and ignores the league's actual roster settings
findings.rootCause: The thresholds are hardcoded and the page never passes the league registry's rosterSettings.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:2421-2429 — `export const DEFAULT_POSITION_MINS = { QB: 3, RB: 4, WR: 5, TE: 2, DL: 3, LB: 3, DB: 3 };` with the docstring at :2413-2419 conceding "Values chosen to fit a 2-QB/2-RB/3-WR/1-TE + flex IDP starter shape common in SF leagues — adjust via options when a league's shape differs significantly." The page calls `computeRosterBreakdown(rosterPlayers || [], allPlayersArray || [])` at :3685 with no third argument, so the defaults always apply. CLAUDE.md documents `leagueKey → sleeperLeagueId + rosterSettings + idpEnabled` as the map the frontend relies on; it is not consulted here.
findings.userImpact: Every league sees the same needs regardless of its starter requirements. In a league with 1 QB the board flags a QB shortage at 2 QBs.

findings.title: hydrateWorkspace silently discards position, assetClass and both vendor dollar fields on every page load
findings.rootCause: The players mapper in hydrateWorkspace projects only four fields, dropping everything replacePlayerPool carefully preserved.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1714-1719 — `return src.map((p, i) => ({ id: ..., rank: ..., name: ..., preDraft: ... }));` — no `pos`, no `assetClass`, no `ktcDollar`, no `idpTradeCalcDollar`. replacePlayerPool at :1579-1595 explicitly carries all four.

findings.title: The live sync path never supplies assetClass, so the IDP/offense vendor routing falls back to a position string the fallback exists to work around
findings.rootCause: replacePlayerPool accepts assetClass and both routing helpers prefer it, but neither code path that actually runs supplies it.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1580-1586 documents the intent: "Authoritative offense/IDP class from the live contract. `nominationCandidates` prefers this over `pos` so a rookie with a missing/blank `position` string is still routed to the right vendor." The auto-sync at frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:3623-3629 pushes `{name, preDraft, pos, ktcDollar, idpTradeCalcDollar}` — no assetClass. The manual sync's preferred serverPool branch hardcodes `assetClass: null` at :4306. The backend never stamps assetClass onto a pick row (server.py:8054-8061).
findings.userImpact: An IDP rookie whose contract `position` is blank routes to KTC, gets no vendor dollar, and drops out of both panels — the exact failure the assetClass field was added to prevent. classifyPos("") returns "other", which is not "idp", so the KTC branch wins.

findings.title: effectiveAuctionPower violates its own documented multiplier bound and amplifies near-equal fields the most
findings.rootCause: The [1−gain, 1+gain] bound applies to the pre-normalization multiplier; the subsequent rescale by Σraw/Σw moves the realized multiplier outside it. Separately, `spread` floors at 0.01×(grand/n), so when MAD is 0 — the natural state of a league before any pick trades — z-scores explode.
findings.evidence: src/api/auction_power.py:68-70 — "``premium_gain`` — max fractional swing of the S-curve. The per-team multiplier is bounded to ``[1 - gain, 1 + gain]`` so the lens can never wildly distort the trusted raw numbers." Production code at frontend/lib/auction-power.js:50 — `const spread = Math.max(mad * 1.4826, 0.01 * (grand / names.length));` and :64 — `const scaled = weighted.map((w) => w * (rawSum / wsum));`. Measured continuous multipliers: a 12-team field at [110, 100×10, 90] gives range [0.6462, 1.3434] and the $90 team is displayed at $58.2; a whale field [1000, 20×9, 10×2] gives 0.5055. A 6-team field at [201,200,200,200,200,199] — a $2 real spread — renders as [227.8, 199.9, 199.9, 199.9, 199.9, 172.5], a $55 spread.
findings.userImpact: The /league draft-capital chart's cyan effective-power marker overstates concentration in exactly the leagues that have none, and the same function feeds the /trade stack-effect adjustment (frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:807-808), so a fabricated concentration signal moves real trade verdicts.

findings.rootCause: The lens was moved client-side; the Python module was kept for its Phase-2 spec and tests.
findings.evidence: src/api/auction_power.py:49-52 — "NOTE: the live UI lens is currently computed client-side from the raw per-team dollars (frontend ``_auction-power.js`` mirrors this module — keep them in lockstep).  This module remains the source of truth + the home of the Phase 2 simulation and the unit tests." `grep -rn effective_auction_power --include=*.py` returns only the definition and tests/api/test_auction_power_parity.py. findings.title: The Target Board budget check ignores the roster-slot limit and over-warns
findings.rootCause: portfolioBuffer subtracts the winning bid of every remaining target, without capping at how many the user can still draft.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:844-849 — `const nonTargetSlotsLeft = Math.max(0, mySlotsRemaining - tbTotals.remainingCount); const portfolioBuffer = myRemaining - tbTotals.remainingWinBid - nonTargetSlotsLeft;` where remainingWinBid (:837) sums all undrafted board slots. Reproduced: 2 slots remaining, $413 remaining, 6 targets summing to $414 → buffer −1 → "Short $1 — trim a target or lower your ceiling". The two most expensive targets I could actually take cost $138.
findings.userImpact: The one place on /draft that checks a budget constraint gives a false shortage warning whenever the wishlist is longer than the roster space — which is the normal way a target board is used (the cap is 6, and slots run down as the draft proceeds).

findings.title: DEFAULT_ROOKIES sums to $1211 while its own comment claims $1200 — and the mismatch is what breaks late-draft inflation on a pristine board
findings.rootCause: Seed data drift; the comment was never updated and the test codified the wrong number as correct.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:177-179 — "Verbatim from the Inflation tab (columns A-C).  Sums to $1200 to keep / the league-wide accounting consistent with the sheet." Computed sum of DEFAULT_ROOKIES.preDraft = 1211 across 72 rows; DEFAULT_TEAMS budgets sum to 1200. frontend/__tests__/draft-logic.test.js:46 pins the real value: `it("72 rookies totaling $1211 of PreDraft value (CSV verbatim)")`.

findings.title: Draft-capital team totals are summed from workbook column Q while the displayed per-pick dollars come from column L
findings.rootCause: The picks loop reads `dollar` from pick_values_per_slot (L2:L73) for the payload but accumulates `val` (the Q45:Q116 value) into team_totals_decimal.
findings.evidence: server.py:7973-7977 — `dollar = (float(pick_values_per_slot[overall_idx]) if overall_idx < len(pick_values_per_slot) else float(val))` stamped into `dollarValue`/`adjustedDollarValue`/`originalDollarValue` at :7985-7990 — then :8000-8001 `team_totals_decimal.setdefault(owner_team, 0.0); team_totals_decimal[owner_team] += float(val)`. The comment at :7971-7972 explicitly names L authoritative. Verified by direct xlsx parse: Q and L are currently identical for all 72 rows, so the divergence is latent, not live.
findings.userImpact: None today. The moment the user edits L without editing Q (the exact scenario the code comment at :7506-7511 anticipates — "Using L directly (instead of re-rounding the Q-column expansion-averaged values)"), a team's auctionDollars will stop equalling the sum of its own picks' dollarValue, silently.

findings.title: The overpay warning in the draft modal renders a doubled dollar sign
findings.rootCause: A literal `$` in JSX text immediately precedes an expression whose formatter already prefixes `$`.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:809-811 — `The top rival can only bid $\n{fmt$(stats.topCompetitorMax)} — you don't need to pay more`. fmt$ returns `$68`, so the sentence renders "The top rival can only bid $$68".

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: The Value column silently switches from the Hill-curve board to the raw scraper composite for 260 rows, and 158 of them display a LARGER number than the deepest genuinely-priced player
findings.rootCause: `_materializePlayerArrayRow` sets `full: Math.round(backendValue || rawValues.full)` where `rawValues.full = displayValue || finalAdjusted || overall`. When the canonical pipeline declines to price a row it stamps `rankDerivedValue: null` and `values.displayValue: null`, leaving `values.overall`/`values.finalAdjusted` holding the pre-pipeline scraper composite. The client promotes that number into the same column, with the same formatting, the same value-band badge and the same sort key as real Hill values.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1008 — `full: Math.round(backendValue || rawValues.full),` and the render at frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1050 — `const val = Math.round(row.rankDerivedValue || row.values?.full || 0);`. Live contract: Devin Bush `values={overall:2549, rawComposite:2549, finalAdjusted:2549, displayValue:null}`, `rankDerivedValue:null` → row displays 2,549, band 'D — Depth value (2000-3999)'. Malachi Moore, the last backend-ranked player (#740): `rankDerivedValue:757` → displays 757, band 'F — Fringe'. 260 of 1,072 rows take the fallback; 249 display a non-zero value; 158 display more than 757.
findings.userImpact: A user sorting or scanning by Value sees Devin Bush (a rotational LB the pipeline refused to price) at 2,549 — 3.4× the value of the deepest player the model actually priced. Sorting the board by Value descending places him at display position 224, interleaved among real top-225 assets while his rank cell reads '#905'. Any trade evaluated off the displayed number for one of these 216 players is evaluated on a scale the trade engines never use — `finder.py`, `suggestions.py`, `angle.py` and `waiver.py` all read `rankDerivedValue`, which is null here. The CSV export carries the same mixed column with no marker.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: 216 players (20% of the board) carry a client-invented rank in the # column, and those numbers are array indices that count unranked picks
findings.rootCause: `buildRows` assigns `computedConsensusRank = i + 1` over the whole sorted array — including the 116 picks the backend deliberately left unranked — and then uses it as `r.rank` for any non-pick row the backend did not stamp.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1359-1373 — `rows.forEach((r, i) => { r.computedConsensusRank = i + 1; … } else { r.rank = r.computedConsensusRank; }`. Live: 740 rows carry a backend rank (max 740); 216 non-pick rows get client ranks #857-#1072. The # column therefore reads 738, 739, 740, then '—' for 44 picks, then jumps to 857. CLAUDE.md describes these as 'players past the backend's OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT (800)' — the backend's limit is 800 (data_contract.py:60) but it stamps only 740, so ranks 741-856 exist on no board at all.
findings.userImpact: A 216-row block of the board is numbered by the client. Those numbers feed `resolvedRank`, the rank sort, `positionRankByName` (so QB/RB/LB positional ranks past the priced board are client-derived), `isEligibleForAnalysis`, and every rank cap in edge-helpers. They are not comparable to backend ranks: they are offset by the pick count, and the 741-856 gap makes the discontinuity visible. Duplicate # values are not structurally prevented — they are avoided today only because the backend's 740-rank ceiling happens to leave a 71-slot gap.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: Four different thresholds turn the same backend signal into three contradictory BUY/SELL verdicts on screen simultaneously
findings.rootCause: `marketGapDirection` is stamped once by the backend with no threshold, then re-thresholded independently by three consumers: the Edge column recomputes the means and requires a 10-rank gap; PlayerPopup's banner requires 3; the advanced filter requires nothing.
findings.evidence: Backend: `src/api/data_contract.py:2788-2793` — `if diff > 0: return "retail_premium"` (no threshold). Edge column: `frontend/lib/display-helpers.js:164` — `if (diff < MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF) { … kind: "aligned" }` with `MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF = 10` (thresholds.js:46). Popup: `frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:968` — `if (!Number.isFinite(magnitude) || magnitude < MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP)` with `MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP = 3` (:949). Filter: `frontend/lib/player-filters.js:182-184` — `const want = c.edge === "buy" ? "consensus_premium" : "retail_premium"; if (dir !== want) return false;`. Measured on the live board: 136 of 420 rows with a backend direction render as HOLD/aligned in the Edge column; 79 rows show a 'Buy Low'/'Sell High' banner in PlayerPopup while the row that opened it says HOLD (Brock Bowers #2 SELL/HOLD, Lamar Jackson #10 BUY/HOLD, Joe Burrow #13 BUY/HOLD); 79 of 249 rows matched by the 'buy' filter and 57 of 171 matched by 'sell' display HOLD.
findings.userImpact: Filtering the board to 'Edge: buy' returns a list in which a third of the rows say HOLD in the Edge column. Clicking any of those opens a drawer with a green 'Buy Low' box. The user has no way to tell which threshold is the product's opinion.

findings.title: The Edge rail prints total source dispersion but labels it as the buy/sell gap
findings.rootCause: `topRetailPremium`/`topConsensusPremium` gate on `marketGapDirection` but format the detail string from `sourceRankSpread` — max-minus-min across all sources — instead of `marketGapMagnitude`, the retail-vs-consensus difference the label describes.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/edge-helpers.js:358 — ``detail: `Buy +${r.sourceRankSpread} ranks`,`` and :336 — ``detail: `Sell +${r.sourceRankSpread} ranks`,``. Live board: Kenneth Walker renders 'Buy +25 ranks'; his `marketGapMagnitude` is 0.6. Trevor Lawrence 'Buy +20 ranks' vs 3.5. Nico Collins 'Buy +23 ranks' vs 9.8. Jalen Hurts 'Buy +22 ranks' vs 10.1. 93 rows qualify for the buy rail.
findings.userImpact: The rail is the fastest-read surface on the page and its headline number is off by up to 40× in the wrong direction — it makes near-aligned players look like large mispricings. Kenneth Walker is presented as a 25-rank buy-low when retail and consensus differ by half a rank on him.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: PlayerPopup's 'Value chain — how we got N' ends on a different number than N on 87% of rows, by a median of 282 points
findings.rootCause: `computeValueChain` reconstructs only the anchor and α-shrunk-subgroup stages, then the header claims those stages explain `values.full`. The live pipeline applies ~11 further stages after that point (TE basis conversion, market corridor clamp, single-source haircut, two-way boost, pick-year discount, pick tethering, count-aware aggregation). None are modelled and none is disclosed.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:612 — `const adjusted = Math.round(anchor + alpha * subgroupDelta);` and :1020 — ``Value chain — how we got {Math.round(values.full || 0).toLocaleString()}``. Measured across the live board: 885 of 1,015 rows with a chain end on a value different from the header. |Δ| p50 = 282, p90 = 878, p99 = 1,590, max = 3,029. Bijan Robinson (#3): header 'how we got 9,706', single chain stage reads 9,999. Drake Maye (#5): header 9,579, chain 9,058. Lamar Jackson (#10): header 8,904, chain 8,280.
findings.userImpact: This is the product's transparency surface — the thing a user opens to decide whether to trust a number. It presents an arithmetic derivation that does not arrive at the number, with no remainder row and no caveat. A user checking the math concludes either that the value is wrong or that the explanation is; both undermine every downstream trade decision the board informs.

findings.title: PlayerPopup computes its own source-agreement verdict and contradicts the confidence badge on the row that opened it
findings.rootCause: `consensusText` computes a coefficient of variation over per-source value contributions with client thresholds 0.15/0.30, an entirely separate metric from the backend's percentile rank-spread bucketing.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:857-863 — `const cv = mean > 0 ? Math.sqrt(variance) / mean : 0; if (cv < 0.15) return 'Strong consensus …'; if (cv < 0.30) return 'Moderate agreement …'; return 'Sources disagree significantly …'`. Backend: `_compute_confidence_bucket` (data_contract.py:1895-1905) buckets on percentile spread vs 0.08/0.20, and `hasSourceDisagreement` (:7716-7719) tests percentile spread vs 0.10 + depth allowance. Live: 25 rows where the popup says 'Sources disagree significantly' while the badge says High confidence and hasSourceDisagreement is false (Carson Schwesinger #42, Sonny Styles #61, Myles Garrett #80, CJ Allen #144, Ernest Jones #192, Quay Walker #197); 22 rows where the popup says 'Strong consensus' while hasSourceDisagreement is true.
findings.userImpact: Myles Garrett shows a green 'High' confidence badge on the board and, one click later, an italic line reading 'Sources disagree significantly — high volatility player'. Two of the product's own trust signals openly disagree, on a metric the backend already computes and stamps.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: The methodology panel publishes a value formula that is neither the live curve nor the current fallback constants, understating the board by up to 16.6%
findings.rootCause: Hardcoded prose constants that were never updated when the pipeline moved to scope-level percentile curves and when the rank-form fallback was refit.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/board-sections.jsx:34 — `value = max(1, min(9999, round(1 + 9998 / (1 + ((rank-1)/45)^1.10))))`. Live pipeline: `percentile_to_value` (src/canonical/player_valuation.py:371-410) with `HILL_PERCENTILE_C = 0.1100`, `HILL_PERCENTILE_S = 1.110` (:126-127), scope-routed across four curves. The contract's own `hillCurves` block confirms offense midpoint 54.89 / slope 1.11, idp 41.417, global 55.888 / 0.725, rookie 76.347 / 0.885. The rank-form fallback that the prose's SHAPE matches uses midpoint 65.4 / slope 0.910 (:82-83). Reproduced numerically: rank 12 → 8,248 published vs 8,562 live; rank 50 → 4,766 vs 5,315 (549 points, 10.3%); rank 200 → 1,632 vs 1,932; rank 500 → 663 vs 795 (16.6%). The same stale pair is the fallback in HillCurveExplorer.jsx:50.
findings.userImpact: A user who reproduces the published formula to sanity-check the board gets numbers 10-17% below what the board shows through the entire mid-range, and concludes the values are inflated. The panel also asserts a single rank curve when the live board runs four scope-specific percentile curves against a fixed 500-rank reference.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: Both the methodology panel and the confidence tooltip publish a confidence rule the backend retired; half the 'High' badges violate it
findings.rootCause: The frontend documents `_CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH`/`_MEDIUM` (30/80 ordinal spread), which the backend reaches only when percentile spread is unavailable. The live path buckets on percentile spread 0.08/0.20.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/board-sections.jsx:31 — 'High = 2+ sources, spread ≤ 30. Medium = 2+ sources, spread ≤ 80. Low = single source or spread > 80.' and frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:150-154 — the same text as the tooltip fallback. Backend `_compute_confidence_bucket` (data_contract.py:1895-1905): `if percentile_spread is not None: if percentile_spread <= _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_HIGH … elif source_rank_spread is not None: if source_rank_spread <= _CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH`. Live board: 50 of 108 'High' rows have `sourceRankSpread > 30` (max 485); 139 of 228 'Medium' rows have spread > 80 (max 507); 42 'Low' rows have spread ≤ 80 with 2+ sources. thresholds.js:8 still claims these constants 'mirror values in src/api/data_contract.py'.
findings.userImpact: About half of every confidence badge on the board is explained by a rule it demonstrably does not satisfy. On the mobile/compact view the backend's real `confidenceLabel` is pruned (compact_view.py:56), so mobile users see ONLY the wrong explanation.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: The compact (mobile) view prunes four fields the rankings UI reads, flipping BUY/SELL labels and blanking the Consensus column
findings.rootCause: `compact_view._PRUNED_PLAYER_FIELDS` drops `effectiveSourceRanks`, `anomalyFlags`, `confidenceLabel` and `blendedSourceRank`, but `marketEdge`, `rowChips`, `confidenceExplain` and the Consensus column all consume them. `preferredDataView()` routes every small-viewport or low-memory device to that view.
findings.evidence: src/api/compact_view.py:51-70 lists all four in `_PRUNED_PLAYER_FIELDS`; frontend/lib/device-profile.js:103-108 — `if (isMobileProfile() || isSlowNetwork()) return "compact";`. Consumers: display-helpers.js:110-113 falls back from `effectiveSourceRanks` to the PRE-Hampel `sourceRanks`; rankings-helpers.js:144-147 needs `anomalyFlags`; page.jsx:1038-1040 renders `blendedSourceRank ?? '—'`. Measured by simulating the prune on the live board: 8 rows change their Edge verdict (Patrick Mahomes #22 '—'→'BUY', Emeka Egbuka #34 HOLD→SELL, Rashee Rice #69 HOLD→BUY, Jayden Daniels #12 '—'→'HOLD'); 52 rows lose their '!' anomaly chip; all 800 rows with a Consensus value render '—'.
findings.userImpact: The same player gets a different trade verdict on a phone than on a desktop, from the same account and the same scrape — and the backend's own comment at data_contract.py:7666-7672 says `effectiveSourceRanks` was published specifically so 'the same player could NOT show conflicting edge signals across UI surfaces'. findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: The playersArray materializer drops isStructurallySingleSource and sourceAudit, making the 'solo' chip unreachable and degrading every '1-src' tooltip
findings.rootCause: `_materializeLegacyDictRow` copies both fields (:1234, :1238-1241); `_materializePlayerArrayRow` copies neither, despite the in-file instruction to keep the two materializers in lockstep. The array path is the live desktop path.
findings.evidence: Missing from frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:987-1129 (compare :1234 `isStructurallySingleSource: Boolean(player.isStructurallySingleSource),` and :1238 `sourceAudit: …` in the legacy materializer). Consumer: frontend/lib/rankings-helpers.js:130-143 — `if (row?.isSingleSource) { const reason = row?.sourceAudit?.reason || "single source"; … } else if (row?.isStructurallySingleSource) { chips.push({ label: "solo", … })`. Live contract stamps `isStructurallySingleSource` on 20 rows and `sourceAudit` on all 1,092. Executing buildRows on it: `row.isStructurallySingleSource defined? 0`, `row.sourceAudit defined? 0`, `rendered solo chips: 0`, `1-src chips: 75` — all 75 falling back to the literal string 'single source'. `isStructurallySingleSource` is even carried in `_DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS` (data_contract.py:8969), so the backend ships it on the override path too and the materializer still discards it.
findings.userImpact: The blue 'solo' chip — the distinction between 'only one board could ever cover this player' and 'other boards should have matched him and didn't' — never renders. 20 players are shown the amber matching-failure chip's semantics or nothing, and the 75 genuine failures show a tooltip that names no reason, which is the entire content of `sourceAudit.reason`.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: The Sources column renders '16/15' on 30 rows because the eligible-source denominator ignores extraScopes
findings.rootCause: The denominator is recomputed on the client from `s.scope` alone. `idpTradeCalc` is registered with `scope: 'overall_idp'` and `extraScopes: ['overall_offense']` and does cover offense, so it contributes to the backend's `sourceCount` but is excluded from the client's eligible set.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1119-1127 — `if (s.scope === "overall_offense") return ["QB","RB","WR","TE","PICK"].includes(pos); if (s.scope === "overall_idp") return ["DL","LB","DB"].includes(pos); return false;`. Registry: dynasty-data.js:230-234 — `key: "idpTradeCalc", scope: "overall_idp", extraScopes: ["overall_offense"]`. Live board: 30 rows render numerator > denominator, all '16/15', all with `idpTradeCalc` present in `sourceRanks` (Jeremiyah Love RB, Carnell Tate WR, Fernando Mendoza QB, Jordyn Tyson WR, Makai Lemon WR, Kenyon Sadiq TE, Jadarian Price RB, Eli Stowers TE, …).
findings.userImpact: A column whose stated purpose is 'matched / structurally eligible' displays a ratio above 1. Separately, the denominator is inflated for everyone: rookie-only boards (`dlfRookieSf` depth 50, `flockFantasySfRookies`) count as eligible for every veteran, and rookie-EXCLUDING boards (`dlfIdp`, `fantasyProsIdp`, both `excludesRookies: true`) count as eligible for every rookie, so coverage looks systematically worse than it is.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: Sorting the Consensus column descending puts 272 unrankable rows at the top of the board
findings.rootCause: The page's own comparator maps missing values to `Infinity` and multiplies by the direction sign, so nulls sort to whichever end the direction points. It bypasses `DataTable.sortRows`, which sinks nulls in both directions.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:592-594 — `va = a.blendedSourceRank ?? Infinity; vb = b.blendedSourceRank ?? Infinity; return (va - vb) * dir;` with `dir = sortAsc ? 1 : -1`. Contrast DataTable.jsx:143-147 — `// nulls last in BOTH directions … if (aNull || bNull) return compareValues(a, b) || x.i - y.i;` — which the page disables via `presorted` (page.jsx:1886). Executed on the live board: 272 rows have `blendedSourceRank == null`; descending places them at indices 0-271, led by '2026 Pick 5.01'. Two null rows produce `(Infinity - Infinity) * -1 = NaN`, an invalid comparator return.
findings.userImpact: One click on the 'Consensus' header buries the entire real board under 272 draft picks and unpriced players. The `rank` and `gap` sorts handle nulls correctly; this one and, in the opposite way, `value` do not.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: Hampel-rejected sources render identically to contributing ones, and their tooltip calls the discarded rank the 'effective rank'
findings.rootCause: `formatSourceCell` reads `row.sourceRanks` (the pre-Hampel map) and `sourceRankMeta[key].valueContribution`, and never consults `row.droppedSources`, which buildRows materializes and nothing renders.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/board-utils.js:46 — `const effectiveRank = row?.sourceRanks?.[src.key];` and :98-103 — ``title: `${src.displayName}: value ${primary}${effectiveRank != null ? `, effective rank #${effectiveRank}` : ""}…` ``. `droppedSources` is on the row (dynasty-data.js:1059-1061) and used only by edge-helpers.js:141-143 to count. Live: Brock Bowers (#2) has `droppedSources: ['fantasyProsSf','draftSharks']`; both cells render as normal — `fantasyProsSf` → '8,310 (#28)', `draftSharks` → '7,940 (#16)' — with tooltips reading 'effective rank #28' / 'effective rank #16'. 215 rows have at least one dropped source.
findings.userImpact: A user reading the source columns to understand why the blend landed where it did cannot see which votes were rejected. The word 'effective' in the tooltip asserts the opposite of what happened: these ranks were specifically excluded from the effective set the confidence, disagreement and gap signals were computed on.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: The 'Market (retail-lean)' preset does the opposite of what its description says for IDPTC — and the test pins the wrong side
findings.rootCause: `presetToWeights` branches on the registry `isRetail` flag; only `ktcSfTep` carries it. The preset descriptions were written assuming IDPTC is retail (which display-helpers.js:292 also assumes, calling it 'the analogous retail anchor').
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/weight-presets.js:68-77 — `const isRetail = !!source.isRetail; if (key === "market") { weight = isRetail ? 2.0 : 0.5; }`; description at :49-51 — `"Retail (KTC, IDPTC) × 2.0, experts × 0.5."`. Registry: `idpTradeCalc` has `isRetail: false` (dynasty-data.js:239). Executed: market preset puts only `ktcSfTep` at 2.0; `idpTradeCalc` gets 0.5. Expert preset gives `idpTradeCalc` 1.5 while the description says retail gets 0.5. `frontend/__tests__/weight-presets.test.js:22-35` asserts the isRetail-driven behavior, so the discrepancy is cemented rather than caught.
findings.userImpact: A user in an IDP league who picks 'Market (retail-lean)' expecting the board to read like what their leaguemates negotiate against gets the IDP retail anchor DOWN-weighted to 0.5 and every IDP expert board weighted equally. The whole IDP half of the board moves the wrong way, and the label says it moved the right way.

findings.area: Frontend rankings surface — `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js` (buildRows / mergeRankingsDelta / applyValuationOverlay / RANKING_SOURCES), `rankings-helpers.js`, `p
findings.title: The 'Seller cash-out' ROS tag compares a 0-9999 value against a 0-86 value and can never fire
findings.rootCause: Scale mismatch between `dynastyValue` (the 1-9999 board) and `rosValue` (the ROS aggregate's 0-100-ish score).
findings.evidence: frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:108 — `if (veteran && isStrong && dynastyValue != null && dynastyValue < rosValue * 0.7) tags.push("Seller cash-out");` with `isStrong = rosValue >= 60` (:100) and `dynastyValue = row.values?.full ?? row.rankDerivedValue` (:142). Live `data/ros/aggregate/latest.json`: rosValue range 0.03-86.42 over 1,085 players. The condition therefore requires `dynastyValue < 60.5` while simultaneously requiring `rosValue >= 60`. Executed against the live board joined to the ROS aggregate: 2 matched veterans with rosValue ≥ 60, 0 fires. Also `row.values?.full ?? row.rankDerivedValue` never reaches the right operand — `values.full` is always a number after buildRows.
findings.userImpact: One of nine advertised contender-layer labels is dead. Low severity because the tag is explicitly informational and the section is gated behind `settings.showRosTags`, but it is a decision label the product claims to produce and does not.

findings.title: Rank range filters exclude the 216 rows whose rank the # column shows
findings.rootCause: `rowMatches` reads `canonicalConsensusRank` while the table's # column and its rank sort read `resolvedRank` (backend rank, else the client ordinal).
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/player-filters.js:166-168 — `const rank = num(row.canonicalConsensusRank); if (c.rankMin != null && (rank === null || rank < c.rankMin)) return false;`. Compare frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:166-168 — `resolvedRank` returns `canonicalConsensusRank ?? computedConsensusRank`, which page.jsx:581-583 uses for the rank sort and :888 renders as `row.rank`.
findings.userImpact: A user filtering 'rank 1-2000' to include the whole board silently loses the 216 client-ranked rows, even though they visibly carry ranks 857-1072 in the column he is filtering on. The fail-closed rule at player-filters.js:15-19 is the right policy; the inconsistency is that the column and the filter disagree about what a rank is.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md and two in-file comments assert the legacy `players` dict is the default materializer path; desktop has requested `view=array` (no legacy dict) since device-profile landed
findings.rootCause: `preferredDataView()` returns 'array' for desktop and 'compact' for mobile; neither is the `view=app` runtime payload the 'legacy is default' claim was written for.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/device-profile.js:103-108 — `export function preferredDataView() { if (isMobileProfile() || isSlowNetwork()) return "compact"; return "array"; }`; consumed at dynasty-data.js:1461-1468. server.py:1969-1975 builds the array payload by `array_payload.pop("players", None)`. Contradicting claims: dynasty-data.js:1857-1860 — 'The legacy path is the DEFAULT one (server.py pops playersArray off the runtime payload), so an applier that writes only the first set … on the path that actually ships'; and CLAUDE.md's valuation-overlay section repeats it.
findings.userImpact: No live breakage — `applyValuationOverlay` defensively writes both key sets, and `mergeRankingsDelta`'s runtime-synthesis branch is unreachable in practice. The risk is to future maintainers: a change reasoned from 'legacy is the shipping path' would be reasoning about a path desktop users never take, and the two materializers have already drifted (previous finding).

findings.area: Trade calculator, trade verdict, and trade retro-grading (frontend/lib/trade-logic.js, trade-share.js, trade-retro-value.js, /trade, /trades, /arbitrage, /finde
findings.title: The trade verdict's direction is undefined: the meter calls the side with the BIGGER pile the winner, while every other part of the same page treats a side's pile as what that side GIVES AWAY
findings.rootCause: There is no single stated convention for what `sides[i].assets` means in a 2-team trade, and the codebase implements both. The verdict label picked one; the flow math, the stack lens, the simulator hand-off, the 3+-team meter and the side-card labels picked the other.
findings.evidence:
GIVE convention — frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:1392-1393 `const value = ...effectiveValue(asset...); result[i].given += value;` then `result[dest].received += value`; frontend/app/trade/trade-sections.jsx:808 `
Giving
` over `side.assets`; frontend/components/graphs/MultiTradeFlow.jsx:80 "Each side appears once on the left (giver)"; frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1313-1319 "Whichever side has more matches is 'my side' (I'm giving)" → those names are sent as `playersOut`; page.jsx:1587 applySuggestion puts the backend's `give` list on side 0. WIN-IS-BIGGER convention — frontend/components/trade/TradeMeter.jsx:37,58-60 `const gap = pwA - pwB; ... winnerText = gap > 0 ? \`${labelA} wins by ${pctGap}%\``; TradeFairnessExplanation.jsx:135 `const winnerLabel = overallGap > 0 ? labelA : labelB;`; page.jsx:2084-2085 `
{verdictFromGap(pwGap)}` with colorFromGap green for gap>0. The arithmetic settles which reading the math uses: trade-logic.js:843 `adjusted: rawA + adjA - stackA` subtracts a side's own stack GAIN, while :1421 `net = received - given + stack[i]` adds it — the two are consistent only if `adjusted` is a give-total. In 2-team mode nothing on screen says which it is: the 'Giving'/'Receiving' labels render only when `sides.length > 2` (trade-sections.jsx:807, 836).
findings.userImpact: Executed on the real module: sides A=[9000] vs B=[6000] produce `gap = +3000` → the sticky tray and meter show green on Side A and 'Side A wins by 33%', while `computeSideFlows` on the identical input returns `net_A = -3000` and the 3-side meter would render Side A as 'Losing value' in red. A user reading the headline verdict can be told the exact opposite of what the same page's flow numbers say. This is the single number the whole page exists to produce.

findings.area: Trade calculator, trade verdict, and trade retro-grading (frontend/lib/trade-logic.js, trade-share.js, trade-retro-value.js, /trade, /trades, /arbitrage, /finde
findings.title: Two share-link producers feed the same trade builder with opposite side semantics, so a trade opened from history simulates backwards
findings.rootCause: buildShareUrl/encodeTrade carries no field saying whether a side's player list is what the team gave or got, and the two producers made opposite choices.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:238-242 builds each share side from `side.got` — the comment at :233-234 says "Each calculator side mirrors what that team RECEIVED". frontend/app/arbitrage/page.jsx:84-88 builds `sides: [{name: myTeam, players: give}, {name: opponent, players: receive}]` — side 0 is what I GIVE. Both land in the same consumer via parseShareParam (frontend/lib/trade-share.js:148-161). frontend/lib/trade-share.js:83-92 encodes only `{n, p}` per side — no direction field.
findings.userImpact: Open a historical trade from /trades in the calculator and press the roster simulator: page.jsx:1314-1338 decides 'my side' by which side holds my roster's players and sends those as `playersOut`. Under the /trades encoding those are the players I RECEIVED, so /api/trade/simulate is asked to remove players I own and add players I already have — the 'Impact on my team' before/after deltas, starter deltas and accept/decline verdict are inverted. The same link from /arbitrage simulates correctly.

findings.area: Trade calculator, trade verdict, and trade retro-grading (frontend/lib/trade-logic.js, trade-share.js, trade-retro-value.js, /trade, /trades, /arbitrage, /finde
findings.title: Fairness bands are absolute points on a board whose trades span two orders of magnitude, so a 27% imbalance is labelled FAIR
findings.rootCause: verdictFromGap/meterVerdict switch on |gap| in raw board points with no normalisation by trade size, while the winner text and the narration beside them switch on percent.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:27-29 `const VERDICT_NEAR_EVEN = 350; const VERDICT_LEAN = 900; const VERDICT_STRONG_LEAN = 1800;` and :1432-1436 `if (absGap < 350) return { label: "FAIR" ... }`. Executed against the real module: `[900]` vs `[450,450]` → raw 900 vs 900, VA 334 to the single-piece side, gap 334 → verdictFromGap 'Near even', meterVerdict FAIR — with percentageGap = 27. In the other direction, totals of 20,000 vs 19,500 (1.75%) give gap 500 → 'SLIGHT EDGE'.
findings.userImpact: Depth-piece and pick-for-pick trades — the majority of real dynasty trades by count — are graded FAIR at imbalances a user would immediately reject, and elite-tier packages are flagged as unfair at differences inside any source's noise. Two users comparing a small trade and a big trade get labels that do not mean the same thing.

findings.area: Trade calculator, trade verdict, and trade retro-grading (frontend/lib/trade-logic.js, trade-share.js, trade-retro-value.js, /trade, /trades, /arbitrage, /finde
findings.title: One card shows three different fairness answers for the same trade
findings.rootCause: The verdict badge uses an absolute gap, the winner text uses a 3% floor, and the narration below uses a 3% fair/lean switch — all rendered together with no shared criterion.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/trade/TradeMeter.jsx:40 `const verdict = meterVerdict(absGap);` vs :57 `if (pctGap >= 3) { winnerText = ... }` vs frontend/components/trade/TradeFairnessExplanation.jsx:121-130 `if (pctGap < 3) { ... return "Sources broadly agree this trade is fair..." }`. Both are rendered from the same sideTotals at frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1950-1956 and :1979.
findings.userImpact: Totals 20,000 vs 19,500 render simultaneously as the badge 'SLIGHT EDGE', the text 'Even', and the sentence 'Sources broadly agree this trade is fair.' The user cannot tell which one is the verdict.

findings.area: Trade calculator, trade verdict, and trade retro-grading (frontend/lib/trade-logic.js, trade-share.js, trade-retro-value.js, /trade, /trades, /arbitrage, /finde
findings.title: Historical trade grades are pure hindsight — today's board applied to trades up to a year old — and the as-of correction is a secondary badge with three silent fallbacks
findings.rootCause: analyzeRawTrade values every asset at the current board; gradeRetro was layered on top as a badge instead of replacing the grade, and its own at-trade leg is incomplete.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:132 `value: row.values?.full || 0` (picks) and :146 `const baseVal = row.values?.full || 0` (players) — the live contract's current value. The headline is built from that: :394-395 `const pctGap = (netAdjusted / scale) * 100; const grade = gradeTradeHistorySide(...)`, rendered at frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:225-232 as '<team> won by X%' with letter grades from league-analysis.js:87-98. The as-of path exists but: frontend/lib/trade-retro-value.js:77-85 `if (it.isPick) { // Picks: lean on the current value ... const v = Number(it.val) || 0; ... source: "current" }`; :52-55 falls back to the EARLIEST sample when the trade predates coverage yet still stamps `source: "rankHistory"` (:91); and frontend/lib/value-history.js:32 `const key = String(Math.max(1, Math.min(180, Math.floor(days))));` clamps the request to 180 days while frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:386 defaults the trade window to 365 days and :394 asks for `{ days: 365 }`.
findings.userImpact: Every 'A+ / Fleeced / won by 38%' verdict on /trades is retrodiction: a player who broke out after the trade makes the acquirer look prescient and the sender look robbed, when at the time the deal may have been even. Trades older than 180 days additionally get an 'at trade' value taken from the oldest snapshot in the window — post-dating the trade — with no UI marker, so the 'Aged well/poorly' badge is itself partly hindsight. Any trade containing a pick is hindsight-priced even in the as-of leg.

findings.area: Trade calculator, trade verdict, and trade retro-grading (frontend/lib/trade-logic.js, trade-share.js, trade-retro-value.js, /trade, /trades, /arbitrage, /finde
findings.title: The Monte Carlo panel silently ignores the page's value mode and every per-player value override — the exact divergence its own docstring says it exists to prevent
findings.rootCause: TradeMeter accepts `valueMode` and `settings` props but its signature drops them, and it is handed the raw `sides` state rather than the override-applied copy the totals use.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/trade/TradeMeter.jsx:24 `export default function TradeMeter({ sides, sideTotals, flows }) {` — `valueMode`/`settings` are passed at frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1954-1955 and never destructured; :107 `<MonteCarloButton sides={sides} />` with no valueMode, so frontend/components/ui/MonteCarloButton.jsx:118 defaults `valueMode = "full"`. Separately, page.jsx:1951 passes `sides={sides}` while the totals at :638-661 are computed from `sidesWithOverrides` (:534-544, which stamps `customValue`), and effectiveValue honours `customValue` first (trade-logic.js:183). MonteCarloButton.jsx:1-21 states the requirement it is violating: "the per-player values sent to the simulator must match what the trade builder displays".
findings.userImpact: Switch the value mode to 'Raw' and the meter, the totals and the MC panel disagree — MC keeps simulating the 'full' board. Type a custom value for a player (a first-class feature with its own UI) and the meter uses it while MC does not, reproducing the meter-vs-MC mismatch (-4281 vs -632) the component was written to fix.

findings.title: RosTradeFitPanel compares a 0-9999 dynasty value against a 0-100 ROS value, making the 'Seller cash-out' tag effectively unreachable
findings.rootCause: The client re-implementation copied the Python predicate but feeds it a value on a different scale.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:75 `if (veteran && isStrong && dynastyValue != null && dynastyValue < rosValue * 0.7) tags.push("Seller cash-out");` with the input supplied at :127 `dynastyValue: row?.values?.full ?? row?.rankDerivedValue ?? null` — the board scale. The Python original expects the same 0-100 scale: src/ros/tags.py:73 uses the identical predicate and its test passes `dynasty_value=40` against `ros_value=70` (tests/ros/test_direction_and_tags.py:146-150, comment `# 40 < 70 * 0.7`). rosValue*0.7 can never exceed 70, so any player with a real board value fails the test.
findings.userImpact: The one tag whose entire purpose is 'sell this player now' never fires for a rostered player. Users see the panel and reasonably conclude no asset in the trade is a sell candidate.

findings.title: Three independent ports of the KTC Value Adjustment with no test tying two of them together
findings.rootCause: src/trade/market_value_adjustment.py was added for the finder without noticing src/trade/ktc_va.py already existed.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:407 `export function ktcAdjustPackage`, src/trade/ktc_va.py:146 `def ktc_adjust_package` ("Verbatim translation of the JS port"), src/trade/market_value_adjustment.py:1-7 `def ktc_adjust_package` ("a line-for-line Python port of the authoritative frontend implementation"). Consumers are split: ktc_va → suggestions.py:_va_gap, angle.py, monte_carlo.py:152; market_value_adjustment → finder_value_adjustment.py:16. Each has its own fixture test (tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py, tests/trade/test_finder_value_adjustment.py) and neither compares against the other. CLAUDE.md's Trade Engines section names neither module.
findings.userImpact: None today — I executed all 139 fixture trades through all three: JS vs ktc_va.py = 0 differences, ktc_va.py vs market_value_adjustment.py = 0 differences. The risk is a one-sided edit: the arbitrage engine and the trade suggestions would then grade the same package differently with both test suites green.

findings.area: Trade calculator, trade verdict, and trade retro-grading (frontend/lib/trade-logic.js, trade-share.js, trade-retro-value.js, /trade, /trades, /arbitrage, /finde
findings.title: Balancing suggestions are sized against a VA-inclusive gap but selected by raw value, so the suggested piece does not close the gap
findings.rootCause: findBalancers treats the gap as a linear quantity, but adding a piece changes the piece counts that drive the Value Adjustment.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:756 `const list = findBalancers(pwGap, pool, valueMode);` where `pwGap` comes from the adjusted totals (:708-712). frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:1256-1260 selects purely on `Number(r.values?.[valueMode] || 0)` sorted by `Math.abs(a.value - target)`. Executed illustration of the sensitivity: `[9000]` vs `[4500,4500]` has raw totals equal and gap 4681 (all VA); `[9000]` vs `[3000,3000,3000]` gap 6014 — adding a third piece to the behind side *widened* the gap by 1333 despite the raw totals staying equal.
findings.userImpact: On any 1-for-many shape, following the app's own balancing advice can move the verdict further from even, and the user has no way to see why.

findings.area: Trade calculator, trade verdict, and trade retro-grading (frontend/lib/trade-logic.js, trade-share.js, trade-retro-value.js, /trade, /trades, /arbitrage, /finde
findings.title: The main verdict feeds KTC's board-specific constants with our blended values, while the per-source table on the same page feeds them KTC's real values
findings.rootCause: ktcAdjustPackage hardcodes KTC's top-of-board reference and 'max player' ceiling; only one of its two call sites supplies inputs from that board.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:249-258 `const KTC_MAX_PLAYER_VAL = 10000; ... const KTC_T_REFERENCE = 10041;` with the justification "we can't observe the live top value at compute time". The verdict path feeds our board: trade-logic.js:212-216 `sortedSideValues` → `effectiveValue(r, valueMode)` → `row.values[valueMode]` (rankDerivedValue). The breakdown path deliberately does not: frontend/components/trade/TradeSourceBreakdown.jsx:97-104 "the V13 Value Adjustment formula and its empirical suppression thresholds … were calibrated against KTC's raw 0-9999 piece values. Feeding the formula the canonical Hill-blended valueContribution instead would mis-fire VA" and :126-129 reads `row.rawSourceValues.ktcSfTep`.
findings.userImpact: The headline verdict's consolidation premium — up to 6,671 points on the shapes I executed, more than half the raw side total — is computed on inputs the formula was never validated against, and the file's own comment states why that mis-fires. Nothing validates the VA on our board; the 139-case fixture only validates it on KTC's.

findings.rootCause: Comments were not updated when the features they describe were removed or moved to the backend.
findings.evidence: (1) frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:193-201 — displayValue's docstring claims it resolves the value "including the Apply Scoring Fit adjustment when the global toggle is on" and warns that effectiveValue "also applies the pick-year discount"; the implementation at :203-209 does neither, effectiveValue at :181-185 applies no discount (the file's own note at :152-162 says the discount is backend-only), and grep for `scoringFit|applyScoring` across frontend/lib, components and app returns nothing. (2) frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:149-152 carries the same phantom "When the user has Apply Scoring Fit on, IDP values shift by delta × weight" above a line that returns `baseVal` unchanged. (3) frontend/components/trade/TradeSourceBreakdown.jsx:7-8, 21 and :97 describe "the V13 Value Adjustment math" and its "empirical suppression thresholds (V13_SUPPRESS_RAW_DIFF…)" while the code calls valueAdjustmentFromSideArrays → ktcAdjustPackage, the KTC-native port that superseded V13 (trade-logic.js:552-559). (4) docs/status/blueprint-gap-analysis.md:88 records "No balancing suggestions" — findBalancers is implemented (trade-logic.js:1244) and rendered (app/trade/page.jsx:728-805). (5) docs/status/master-implementation-audit.md:75 describes app/trade/page.jsx as "314 lines … 4 value modes"; it is 2,105 lines with 2 (VALUE_MODES, trade-logic.js:16-19).
findings.userImpact: No runtime effect. It cost this audit real time and it is the mechanism by which the next reader concludes a scoring-fit adjustment is applied to trade values when none is.

findings.title: The /trades header claims trades are 'graded at alpha=1.65' but alpha no longer touches the grade
findings.rootCause: The alpha-weighted net was demoted to a winner/loser sort key when the KTC VA path landed; the header text was left behind.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:488 renders `${analysis.analyzed.length} trades in the last ${windowDays} days, graded at alpha=${alpha}.` The grade comes from frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:394-395 `const pctGap = (netAdjusted / scale) * 100; const grade = gradeTradeHistorySide(...)` where netAdjusted = netLinear + vaNet (:386-387). netWeighted (the alpha term, :317 `weighted += Math.pow(Math.max(safeVal, 1), alpha)`) is used only at :418-421 to order winner/loser, and league-analysis.js:389-390 explicitly excludes it from the denominator because it "would crush all pcts toward zero".
findings.userImpact: Users tuning `settings.alpha` expect the grades to move; they do not, except for which side is labelled winner in a 3+-team deal.

findings.title: scoreTeamTiers' pick term has the wrong net sign: draft picks INCREASE a team's contender score by +0.1 per unit, while the UI tells the user they are penalised at -10%
findings.rootCause: `totalValue` accumulates pick value (frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:1016), then `depthValue = totalValue - starterValue` (:1027) carries that pick value into the +0.2 depth term, and the explicit -0.1 penalty is applied on top. Net coefficient on pick value is 0.2 - 0.1 = +0.1.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:1026-1028 — `const starterValue = starters.reduce((s, p) => s + p.meta, 0); const depthValue = totalValue - starterValue; const score = starterValue * 0.7 + depthValue * 0.2 + (pickValue > 0 ? -pickValue * 0.1 : 0);`  with :1016-1017 `totalValue += val; pickValue += val;`. The docstring at :974 says 'Pick surplus penalized at -10% (rebuild signal)'. The user-facing InfoTip at frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:522-525 says 'Teams are scored on starter quality (70%), roster depth (20%), and a pick-surplus penalty (-10%).'
findings.userImpact: The team hoarding the most draft capital — by definition the most rebuild-shaped roster in the league — is ranked as the strongest contender. Replayed on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json with an approximate pick-label resolver and a top-21-by-value starter proxy: the owner holding 72 picks worth ~175k ranks #1 as shipped and #6 with the sign corrected, and 7 of 12 teams change position. The tier boundaries are ceil(n/3), so teams cross the Contender/Mid-Tier/Rebuilder line on this error. A manager reading this card would conclude they are contending when the roster says rebuild.

findings.area: Team-level decision/judgement systems: `/league` (public tabs + subroutes), `/rosters`, `/phases`, `/league-comparison`, `frontend/components/terminal/*`, and t
findings.title: The public trade grader applies the private grader's letter thresholds to a completely different quantity, so the same trade is 'Fair' on /trades and 'Robbery' on /league
findings.rootCause: `src/public_league/activity.py` grades on the alpha-exponentiated side totals — the exact quantity the private path's comment forbids — while reusing the private path's 3/8/15/25/40 letter cuts, which were calibrated for a linear-value percentage gap.
findings.evidence: src/public_league/activity.py:118 `total += pow(max(val, 1.0), _GRADE_ALPHA)` with `_GRADE_ALPHA = 1.65` (:49) and :131 `pct = ((max_w - min_w) / max_w) * 100.0`. Against frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:388-394: 'Don't include the alpha-powered weighted sums — those dominate by an order of magnitude and would crush all pcts toward zero.' followed by `const scale = Math.max(gotEffective, gaveEffective, 1); const pctGap = (netAdjusted / scale) * 100;`. The header comment at activity.py:40-44 claims 'a trade graded on the private /trades page lands in the same bucket on the public /league activity timeline.'
findings.userImpact: Reproduced numerically. A 1×8000-for-2×4000 swap (perfectly even on linear value) yields publicPct = 36.27 → 'A+ Big win' for one side and 'D Robbery' for the other, versus privatePct = 0.00 → 'A Fair trade' for both. A 1×6000-for-3×2000 swap yields publicPct = 51.04, past the 'F Fleeced' line, versus private 0.00. Every consolidation trade — the most common shape in dynasty — is publicly labelled a robbery. These letters and words appear on a PUBLIC page next to a named league-mate.

findings.title: The 'Rebuild' phase is unreachable on live data, which silently kills the /phases page's headline trade-partner feature
findings.rootCause: Two compounding choices: (1) `medianAge < leagueMedians.age` uses a strict `<` against a median of integer-valued team medians, so every team tied at the median is classified 'older'; (2) the team's median age is computed over its TOP 25 PLAYERS BY VALUE, which excludes exactly the cheap young prospects that constitute a rebuild.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/team-phase.js:85-86 `const isYounger = medianAge != null && leagueMedians.age != null && medianAge < leagueMedians.age;` and :65-67 `const top = [...lookup].sort((a, b) => b.value - a.value).slice(0, TOP_N_FOR_VALUE); ... const ages = top.map((p) => p.age).filter(...)` with `TOP_N_FOR_VALUE = 25` (:29). Partnerships require rebuilders: :118 `const rebuilders = enriched.filter((t) => t.phase.key === 'rebuild');`
findings.userImpact: Replayed on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json (ages exact, value proxied by `_finalAdjusted`): league median team-age = 25.0 and FIVE of twelve teams have a top-25 median age of exactly 25.0 — all five are forced to the 'older' side. Resulting distribution: Win-now 2, Contender 4, Mixed 6, Rebuild 0. With zero rebuilders, `partnerships` is empty, so the 'Natural trade partners for you' block (TeamPhasePanel.jsx:161-188) renders nothing at all — the panel's stated reason for existing (team-phase.js:22-24) produces no output, and no message explains why. Rosters carry 44-58 players; the age median ignores 33-38 of them.

findings.area: Team-level decision/judgement systems: `/league` (public tabs + subroutes), `/rosters`, `/phases`, `/league-comparison`, `frontend/components/terminal/*`, and t
findings.title: Luck score and Power rankings count in-progress weeks as finished games, so the verdict and the rank visibly change during Sunday afternoon and re-settle Monday night
findings.rootCause: `metrics.is_scored` returns True for any roster with points > 0, so a team that has played Thursday is treated as having a final score while its opponent still sits at 0. `luck._season_weekly_scores` and `luck._actual_week_results` both accept those partials. The playoff-odds module guards exactly this case; luck.py and power.py do not.
findings.evidence: src/public_league/metrics.py:57-59 `def is_scored(entry): return matchup_points(entry) > 0`. src/public_league/luck.py:91-92 `if not metrics.is_scored(entry): continue` (all-play field shrinks to whoever has played) and :117 `if not metrics.is_scored(a) and not metrics.is_scored(b): continue` followed by :126-130, which awards a full 1.0 actual win to the side with points against a side at 0. Contrast src/public_league/playoff_odds.py:135-139: 'Both sides have points > 0 — the standard current-week gate. During a live week we require both sides to have posted scores before counting, otherwise a Thursday-only finish gets credited as a phantom win over an opponent still sitting at 0.' power.py:87 and :98 call the unguarded luck helpers directly.
findings.userImpact: The public snapshot TTL is 300 seconds (server.py:8379), so during a live NFL week these numbers recompute roughly every 5 minutes off partial scores. A phantom win moves luckDelta by up to 1.0, which is wider than the entire ±0.3 'Deserved' band — a manager can be 'Blessed' on Sunday evening and 'Unlucky' on Monday night with no game having changed hands. Power rank deltas move the same way. Nothing on either tab indicates the week is in progress.

findings.title: ROS Buyer/Seller direction: two of its four documented inputs have no effect, and one of its seven labels is unreachable in production
findings.rootCause: `team_ros_strength_percentile` is read into a local and used only to format a display string. `roster_age_profile` is always {} because `build_team_directions` is only ever called without a `teams` argument, so the age-gated branch can never fire.
findings.evidence: src/ros/direction.py:78 `strength_pct = team_ros_strength_percentile or 0.0` — its only other appearance is :120 inside the summary f-string; no branch at :80-115 reads it, yet the docstring at :73-75 claims 'a team's exact band can shift on age + roster strength'. src/ros/trade_deadline.py:112-116 — `def build_section(snapshot): _ = snapshot  # roster ages come from team_strength snapshot directly` then `return {'teams': build_team_directions()}` with no `teams=`. That makes `team_obj` None at trade_deadline.py:85, `roster_age = {}`, and `age_heavy = bool({}.get('vetCount', 0) >= 4)` = False at direction.py:77, so 'Strong Seller / Rebuilder' (:98-103) never fires. The comment 'roster ages come from team_strength snapshot directly' is false — `build_roster_age_profile` is never called in production.
findings.userImpact: Enumerated the full decision surface: the label is a pure function of playoff odds and championship odds, and the `else` fallback swallows large regions. A team at 90% playoff odds with 3% title odds is labelled 'Hold / Evaluate' with the recommendation 'Avoid extreme buy/sell' — the opposite of correct at a trade deadline. The documented 'Hold: 0.35 <= playoff < 0.55' band is realised as 0.40-0.45 only. The frontend carries a colour entry for 'Strong Seller / Rebuilder' (frontend/app/league/sections/ros-trade-deadline.jsx:46) that no user will ever see.

findings.title: Luck verdicts use absolute win thresholds across scopes and disagree with their own colour coding
findings.rootCause: `luckLabel` and `luckColor` are two independent frontend band sets over the same `luckDelta`, and neither normalises by games played even though the backend ships `luckPerGame`.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/league/sections/luck.jsx:34-41 `if (delta > 0.5) return '#2ecc71'; if (delta > 0.1) return '#7bdfb3'; if (delta < -0.5) return '#ff6b6b'; if (delta < -0.1) return '#ffab6b';` versus :43-50 `if (delta > 1.0) return 'Blessed'; if (delta > 0.3) return 'Lucky'; if (delta > -0.3) return 'Deserved'; if (delta > -1.0) return 'Unlucky'; return 'Cursed';`. Both are applied to the same rows whether the scope selector is 'career' or a single season (:300-304, :393). The backend emits `luckPerGame` at src/public_league/luck.py:290 and no frontend file reads it.
findings.userImpact: Enumerated the disagreement: luckDelta = +0.2 renders pale green (a 'lucky' colour) with the word 'Deserved'; -0.2 renders orange (an 'unlucky' colour) with the word 'Deserved'; +0.6 renders the brightest green with only 'Lucky'. Separately, a ~45-game career row and a 14-game season row share the same +1.0 'Blessed' cut, so 'Blessed' means roughly 2.2% of games over a career and 7.1% over a season — the career column systematically over-reports luck.

findings.area: Team-level decision/judgement systems: `/league` (public tabs + subroutes), `/rosters`, `/phases`, `/league-comparison`, `frontend/components/terminal/*`, and t
findings.title: Power rankings v1 blends three different time scales and presents a career record as a weekly one; three descriptions of the same formula disagree
findings.rootCause: `career_state` is declared outside the season loop and is never reset, so the 50%-weighted PPG term is a career average across up to `PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS` (default 3) seasons, while the all-play term is a single week and `recent_buffer` resets per season.
findings.evidence: src/public_league/power.py:82-84 `career_state: dict[...] = defaultdict(lambda: {'points': 0.0, 'games': 0, ...})` declared before `for season in seasons_sorted:` at :86, with the comment at :81 'Cross-season continuous accumulators (career PPG-to-date)'. Contrast the module docstring at :6: 'Points per game (PPG) — overall scoring strength, season-to-date.' The all-play term at :126-131 admits the shortcut in a comment: 'simpler + still useful is current-week all-play share'. `record` at :143-147 is `f'{round(career wins)}-{games - wins}'` — a career record rendered under a column headed just 'Record' next to '2026 week 5' (frontend/app/league/sections/power.jsx:226, 369). PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS defaults to 3 (src/public_league/sleeper_client.py:44).
findings.userImpact: A 'weekly power ranking' whose dominant 50% term averages ~45 games barely moves week to week, so the tab's week-over-week rank delta column is mostly noise from the 25% single-week all-play term. The 'Record' column shows a multi-season record where a reader expects the current season's. The methodology string the UI prints verbatim (power.py:214-219) says 'PPG percentile' and 'all-play win share' without disclosing that one is career-long and the other is one week.
