findings.title: The /settings hint for ROS Power Rankings says the opposite of the shipped default, and the ROS Playoff Odds toggle does nothing at all
findings.rootCause: The default flipped to true in the settings registry but neither the hint text nor the LeagueClient comment was updated; and `useRosPlayoffOdds` was shipped as a live toggle with no consumer.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/useSettings.js:143 `useRosPowerRankings: true,` versus frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:761 hint 'Defaults off until you've validated v2 against a few weeks of standings.' and frontend/app/league/LeagueClient.jsx:99-100 comment 'useRosPowerRankings false until validated per-user'. For the second toggle: `useRosPlayoffOdds` appears exactly three times in the tree — useSettings.js:148 (default true), settings/page.jsx:765-766 (the switch), and nowhere else. Its own hint at :769 calls it a 'PR-future toggle'.
findings.userImpact: Users are shown the un-validated v2 power ranking by default while the settings page tells them v2 is off until they validate it — so nobody validates it and nobody knows they are looking at it. The playoff-odds toggle is a control that changes nothing; a user who flips it will believe the odds beneath it changed. As a side effect, the entire v1 Power path — including `public_league/power.py` and the `PlayoffOddsChart` component — is only reachable by turning a toggle off, which means the playoff-odds Monte Carlo is effectively dormant on the default experience.

findings.area: Team-level decision/judgement systems: `/league` (public tabs + subroutes), `/rosters`, `/phases`, `/league-comparison`, `frontend/components/terminal/*`, and t
findings.title: The buy-low insight's 'long steady' filter is never implemented, on either the frontend or the backend, while the metric name and the reason string both claim it
findings.rootCause: The two-legged rule was specified in a comment and a metric identifier but only the short-drop leg was written.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:466-467 `// Buy-low candidate: LEAGUE-wide — not on my roster, value >= 3000, // 7d trend <= -3 (dipped), 30d trend still >= 0 (long-term fine).` The filter chain at :469-492 checks roster membership, rank <= 150, value >= 3000 and `t7 <= -3` and stops — no 30-day figure is read anywhere in the block. Same on the backend: src/api/terminal.py:1109-1121 checks roster, rank, value and `rc > -3` only. Both emit `'metric': 'short_drop_long_steady'` (:502, terminal.py:1135).
findings.userImpact: A player in sustained structural decline — down on both the 7-day and 30-day windows — is presented as the roster's single named buy-low with the reason 'window open before the market corrects' (portfolio-insights.js:501). The filter that was supposed to exclude exactly that case does not exist. Note that both implementations use `rankChange` (last-scrape delta), not a 7-day trend, despite the comment calling it '7d'.

findings.area: Team-level decision/judgement systems: `/league` (public tabs + subroutes), `/rosters`, `/phases`, `/league-comparison`, `frontend/components/terminal/*`, and t
findings.title: 'Age curves' on /rosters are a board-composition artifact, not an aging model, and are captioned as a sell signal
findings.rootCause: The curve is the median value of every board row at each integer age, with no minimum bucket size and no correction for the fact that the population at each age is selected by survival.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/graphs/AgeCurveOverlay.jsx:53-61 — for each age it takes `median(bucket)` over whatever rows exist, and a bucket of size 1 yields that one player's value as the 'median'. Null points are dropped before pathing at :154-156, so a missing age is bridged with a straight line and no visual marker. The board handed in is the entire pool minus picks and kickers (frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:318-320). The InfoTip at :341-347 reads: 'Use it to spot aging risk: a cluster of RBs past the position's peak is a flag to sell; a cluster before it means you are set up for the window.'
findings.userImpact: The young end of every curve is dragged down by hundreds of near-zero-value 23-25 year old roster filler; the old end is computed over a handful of survivors who are, by construction, the ones still worth something. The curve can therefore slope upward with age and be read as 'this position peaks at 32'. A single 34-year-old on the board sets the entire age-34 'median'. The caption instructs the user to make sell decisions on it.

findings.title: activity-feed.js's private trade builder cannot work against the real contract, and its unit test validates a fixture shape the scraper never emits
findings.rootCause: `tradeToEvent` reads a Sleeper-transaction shape (`roster_ids` / `adds` / `drops`, and `positions` keyed by player id to an object with `.name`), but the contract stores trades as `{week, timestamp, sides:[{team, got, gave, ownerId, rosterId}]}` and `sleeper.positions` as cleanedName → position string.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/activity-feed.js:46-53 `const positions = rawData?.sleeper?.positions || {}; for (const pid of [...Object.keys(adds), ...Object.keys(drops)]) { const meta = positions[pid]; const name = meta?.name || (typeof meta === 'string' ? meta : null);` — against 'Dynasty Scraper.py':1301 `'positions': position_map,` where position_map is built name→position ('Dynasty Scraper.py':1237-1247, 1284-1285). Trades are emitted at 'Dynasty Scraper.py':1556-1567 as `{'leagueId', 'week', 'timestamp', 'sides': [{'team','rosterId','ownerId','got','gave'}]}` — no `adds`, `drops`, `roster_ids` or `transaction_id`. Also :38 matches `String(t?.rosterId)` against roster ids, but teams carry `roster_id` ('Dynasty Scraper.py':1256) and nothing in src/api/data_contract.py stamps `rosterId`. The test fixture at frontend/__tests__/activity-feed.test.js:11-27 invents `positions: {'100': {name: 'Caleb Williams'}}` and `trades: [{roster_ids, adds, drops}]`.
findings.userImpact: None today — the function has zero production callers, and /league/activity correctly uses `buildPublicActivityEvents` (the comment at activity-feed.js:150-158 explains why). The impact is that a green test suite asserts this code works. Anyone reviving it for a private activity feed would ship a feed with no team names and no player names and see passing tests.

findings.area: Team-level decision/judgement systems: `/league` (public tabs + subroutes), `/rosters`, `/phases`, `/league-comparison`, `frontend/components/terminal/*`, and t
findings.title: The League Edge Map's declared minimum-edge filter is dead code, and three surfaces gate the same 'market mispricing' concept on three different quantities
findings.rootCause: `MIN_EDGE_PCT` was declared next to `buildLeagueEdgeMap` and never referenced; the actual gate lives in a different module on a different quantity, and a third surface uses a fourth quantity.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:827 `const MIN_EDGE_PCT = 3;` — grep over the whole frontend returns exactly one hit, its own declaration. The real gate is frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:949 `const MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP = 3;` applied at :968 to `marketGapMagnitude` (a rank gap, not a percentage). The backend applies NO minimum at all — src/api/data_contract.py:2787-2793 returns a direction for any non-zero difference between the retail and consensus mean ranks. Meanwhile frontend/app/edge/page.jsx:142-144 gates the same buy/sell concept on `(r.sourceRankSpread ?? 0) >= PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD`.
findings.userImpact: A per-team 'sellEdge' is a raw sum of unbounded per-player percentages with no floor, so a team with many marginal 3-rank disagreements can out-rank a team with a genuinely mispriced star. The card's InfoTip (frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:575-580) presents this as 'Market price vs. our model, per team' with no indication of what qualifies. And a player who is a 'Sell' on /rosters may not appear on /edge at all, because the two pages gate on different numbers.

findings.area: Team-level decision/judgement systems: `/league` (public tabs + subroutes), `/rosters`, `/phases`, `/league-comparison`, `frontend/components/terminal/*`, and t
findings.title: Rivalry index double-counts close games through nested thresholds — the exact error the repo's own intel module devotes its docstring to condemning
findings.rootCause: `gamesDecidedByFive` and `gamesDecidedByTen` are incremented by two independent `if` statements rather than an elif chain, so every ≤5-point game also counts as a ≤10-point game and is scored twice.
findings.evidence: src/public_league/rivalries.py:118-121 `if margin_abs <= 5.0 + 1e-9: rec['gamesDecidedByFive'] += 1` followed by `if margin_abs <= 10.0 + 1e-9: rec['gamesDecidedByTen'] += 1` — not elif. The index at :171-178 then weights both: `3 * gamesDecidedByFive + 2 * gamesDecidedByTen`. Compare src/intel/signals.py:16-25, which rejects the identical pattern: 'The windows are nested, so a movement one hour old is inside all three terms... One event, six counted.'
findings.userImpact: Verified: one 3-point regular-season game this season scores 8 index points (3 + 2 + 1 meeting + 2 recency); one 40-point blowout in the same slot scores 3. A single nail-biter is worth 2.7 blowouts. The index drives the rivalry ordering, the 'Top rival' link on every franchise page, and the featured rivalry in the /league Open Graph description — and none of the weights appear anywhere in the UI.

findings.title: PlayoffOddsChart has no case for one of the backend's five schedule-certainty values, so the most-informed inference mode renders as 'Unknown schedule source'
findings.rootCause: The component's certainty map was written against a four-value enum documented in its own header; the backend emits six values including `inferred_from_posted`.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/graphs/PlayoffOddsChart.jsx:33-40 handles `posted`, `partial`, `inferred`, `final`, `preseason` and falls through to `{ text: 'Unknown schedule source' }`. The header comment at :12-13 states the enum as '{posted, partial, inferred, final}'. src/public_league/playoff_odds.py:625 sets `schedule_certainty = 'inferred_from_posted'` when the remaining pairings were successfully inferred from the observed posted-week cycle (:260-314) — the strongest inference the module makes, stronger than the round-robin `inferred` fallback.
findings.userImpact: The badge tells the user the schedule source is unknown precisely when the simulator has done its best work, and it renders in the neutral grey used for 'Season complete' rather than a caution colour. Reachable only on the non-default v1 Power view, which limits exposure.

findings.area: Team-level decision/judgement systems: `/league` (public tabs + subroutes), `/rosters`, `/phases`, `/league-comparison`, `frontend/components/terminal/*`, and t
findings.title: FranchiseTrajectory's x-axis encoding spends 78% of the chart width on empty offseasons
findings.rootCause: `encodeWeekKey` uses `season * 100 + week` as a linear x coordinate, so consecutive weeks are 1 apart while the gap from week 17 of one season to week 1 of the next is 84.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/graphs/FranchiseTrajectory.jsx:43-48 `return Number(season) * 100 + Number(week);` fed straight into `linearScale(tMin, tMax, 0, box.innerWidth)` at :77.
findings.userImpact: Computed for three 17-week seasons: total span 216 units, of which 48 (22.2%) is in-season and 168 (77.8%) is offseason gap. Each season's 17 weeks are compressed into roughly 7% of the chart width, with three-quarters of the plot showing straight lines through nothing. The season-boundary markers at :146-157 are drawn at the midpoint of those gaps, so they read as data.

findings.area: Team-level decision/judgement systems: `/league` (public tabs + subroutes), `/rosters`, `/phases`, `/league-comparison`, `frontend/components/terminal/*`, and t
findings.title: The flex card on /league-comparison has an unreachable colour band, and the position cards' colours diverge from the backend's own status bands
findings.rootCause: `absDiffTone` is called with a partial band object whose `mid` exceeds the default `hi`, and the frontend band set omits the backend's fourth threshold.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/league-comparison/sections/SummaryCards.jsx:177-183 `const b = bands || { lo: 0.5, mid: 1.5, hi: 3 }; ... if (d <= b.lo) green; if (d <= b.mid) cyan; if (d <= (b.hi || 3)) amber; return red;`. Called for flex at :148 as `absDiffTone(flex.relDiffPct, { lo: 1, mid: 5 })` — `b.hi` is undefined so `(b.hi || 3)` is 3, which is less than mid=5, making the amber branch unreachable. Separately the backend's `StatusBands` (src/league_comparison/metrics.py:274-278) carries a fourth threshold `over: 5.0` that the frontend has no equivalent for, so a 4pp difference renders red while `status_label` (:284-298) still returns 'High'/'Low' rather than 'Too high'/'Too low'.
findings.userImpact: Cosmetic but contradictory: the flex card jumps green → cyan → red with no warning state, and a position card can show a red delta next to a status word that is not the backend's most severe. On a page whose entire output is a judgement about whether scoring is distorted, the colour is doing as much work as the word.

findings.area: Team-level decision/judgement systems: `/league` (public tabs + subroutes), `/rosters`, `/phases`, `/league-comparison`, `frontend/components/terminal/*`, and t
findings.title: 'Insider Trading' is an accusation-shaped name on a product that makes no accusation and therefore has no false-positive rate to report — the risk is entirely in the label
findings.rootCause: Product naming. There is no collusion, tampering or wrongdoing detector anywhere in the tree.
findings.evidence: Grepped the full repository for collusion/insider detectors: the only hits are the product name itself (src/intel/__init__.py:6, src/intel/service.py:22, signals.py:1) and one unrelated comment in src/roster_intel/partner.py:585 mentioning 'collusion optics' as a reason a trade might be declined. The page renders exactly six observable counts per asset — buys, sells, net, volume, unique managers, unique leagues — plus a sample-strength tier (frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx:596-642). Its header explicitly disclaims a skill cohort at :480-484: 'These are the managers in this league, not a skill-filtered cohort.' The tier badge's tooltip at :68 says 'Sample strength: how much evidence sits behind this signal, not how strong the direction is.' The lead model publishes and RENDERS its own limitations (src/intel/leads.py:395-419 → frontend/components/InsiderLeads.jsx:380-387). The board is auditable to individual movements (:243-282, 'verify the count').
findings.userImpact: Bluntly: this is the best-evidenced system in the audit and it does not need a false-positive rate, because it asserts nothing falsifiable — every number is a count of a public transaction, with the underlying movements one click away. The exposure is reputational, not statistical: a page titled 'Insider Trading' that lists named league-mates and what they bought reads as an allegation to anyone who does not open it, and the page title is what gets screenshotted into a league chat. The confidence tier cuts (volume>=12/managers>=4/leagues>=3 for 'high', src/intel/signals.py:120-122) are unvalidated priors, but they gate a badge, not a claim.

findings.title: Six exports in league-analysis.js and one whole config surface in team_assignment.py are inert

findings.evidence: Zero non-definition references anywhere in frontend/ for: `computePositionRanks` (league-analysis.js:752-762), `heatmapColor` (:765-772), `heatmapTextColor` (:774-782), `buildRosterIdNameMap` (:234-236), `MIN_EDGE_PCT` (:827), `filterTradesToRollingWindow` (:76-83, called internally only). `ordinal` and `POS_GROUP_LABELS` are imported at frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:13, 20 and never used. In src/api/team_assignment.py:263 `thresholds = config['thresholds']` is bound inside the scorer and never read — the six rank thresholds at :92-100 (`eliteProductionTop10Rank`, `qbStarterPositionRank`, `skillStarterPositionRank`, `skillCommitteePositionRank`, `idpEliteSourcesPositionRank`, `idpStarterPositionRank`) and the weights `eliteProductionTop10` (:85) and `idpElite` (:89) have no effect on any score; the scorer branches on `depth_order == 1 / in (2,3)` instead (:280-310).
findings.userImpact: Low directly — only `assignmentMinPoints` reaches the UI (frontend/app/league/sections/team-assignment.jsx:244). The team_assignment code is at least honest about the proxy at :299-303 ('depth-chart order as a stand-in for elite at position'); the config file is not.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: The live FAAB bid is a share of a DRAFT PICK's value - every recommended bid is ~2.4x too low
findings.rootCause: server.py:4960-4984 computes top_pool_value as the max rankDerivedValue over every contract row not on a roster, with no assetClass filter. Draft picks are rows in playersArray and are never on a team's players list, so they dominate the pool. That value becomes the denominator of the only real input to the bid (share = candidate/top, faab_recommender.py:322-326 -> waiver.py:89-91).
findings.evidence: server.py:4969-4977 - `for row in arr: ... rname = _norm(row.get("displayName")...); if not rname or rname in rostered_norms: continue; v = float(row.get("rankDerivedValue") or 0); if v > top_pool_value: top_pool_value = v`. Measured on the 2026-08-04 contract rebuilt via build_api_data_contract: 427 unrostered rows, 144 of them assetClass=='pick'; top_pool_value = 7831.0 = '2026 Pick 1.01'; best genuine free agent = 1905.0 (Marlin Klein, TE). _compute_faab_bid(1770, 100, 7831) = (11, 8, 4) vs (1770, 100, 1770) = (30, 21, 10).
findings.userImpact: For Mitchell Evans (best add on the live board) the desk recommends standard $12 / conservative $8 / aggressive $17. With a free-agent-only denominator the same code returns $29 / $20 / $41. Every user of the bid desk is told to bid roughly 40% of what this model's own arithmetic intends, on every player, all season. The error also propagates into the contention model, whose rival estimates are multiples of the same baseline (simulated topRival $5, clearing $6).

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: The FAAB dollar figure is a value percentile mapped onto a dollar scale, not a bid derived from budget, replacement value, competition or expected contribution
findings.rootCause: The entire chain rests on aggressive_pct = 0.05 + 0.25 * (value / pool_max) (src/trade/waiver.py:91). Nothing in it references weeks remaining, roster need, starter vs bench slot, replacement level, points added, or budget already spent. Every later stage is a multiplier on that number.
findings.evidence: src/trade/waiver.py:86-95 - `share = candidate_value / top_v ...; aggressive_pct = 0.05 + 0.25 * share; aggressive = max(1, round(league_budget * aggressive_pct))`. Because share is normalized to the pool maximum, the top free agent always prices at exactly 30%/21%/10%: measured _compute_faab_bid(1905, 100, 1905) = (30, 21, 10), where 1905 is Marlin Klein, a TE outside every starting lineup on the live board. The one stage that could ground the number in observed prices, _position_calibration (faab_recommender.py:172-194), blends 50/50 with the position's historical AVERAGE regardless of player quality, needs >=3 samples, and is structurally unavailable for the non-default league (server.py:5003-5017).
findings.userImpact: The number is not defensible as a bid. It answers 'what fraction of the board's top asset is this player?' and prints a dollar sign on the answer. In a barren week it recommends 21% of budget for the least-bad option; in a week with a genuine league-winner on the wire it recommends the same 21%. There is no mechanism by which it can say 'bid nothing this week' other than the drop-side comparison.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: Two different FAAB dollar figures for the same player are rendered on the same page, and they disagree by 75%
findings.rootCause: /waivers renders a client-computed FAAB hint column (computeFaabHint) in the Best-moves table, normalized to the top of the DISPLAYED batch and a hard-coded $100 budget, while the bid desk above it renders the backend recommend_faab standard, normalized to the pick-contaminated whole-pool max. Neither knows the other exists.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/waivers/page.jsx:206-223 - `computeFaabHint(Number(m.addValue || ...), { leagueBudget: 100, topValueInPool: topAddValue })` with topAddValue = max addValue in moves (page.jsx:167-174). Measured on the live contract for team 'Blaine': the hint column prints $21 for Mitchell Evans (topValueInPool = 1770 = his own value => share 1.0 => 30% aggressive / 21% reasonable), while POST /api/waiver/faab-recommend returns standard: 12 for the same player and the same $100 budget. The unused backend suggestions route returns a third number, reasonable: 20.
findings.userImpact: A user reads $21 in the Best-moves table, clicks the same player into the calculator, and the bid desk says $12. Both are presented as this product's recommendation. The top row of that column also always reads $21/$30 by construction, because share is 1.0 for whoever leads the batch.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: The waiver comparison subtracts raw scraper-composite values from canonical board values, and every headline drop recommendation is one of those rows
findings.rootCause: rowValue falls back to values.full when rankDerivedValue is absent (waiver-logic.js:196-205). On the default view=app payload buildRows takes the legacy-dict branch (server.py:1953-1954 strips playersArray from the runtime view), where values.full = rankDerivedValue || rawValues.full - i.e. _finalAdjusted, the raw scraper composite. The candidate pool guards against this (rowHasNoRealRank + sourceCount<2 at waiver-logic.js:341,363) but the ROSTER side applies neither gate (waiver-logic.js:547-554 checks only assetClass=='pick' and rowValue<=0).
findings.evidence: waiver-logic.js:201-204 - `const v = Number(row?.rankDerivedValue); if (Number.isFinite(v) && v > 0) return v; const v2 = Number(row?.values?.full); return ...`. Executed against the real contract with the real buildRows on a runtime-shaped payload: 12 of team Blaine's 52 matched roster rows carry rankDerivedValue null and are priced off _finalAdjusted (AJ Haulcy 1954, Divine Deablo 1913, James Pearce 1907, Cole Bishop 1876, Mack Hollins 1107, Derek Carr 888, Colton Hood 497...). The resulting top-5 Droppable rows are Colton Hood 497, Caden Curry 510, Dante McClellan 515, Bryan Thompson 744, Isaiah Williams 744 - ALL unstamped fallback rows. Scale mismatch over the 805 players carrying both numbers: _finalAdjusted/rankDerivedValue median 1.099, p10 0.958, p90 1.268, max 1.704.
findings.userImpact: Every 'Drop X' the page leads with is a number the canonical pipeline declined to stamp, subtracted from a canonical number to produce the net gain and the tier badge. The gating is one-sided: an unstamped player can only ever be DROPPED, never ADDED. The headline tier flips on this alone - with the fallback rows in, the top move is 'strong' (net 1273); with them out, 'considering' (net 848). CLAUDE.md records this exact scale-mixing as a defect already fixed in finder.py (WS-J F-6 / finding K); it survives here.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: computeFaabHint is not a faithful port of _compute_faab_bid - 10.8% of the input grid returns different dollars
findings.rootCause: Python round() is round-half-to-even; JS Math.round() is round-half-up. Both implementations round three times (aggressive, reasonable, lowball).
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js:851 claims 'JS port of ``src/trade/waiver.py::_compute_faab_bid``'. Executed both over a 600-point grid (budgets 50/100/200 x 200 share steps): 65 divergences. budget 100, value 2999.7, top 9999 -> JS (13,9,5), Python (12,8,4); budget 50, value 9999 -> JS (15,11,5), Python (15,10,5). No parity test exists (tests/api/test_source_registry_parity.py covers the source registry, nothing covers this pair).
findings.userImpact: Small in dollars, but the two surfaces cannot be reconciled even after the denominators are fixed, and the docstring asserts a parity the code does not hold.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: The FAAB hint column hard-codes a $100 league budget
findings.rootCause: page.jsx passes { leagueBudget: 100 } literally, while the real budget is available two components away (leagueFaab.leagueBudget from /api/public/league/faabAnalytics, and selectedTeam.faabBudget from the Sleeper overlay).
findings.evidence: frontend/app/waivers/page.jsx:211-219 - `computeFaabHint(..., { leagueBudget: 100, topValueInPool: topAddValue })`, headerInfo at :222 'Quick baseline share of a $100 budget'. ManualAddDrop.jsx:99-124 renders the REAL budget in the same page's header strip. config/leagues/registry.json defines two active leagues; the default league's Sleeper settings carry waiver_budget: 100 (verified in exports/latest), the second league's budget is Not Verifiable from Repository.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: The Max bid pill is labelled 'your remaining' even when it is the league budget
findings.rootCause: recommend_faab sets cap_source = team_faab_remaining if not None else league_budget and returns it as max (faab_recommender.py:530-550); the UI labels that tile unconditionally.
findings.evidence: src/trade/faab_recommender.py:533-534 - `cap_source = team_faab_remaining if team_faab_remaining is not None else league_budget`; frontend/components/waivers/FaabRecommendation.jsx:511-515 - `<StatTile label="Max" value={fmtBid(data?.max)} meta="your remaining" />`. team_faab_remaining is only set when teamOwnerId matches a CURRENT roster AND the overlay resolved an integer faabRemaining (server.py:5033-5044); the baked contract carries no faabRemaining at all (verified against exports/latest), so any overlay failure silently produces this state.
findings.userImpact: A user who has spent 90% of their budget can be shown 'Max $100 - your remaining' and bid money they do not have. The failure is silent: nothing else on the panel distinguishes the two cases.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: /api/waiver/suggestions scales its bids off faabRemaining passed as the league BUDGET, and takes it from the request body
findings.rootCause: server.py reads faabRemaining from the POST body (default 100) and passes it as user_faab_remaining, which find_waiver_targets forwards as league_budget= into _compute_faab_bid.
findings.evidence: server.py:4805-4818 - `faab_remaining = int(body.get("faabRemaining", 100))` -> `user_faab_remaining=faab_remaining`; src/trade/waiver.py:195-207 - `if user_faab_remaining is None or user_faab_remaining <= 0: user_faab_remaining = 100` then `_compute_faab_bid(c.consensus_value, league_budget=user_faab_remaining, ...)`. The endpoint never consults the league registry or the Sleeper overlay for the real budget.
findings.userImpact: Zero today - the route has no caller (verified: no reference in frontend/, no Next bridge route under frontend/app/api/waiver/). But the code computes 30% of REMAINING where the formula's own comments say 30% of BUDGET, so any future caller inherits a silently different meaning. It also ignores idpEnabled: _BASE_POSITIONS (waiver.py:27-48) always includes DL/LB/DB, so an offense-only league would get IDP waiver targets.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: tierBids is computed and shipped on every analytics payload but consumed by nothing, while two docstrings claim it drives calibration
findings.rootCause: faab_analytics builds a four-tier bid histogram; the recommender's calibration reads only positionBids.
findings.evidence: src/api/faab_analytics.py:306 - `"tierBids": {label: _stats_block(vals) for label, vals in tier_bids.items()}`; the only other repo references are its own docstring line 198 and the tests. src/trade/faab_recommender.py:13-14 documents step 4 as 'League analytics calibration (blend with historical bid-by-pos+tier)' and src/api/faab_analytics.py:11-14 says it calibrates against 'similar position+tier'. _position_calibration (faab_recommender.py:183-194) reads positionBids[position] only. recentWins is likewise unconsumed.
findings.userImpact: The recommendation blends a $1 dart throw halfway toward the same position average as a league-winning claim, while the documentation says it is tier-aware. An auditor reading the docs concludes the bid is better grounded than it is.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: The rival-contention model reads the unscoped market contract while the user's bid reads the valuation-lens-scoped one
findings.rootCause: The endpoint threads valuation_mode into _valuation_scoped_contract and uses the scoped arr for the add/drop values and pool max, but passes the module-global latest_contract_data to the contention estimator for the opponent asset pool and the player-position map.
findings.evidence: server.py:4892-4894 `contract, valuation_mode, valuation_note = await _valuation_scoped_contract(...)` and :4896 `arr = (contract or {}).get("playersArray")`, versus server.py:5227-5233 `contract=latest_contract_data, ... id_to_position=_faab_contention.player_position_map(latest_contract_data)`.
findings.userImpact: Under the league-adjusted lens the user's bid is priced on one board while rival need levels and the opponent asset pool come from another, yet the response stamps a single valuationMode for both. Second-order, since need levels are categorical.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: The 'Smash only' upgrade filter and most of the min-gain slider are unreachable on live data
findings.rootCause: The tier thresholds are absolute board-point gaps (2000/1000/250) calibrated for starter-vs-bench swaps, but the waiver pool tops out far below the roster gap needed to clear them.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js:43-47 `smash: 2000`; frontend/app/waivers/page.jsx:54-59 exposes `{ value: "smash", label: "Smash only" }`; page.jsx:666-674 ships a min-gain slider with max={5000}. Executed across all 12 rosters on the live contract: maximum netGain anywhere in the league = 1284; tier counts across all teams = {strong: 92, considering: 1013, marginal: 95, smash: 0}; the smash-filtered addable list is length 0 for every one of the 12 teams.
findings.userImpact: A user who selects 'Smash only' always gets 'No upgrades match your filters', which reads as a broken page rather than an empty answer. Roughly three quarters of the slider's travel is dead.

findings.area: Waivers + FAAB (frontend /waivers, lib/waiver-logic.js, ManualAddDrop, FaabRecommendation; backend /api/waiver/suggestions, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, faab_rec
findings.title: Player headshots in the add/drop picker read a field the default payload does not carry
findings.rootCause: ManualAddDrop reads r.raw?.playerId, but on the default view=app (legacy-dict) path row.raw is the legacy player object, which keys the Sleeper id as _sleeperId; the materialized row exposes it as row.playerId.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/waivers/ManualAddDrop.jsx:209 and :247 - `playerId={r.raw?.playerId}` / `playerId={row.raw?.playerId}`; frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1269 `raw: player` (legacy dict entry) and :1176 `playerId: String(player._sleeperId || "").trim() || null`. Verified against the built contract: players['Mitchell Evans'] has _sleeperId '12473' and no playerId key. FaabRecommendation.jsx:283 gets this right by falling back.
findings.userImpact: Cosmetic - the picker renders fallback avatars on the default payload path.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: /edge "Sell signals" is a scoring-format artifact: 36 of 36 eligible tight ends are labelled SELL, and zero are labelled BUY
findings.rootCause: _compute_market_gap compares raw ordinal ranks between ktcSfTep (a TE-PREMIUM board, `is_tep_premium: True`, the sole is_retail source) and a consensus mean dominated by base-TE boards. The pipeline's TE basis conversion (te_premium.convert_te_value, data_contract.py:6451-6467) operates on VALUES inside the blend and never touches the ordinals fed to _compute_market_gap, so the format difference passes straight through into the buy/sell direction.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:2786-2792 `retail_mean = sum(retail_ranks) / len(retail_ranks)` … `diff = consensus_mean - retail_mean` … `if diff > 0: return "retail_premium"`. Recomputed on the live 2026-08-04 contract, direction by position for top-250 offense rows: TE {sell: 36}, QB {buy: 29, sell: 2}, RB {sell: 14, buy: 31}, WR {buy: 47, sell: 17}. Of the 50 rows that qualify for the Sell panel, 34 are TEs; 9 of the 10 actually rendered are TEs (Eli Raridon, Oscar Delp, Mason Taylor, Greg Dulcich, Hunter Henry, Pat Freiermuth, Dalton Schultz, AJ Barner, Max Klare). Excluding idpTradeCalc does not change it: still 36/36 sell.
findings.userImpact: A user who acts on /edge is told to sell every tight end on their roster and buy nearly every quarterback, every single day, forever. The signal carries no player-specific information at those positions — it is a restatement of which scoring format KTC publishes.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: /edge Buy/Sell panels gate and rank on sourceRankSpread, which is not the retail-vs-consensus gap they claim to show
findings.rootCause: The panels read marketGapDirection (retail vs consensus) for the SIGN but sourceRankSpread (max−min across all sources) for the MAGNITUDE and the sort. marketGapMagnitude — the field that actually measures the gap — is stamped by the backend and never read by this page.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/edge/page.jsx:137-150 `r.marketGapDirection === "retail_premium" && (r.sourceRankSpread ?? 0) >= PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD` … `.sort((a, b) => (b.sourceRankSpread ?? 0) - (a.sourceRankSpread ?? 0))`; frontend/lib/edge-helpers.js:336 `detail: \`Sell +${r.sourceRankSpread} ranks\``; frontend/app/edge/edge-columns.jsx:84 `accessor: (r) => r.sourceRankSpread ?? null`. Backend stamps the correct field at src/api/data_contract.py:7723 `row["marketGapMagnitude"] = gap_mag`. Measured on the live contract over the 143 qualifying rows: Spearman(spread, gapMag) = 0.585; 60 rows (42%) have a real gap under 10 ranks and 29 (20%) under 5, minimum 0.08. De'Zhaun Stribling is rendered as the #3 Sell signal with spread 184 and a real retail-vs-consensus gap of 6 ranks — his spread comes from idpTradeCalc 288 vs dynastyDaddySf 104, two sources on the SAME side of the comparison.
findings.userImpact: The list is ordered by a quantity orthogonal to the claim in the panel title, and the per-row caption "Sell +184 ranks" is a number that does not describe any retail-vs-consensus gap.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: 38% of rows in /edge's Buy/Sell panels render as HOLD in the /rankings Edge column for the same player in the same session
findings.rootCause: Two independent definitions of the same BUY/SELL verb. /rankings requires |consensusMean − retailMean| ≥ 10 ordinal ranks; /edge requires only a nonzero difference plus sourceRankSpread ≥ 20 and board rank ≤ 250. Neither reads the other.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/display-helpers.js:164-171 `if (diff < MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF) { return { label: "aligned", … kind: "aligned" } }` → marketAction:241-248 maps aligned to `label: "HOLD"`; frontend/lib/thresholds.js:46 `export const MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF = 10;` versus frontend/app/edge/page.jsx:143 `(r.sourceRankSpread ?? 0) >= PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD` (=20). Recomputed on the live contract: of the 143 rows eligible for the /edge Buy/Sell panels, the /rankings Edge column reads HOLD for 55 of them (38%) — including A.J. Brown, C.J. Stroud, Christian McCaffrey, Bryce Young, Chris Olave. Among the 10 rows actually rendered per panel, De'Zhaun Stribling (gap 6) is the live contradiction.
findings.userImpact: The same payload gives contradictory trade verbs on two pages one click apart, with no indication that the two use different rules.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: A single source dropping out silently re-ranks most of the board, and the result is published as a real move with buy/sell framing
findings.rootCause: canonicalConsensusRank is a blend over whichever sources happened to produce a row this cycle. rankChange diffs against the previous build and /api/movers diffs against a historical snapshot; neither pass records or compares the SOURCE SET, so a change in inputs is indistinguishable from a change in the market.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:4729-4736 `prev = previous.get(name)` … `row["rankChange"] = prev - cur_rank` — no coverage term. Simulation on the live payload via `build_api_data_contract(raw, source_overrides={key: {'include': False}})` (which does not write the snapshot): dropping dlfSf changes canonicalConsensusRank for 438 of 740 ranked rows, 7 of them by ≥15 ranks (Marquise Brown −20, Deebo Samuel −19, DeMario Douglas −18); dropping yahooBoone changes 509 rows, 10 by ≥15 (Grant Calcaterra +57, Quinn Ewers +52, Riley Nowakowski +51, Dyami Brown −38). 15 is exactly the /api/movers default threshold (server.py:3378).
findings.userImpact: Rows appear in "Risers — buy-low candidates" / "Fallers — sell-high candidates", in the ticker, and in /trending, complete with a per-source breakdown, purely because a fetcher failed. Nothing on those surfaces distinguishes this from a market move.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: HOLD is returned for "we have no history at all" with the reason "Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers"
findings.rootCause: HOLD is the fallback when zero rules fire. Zero rules fire both when a player is genuinely quiet and when trend7, trend30 and volatility are all null. The engine has no insufficient-evidence state.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/signal-engine.js:195-203 `if (fired.length === 0) { return { signal: SIGNALS.HOLD, primary: null, reason: "Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers.", tag: "default_hold", fired: [] }; }`; identical at src/api/terminal.py:959-965. buildContext (:224-227) produces null trends whenever historyPoints is empty, and computeVolatility returns null below 3 points (value-history.js:110).
findings.userImpact: On a fresh deploy, after a rank_history.jsonl loss, or for any player the log does not cover, the entire roster renders as "Hold — Stable", asserting stability the system has no evidence for. data/rank_history.jsonl does not exist in this checkout at all, so this is the state a cold environment presents.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: SELL fires — and emails — on one day of movement while the reason claims a sustained 30-day downtrend
findings.rootCause: computeWindowTrend takes the earliest point INSIDE the window rather than a point windowDays old. When the log is shorter than 30 days, trend30 is numerically identical to trend7, so the "7d continues 30d" conjunction is satisfied by a single observation.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/value-history.js:94-100 `const cutoff = latest.t - windowDays * 86400_000; for (const p of points) { if (p.t >= cutoff) { baseline = p; break; } }`. Reproduced with node: a 2-point series 1 day apart gives trend7 = trend30 = −5; a 3-point series 2 days apart gives trend7 = trend30 = −6. The rule at signal-engine.js:85-88 then fires SELL with `reason: \`7d trend ${fmtDelta(c.trend7)} continues a 30d trend of ${fmtDelta(c.trend30)}.\`` SELL is in ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS (src/api/signal_alerts.py:57), so it is emailed.
findings.userImpact: Users are emailed a SELL on a 5-rank single-scrape wobble, with a rationale asserting a month-long pattern the data cannot support.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: The Hampel outlier filter can manufacture the market gap that /edge then reports as a BUY signal
findings.rootCause: The blend drops outlier sources and stamps effectiveSourceRanks; the market-gap and IDP-edge computations both read the POST-drop map. When the dropped sources are the ones agreeing with the retail anchor, the surviving consensus mean is pulled away from retail and a large gap appears.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:7663-7672 `effective_source_ranks = {k: v for k, v in source_ranks.items() if k not in dropped_set}` … `gap_dir, gap_mag = _compute_market_gap(effective_source_ranks)` (:7721). Live row, Nick Bolton: `sourceRanks = {idpTradeCalc: 158, dlfIdp: 155, idpShow: 158, fantasyProsIdp: 66, draftSharksIdp: 97}`, `droppedSources = ['dlfIdp', 'idpShow']`, `effectiveSourceRanks = {idpTradeCalc: 158, fantasyProsIdp: 66, draftSharksIdp: 97}`. The two dropped sources agreed with IDPTC to within 3 ranks. /edge computes consensus mean 81.5 vs IDPTC 158 → diff 76 → "BUY" (display-helpers.js:319-397 reads effectiveSourceRanks first). 215 of 1,092 live rows carry droppedSources.
findings.userImpact: A 76-rank buy signal on a player where 3 of 5 sources agree within 3 ranks. The filter designed to protect the blend from outliers is being used as evidence of market disagreement.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: idpTradeCalc's offense ranks sit a median 104 ranks below the rest of the consensus and flip the buy/sell verdict on 10.6% of offense rows
findings.rootCause: idpTradeCalc is registered under overall_idp with `extra_scopes: [SOURCE_SCOPE_OVERALL_OFFENSE]`, so its offense ordinals come from a combined offense+IDP board where defenders occupy slots. Those ordinals are then averaged as a peer with pure-offense boards inside the "expert consensus" mean.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:1039-1041 `"scope": SOURCE_SCOPE_OVERALL_IDP, "extra_scopes": [SOURCE_SCOPE_OVERALL_OFFENSE]`; _compute_market_gap:2780-2782 puts every non-retail key on the consensus side with no scope check. Measured over 386 live offense rows carrying both idpTradeCalc and ktcSfTep: idpTradeCalc's effective rank minus the mean of the other consensus sources is median +104.2 / mean +130.4. Dropping idpTradeCalc from the consensus flips the buy/sell direction on 41 of 386 rows (10.6%). Concrete rows: Hunter Henry idpTradeCalc 294 vs a 153-244 range for every other source; Eli Raridon 495 vs 163-276.
findings.userImpact: One structurally-deeper source biases every offense row toward "retail premium" (SELL), and on one row in ten it is solely responsible for the verdict the user is shown.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: News impact polarity is a keyword coin-flip: "released" and "waived" are stamped POSITIVE, and one item's impact is applied to every player it names
findings.rootCause: classify() returns a single (severity, kind, impact) triple per item from two ordered regexes, and match_players applies that one impact to every known name found by substring in the text.
findings.evidence: src/news/providers/_rss.py:46-61 `_WATCH_KEYWORDS = ("trade", "traded", "signs", "signed", "contract", …, "released", "waived", "claim", "claimed", "activated")`; :96-98 `if _WATCH_RE.search(text): … return "watch", kind, "positive"`; :28-45 `_ALERT_KEYWORDS` includes "questionable" and "doubtful" → `return "alert", "injury", "negative"` (:94-95); :139-146 `for name in known_names: … if (key in haystack) { out.append(PlayerMention(name=name, impact=impact)) }` — one `impact` argument for all matches. Consumers: signal-engine.js:233-239 and terminal.py:776-784 count these into positiveImpactCount / negativeImpactCount / alertCount, which drive BUY@38, SELL@78, RISK@100 and MONITOR@65 — all four of which are in ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS.
findings.userImpact: "Player X released by the Jets" produces a positive impact; combined with any upward rankChange it emails a BUY. A headline reading "X placed on IR; Y promoted to starter" stamps alert+negative on BOTH names, so the beneficiary Y can be emailed a RISK. A routine Wednesday "questionable" tag is an alert-severity injury event.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: Four independent BUY/SELL label families run on the same players with four different threshold sets and no reconciliation
findings.rootCause: Each system was built against its own inputs and never cross-referenced. Two of the four email the user.
findings.evidence: (1) frontend/lib/signal-engine.js:29-36 + src/api/terminal.py:848-972 — RISK/SELL/MONITOR/STRONG_HOLD/BUY/HOLD from rank trend, volatility, news. (2) frontend/lib/display-helpers.js:205-255 — BUY/SELL/HOLD at |mean gap| ≥ 10 ranks. (3) frontend/app/edge/page.jsx:137-165 — Buy/Sell panels at spread ≥ 20 with any nonzero gap. (4) src/bdvm/market.py:185-225 — STRONG_BUY/BUY/HOLD/SELL/STRONG_SELL/NO_MARKET at alpha ±400/±900 with a 14-day persistence guard, flag default TRUE (src/api/feature_flags.py:225) and emailing via ACTIONABLE_BDVM_SIGNALS (src/api/bdvm_signal_alerts.py:43). A fifth vocabulary, idpMarketAction, adds BUY/SELL/HOLD for defenders with idpTradeCalc as "retail" — the opposite of the backend's retail definition.
findings.userImpact: The same player can simultaneously read BUY on /rankings, SELL on /bdvm, and Hold in the Signals panel, and the user can receive two contradictory emails in one sweep. Nothing on any surface names which concept produced which verb.

findings.title: Dismissing a signal in the Signals panel does not silence it in the TopSignalsRail directly above
findings.rootCause: BuySellHold dismisses using the Sleeper-ID alias key when one exists, and user_kv stores only the single key it is handed. TopSignalsRail's dismissal check constructs only the display-name key.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/terminal/BuySellHold.jsx:279-285 `const key = entry.aliasSignalKey || entry.signalKey; dismissSignal(key, …)` — alias preferred; src/api/user_kv.py:471-479 writes exactly one key (`patch["dismissedSignalsByLeague"] = _merge_per_league_dismissals(existing, key, add={str(signal_key): expires_at})`). BuySellHold reads both keys (:147-152 `const expiresAt = Math.max(primaryExp, aliasExp);`) but TopSignalsRail:39-43 reads only `` `${name}::${tag}` ``. Every offense/IDP row carries a Sleeper ID (rawData.players[...]._sleeperId, BuySellHold.jsx:90-101), so the alias branch is the normal path.
findings.userImpact: The user dismisses a SELL, the panel hides it, and the same SELL card stays pinned at the top of the page.

findings.title: Every card in TopSignalsRail is missing its position, value, 30-day delta and evidence line because four field names do not exist
findings.rootCause: The component reads fields off `verdict` that live on `entry`, and a `delta30d` / `evidence` shape the engine has never produced.
findings.evidence: evaluateRoster returns `{ row, context, verdict, news }` (frontend/lib/signal-engine.js:314). TopSignalsRail.jsx:50 `const d = Number(verdict?.context?.delta30d);` — `verdict` has no `context` key, and `buildContext` returns `trend30`, not `delta30d` (signal-engine.js:252). :56 `const v = Number(verdict?.context?.value);` — same missing path. :65 `const evidence = entry?.verdict?.evidence?.[0] || "";` — `evaluate` returns `{signal, primary, reason, tag, fired}`, no `evidence` (:206-217). :61 `entry?.row?.position` — buildRows emits `pos`, never `position` (frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:996, 1177). Repo-wide grep confirms `delta30d` appears on the signal path only in this file's comment and dead read, and `verdict.evidence` only here.
findings.userImpact: The rail promises "top 3 buy and sell candidates" and renders a badge and a name — no position, no value, no movement, no reason. The comment at :46-49 asserts buildContext sets delta30d, which is false.

findings.title: MoversPanel labels risers as buy-low candidates and fallers as sell-high candidates — both inverted
findings.rootCause: Column headings assign a trade verb opposite to the direction of the data they head.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/terminal/MoversPanel.jsx:191-193 `Risers — buy-low candidates` over `risers = data?.risers || []`; :207-209 `Fallers — sell-high candidates` over `fallers`. server.py:3367 defines the terms unambiguously: "Risers = rank improved (number got smaller). Fallers = rank got worse." server.py:3495-3498 `if delta > 0: risers.append(entry) else: fallers.append(entry)` with `delta = r_then - r_now`.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: "Value crosses threshold" alerts are level tests with no memory, and re-fire every 24 hours indefinitely
findings.rootCause: evaluate_alerts compares the current value against the threshold with no reference to the previous value, so it cannot detect a transition. The only limiter is a 24h cooldown.
findings.evidence: src/news/custom_alerts.py:224-231 `v = int(round(float(value)))` … `crossed = (direction == "above" and v >= threshold) or (direction == "below" and v <= threshold)`; :54 `COOLDOWN_HOURS = 24`; :149-160 `_is_cooldown` returns True only within 24h of the last fire. Module docstring :5 claims "fires when rankDerivedValue crosses a target"; the UI reads "crosses above" (frontend/components/CustomAlertsConfigurator.jsx:223).
findings.userImpact: A user who sets "alert me when Player X crosses above 6000" on a player already at 7500 gets an email every single day, forever. The alert channel trains the user to ignore it.

findings.evidence: frontend/lib/movers.js:48-50 `if (windowDays <= 1) { const rc = Number(r.rankChange); … }` under a docstring at :31-40 reading "the 1-day case uses the contract's pre-stamped rankChange (which is the day-over-day delta the backend already computes)"; WINDOW_OPTIONS:20 `{ key: "1d", label: "1 day", days: 1 }`. src/api/data_contract.py:4710-4742 reads and rewrites the snapshot on the same build; .github/workflows/scheduled-refresh.yml:14 `- cron: "42 */2 * * *"`. MarketTicker gets this right ("fewer than 3 moves since last update", MarketTicker.jsx:126) and ScoutingIntel gets it right ("on the last scrape", portfolio-insights.js:501).

findings.title: Window labels across the movement surfaces count snapshots, not days, and degrade silently when scraping lapses
findings.rootCause: load_history slices the last N ENTRIES; entries are appended only on a fresh scrape and deduped to one per UTC date. /api/movers then anchors on series[0] with no date check at all.
findings.evidence: src/api/rank_history.py:368 `windowed = entries[-max(1, int(days)) :]`; server.py:3390 `history = _rank_history.load_history(days=window + 1)` then :3443-3444 `latest = series[-1]` / `anchor = series[0]`; append only on fresh scrape at server.py:1866-1868 `if is_fresh_scrape: _rank_history.append_snapshot(contract_payload)`. MoversPanel subtitle: `Rank deltas vs. ${windowDays}d ago` (MoversPanel.jsx:163). PlayerMarketMovement offers a 180d tab (:26) against a client cache clamped to 180 (`Math.min(180, …)`, value-history.js:32).
findings.userImpact: If the scraper misses days, "vs 14d ago" quietly becomes "vs however far back our 15 surviving snapshots reach" while still printing 14d. The frontend's own computeWindowTrend at least applies a real date cutoff; the server endpoint does not.

findings.title: The IDP Buy/Sell comparison averages effective ranks that are not on a common scale
findings.rootCause: idpTradeCalc contributes a direct ordinal while the expert boards contribute ladder-translated synthetic overall-IDP ranks. The translations disagree with each other by hundreds of positions, and idpMarketEdge averages them as peers against the untranslated anchor.
findings.evidence: Live row, Micah Parsons sourceRankMeta: `dlfIdp {rawRank: 3, effectiveRank: 47, method: 'exact', ladderDepth: 370}`, `idpShow {rawRank: 5, effectiveRank: 64}`, `fantasyProsIdp {rawRank: 54, effectiveRank: 242}`, `draftSharksIdp {rawRank: 130, effectiveRank: 528, method: 'ds_combined_cross_market'}`, `idpTradeCalc {rawRank: 64, effectiveRank: 64, method: 'direct'}`. frontend/lib/display-helpers.js:333-337 `const consensusRanks = Object.entries(ranks).filter(([k, v]) => IDP_CONSENSUS_KEYS.has(k) && v != null).map(([, v]) => Number(v));` then :368 `const consensusMean = consensusRanks.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / consensusRanks.length;`. Result: the four best IDP players in the pool (Abdul Carter, Micah Parsons, Jared Verse, Myles Garrett) are the four largest SELL signals, with gaps of 176, 156, 155 and 107 ranks.
findings.userImpact: The IDP sell list is a list of elite defenders, produced by translation spread rather than by market disagreement. Only 17 rows are evaluated at all, so the panel is small enough that these dominate it.

findings.area: SIGNAL layer — signal-engine, edge-helpers, movers/market-movers, thresholds, value-history, ros-index/sources, news-service/filters; pages /edge /trending /mar
findings.title: Both signal engines attribute other players' news impact to the player being evaluated
findings.rootCause: After selecting the items that mention a player, both engines iterate over ALL PlayerMentions in each item and increment the counters, rather than reading only the mention for the player under evaluation.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/signal-engine.js:233-239 `for (const it of items) { if (it.severity === "alert") alertCount += 1; for (const p of it.players || []) { if (p?.impact === "negative") negativeImpactCount += 1; else if (p?.impact === "positive") positiveImpactCount += 1; } }`; identical at src/api/terminal.py:776-784. `items` is `newsByPlayer.get(key)` (signal-engine.js:311) — items mentioning this player, but every co-mentioned player's impact is then counted for him.
findings.userImpact: An item naming five players inflates the counter fivefold. Combined with the uniform per-item polarity from _rss.py, a player merely named alongside an injured teammate inherits that item's negative impact and can be pushed to RISK or SELL. The counters are wrong on both engines identically, so the parity fixture cannot catch it.

findings.area: Remaining frontend surfaces: home, /settings, /more, /admin, /design, /players/compare, /tools/* (3), all 30 frontend/app/api bridge routes, middleware + public
findings.title: The measured TE-premium curve (ADR-015) is structurally unreachable from the UI: the default settings object forces the override path on every session
findings.rootCause: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier is the finite number 1.15, not the null sentinel that means "let the backend derive/curve it". tepMultiplierIsCustomized returns true for any finite number, so fetchDynastyData takes the override POST path for every user with untouched settings and sends tep_multiplier: 1.15. The backend stamps that as source="override", and the curve gate is `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:` — so the curve never runs on any board a browser renders. A one-time migration actively converts persisted null (the old auto value) INTO 1.15.
findings.evidence:
frontend/components/useSettings.js:35 `tepMultiplier: 1.15,               // 1.15 default; 1.0..1.5 = explicit operator override`
frontend/components/useSettings.js:184-188 `if (merged.tepMultiplier == null || merged.tepMultiplier === 1.0 || merged.tepMultiplier === 1.25) { merged.tepMultiplier = 1.15; }`
frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:893-897 `export function tepMultiplierIsCustomized(tepMultiplier) { if (tepMultiplier === null || tepMultiplier === undefined) return false; const n = Number(tepMultiplier); return Number.isFinite(n); }`
frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1987 `const tepCustomized = tepMultiplierIsCustomized(tepMultiplier);` → :1989 `const customized = sitesCustomized || tepCustomized || tepNativeCustomized;` → :2042-2044 `if (tepCustomized) { body.tep_multiplier = tepMultiplier; }`
src/api/data_contract.py:8524-8526 `else: tep_multiplier_effective = float(tep_multiplier); tep_multiplier_source = "override"`
src/api/data_contract.py:8686 `tep_multiplier_is_override=(tep_multiplier_source == "override"),`
src/api/data_contract.py:6450-6452 `te_basis_conversion = False` / `_convert_te_value = None` / `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:`
src/api/data_contract.py:7194-7207 `if te_basis_conversion: value = min(float(_convert_te_value(value, from_basis=_TE_SOURCE_DEFAULT_BASIS, to_basis=_BOARD_TE_BASIS)), 9999.0) ... else: value = min(value * effective_non_tep_multiplier, 9999.0)`
Executed the two predicates verbatim in node against SETTINGS_DEFAULTS: `{sitesCustomized:false, tepCustomized:true, tepNativeCustomized:false, customized:true}` → `POST body: { tep_multiplier: 1.15 }`.
findings.userImpact: Every TE on the rendered board is priced with the flat 1.15 rather than KTC's measured uplift. Reproduced ratio of curve to flat, by base value: 9000→+5.1%, 5000→+5.1%, 3000→+10.8%, 2000→+17.8%, 1000→+34.8%, 600→+53.1%, 400→+72.4%, 200→+78.5%. Mid- and low-board tight ends are systematically undervalued in the trade calculator, the arbitrage finder, waivers and the draft board — every engine reads the same rankDerivedValue. It also means CLAUDE.md's ADR-015 description of the live pipeline, and the claimed rollback lever RISKIT_FEATURE_TE_BASIS_CONVERSION=0, describe a code path no user reaches; setting that flag to 0 would change nothing observable.

findings.title: Hill Curve Explorer draws the curve ~300 ranks past where the engine stops, so a chart artifact reads as a model residual
findings.rootCause: The backend clamps rank→percentile at _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N = 500 (p ≤ 1.0), so every player past rank 500 shares the curve's tail value. The frontend evaluator has no such clamp and keeps descending, while its x-domain is driven by the live board's max rank (backend OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT is 800).
findings.evidence:
frontend/components/graphs/HillCurveExplorer.jsx:39-43 `function hillValue(rank, { midpoint, slope }) { const r = Math.max(1, rank); const exponent = Math.pow((r - 1) / midpoint, slope); return Math.max(1, Math.min(9999, Math.round(1 + 9998 / (1 + exponent)))); }` — no reference-N clamp
frontend/components/graphs/HillCurveExplorer.jsx:158-159 `const maxRank = ranked.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.rank), 300); const xMax = Math.max(maxRank, 300);`
src/canonical/player_valuation.py:406 `p = max(0.0, min(1.0, float(percentile)))`
src/api/data_contract.py:4881 `p = (float(rank) - 1.0) / max(1.0, float(_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N - 1))` with :4933 `_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N: int = 500`
frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1518-1520 (the InfoTip telling the reader how to interpret it): "The curve is the canonical rank-to-value shape; each dot is where a player actually lands after per-source aggregation."
findings.userImpact: Reproduced on the global curve (midpoint 55.888, slope 0.725): the drawn curve reads 1520 at rank 600, 1381 at 700, 1270 at 800, while the engine holds 1698 flat from rank 500 onward — a −178 / −317 / −428 gap. On the offense curve at rank 800 it is 488 vs 794. Every deep player therefore plots ABOVE the curve by a growing margin, which under the panel's own explanation reads as "the blend systematically overprices the back half of the board". It is the chart's missing clamp.

findings.title: /players/compare's fairness bands are uncalibrated inline constants that exist nowhere else in the codebase
findings.rootCause: The 5% and 12% cut points and their prose prescriptions are literals in the render function. frontend/lib/thresholds.js exists specifically to hold shared cut points and to mirror the backend's; these are not in it, and nothing on the backend produces a comparable verdict.
findings.evidence:
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:382 `const tone = pctGap < 5 ? "var(--cyan)" : pctGap < 12 ? "var(--amber)" : "var(--red)";`
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:388-392 `{pctGap < 5 ? "Effectively even — fair 1-for-1." : pctGap < 12 ? "Slight lean — small balancer would close the gap." : "Stretch — needs a meaningful add-on to balance."}`
frontend/lib/thresholds.js:1-12 `// Single source of truth for numeric thresholds used across Rankings, Edge, and Finder surfaces. … When changing a threshold here, check whether the backend equivalent needs to match:` — and the file contains no compare-page entry.

A 500-point gap at the top of the board is called fairer than a 60-point gap at the bottom. The panel is titled "Quick verdict" and reads as a fairness ruling; it is a percentage of the larger number with two guessed cut points.

frontend/app/admin/page.jsx:83 `if (err) { … }` — the "Not authorized" branch, reachable only from that fetch
server.py:2732-2736 `_PUBLIC_API_EXACT = frozenset({ "/api/health", "/api/status", …` — /api/status requires no session at all

findings.rootCause: The bridge-route layer covers an arbitrary 30 endpoints. In production nginx sends all of /api/* to FastAPI so the gap is invisible; locally, Next serves /api/* itself and any uncovered path 404s. Nothing states the inclusion criterion and no test enumerates it.

`find frontend/app/api -type f` returns exactly 30 route.js files; none is `terminal`, none is under ros/.

deploy/nginx/chaseupside-proxy.conf: `location /api/ { proxy_pass http://dynasty_backend; … }` (the only /api rule) vs `location / { proxy_pass http://dynasty_frontend; … }`

findings.title: Bridge routes are inconsistent about forwarding the session cookie, so dev-mode league resolution and auth differ per endpoint
findings.rootCause: Cookie forwarding was added ad hoc. The shared helper lib/backend-proxy.js never forwards cookies at all, so every route built on it is anonymous to the backend.
findings.evidence:
frontend/lib/backend-proxy.js:27 `const res = await fetch(url.toString(), { cache: "no-store", signal: ctl.signal });` and :46-52 `fetch(url.toString(), { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(body), signal: ctl.signal, cache: "no-store" });` — no Cookie header in either
Forwards cookie: dynasty-data (:65-66), trade/finder (:27,:33), angle/find (:18,:24), angle/packages (:18,:29), rankings/overrides (:44-46), valuation/league-adjusted (:37-39), sleeper/draft/picks (:22,:29), auth/status (:7,:15), auth/logout (:5,:14)
Does NOT forward cookie: trade/suggestions (:20-26), trade/import-ktc (:37-43), draft-capital (via proxyGet), bdvm/values, bdvm/roster, bdvm/trades, bdvm/trade-eval (all via proxyGet/proxyPost), sharp/market, sharp/cohort, ros/pick-projections, league-comparison, news, status, scrape
CLAUDE.md's own resolver spec: server.py::_resolve_league_for_request picks "2. the authenticated user's activeLeagueKey from user_kv" — which requires the cookie.
findings.userImpact: In dev, POST /api/trade/suggestions (a roster-aware, league-scoped, auth-requiring engine) reaches the backend with no session: the resolver falls through to the registry default league and the private gate sees an anonymous caller. Same for the four BDVM routes and draft-capital. A developer validating multi-league behavior locally is testing the default league regardless of what they selected. POST /api/scrape also forwards nothing, so the dev bridge cannot authenticate an operator action.

findings.area: Operational audit — scheduled jobs, monitoring, alerting and failure behavior (what is actually RUNNING vs merely configured)
findings.title: Every Sharp diagnostic workflow is structurally incapable of committing its artifact — `git add` on a path that .gitignore excludes
findings.rootCause: .gitignore:45 is a bare `data/` with narrow negations only for `data/ros/`. All four Sharp workflows that are supposed to record production state write to `data/ops/` and stage it with a PLAIN `git add`, not `git add -f` (which is what scheduled-refresh.yml correctly uses for data/scrape_state, data/player_map and data/sleeper_last_good.json). `git add` on an ignored path exits 1, and every one of these steps runs under GitHub's default `bash -e`, so the step aborts.
findings.evidence: `.gitignore:45: data/`. verify-sharp-production.yml:163 `git add data/ops/sharp-production-smoke.json`; force-sharp-production-now.yml:257 `git add data/ops/sharp-force-production-live.json`; trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml:136 `git add data/ops/sharp-no-environment-result.json`; trigger-sharp-now-via-merge.yml:130 `git add data/ops/sharp-merge-trigger-result.json`. `git check-ignore -v data/ops/sharp-production-smoke.json` → `.gitignore:45:data/`. Reproduced in a scratch repo: plain `git add` exit=1, `git add -f` exit=0. `git ls-files data/ops` → 0 files. Live proof from Actions job 91858761506 (2026-08-04T01:20:44Z): `The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: data / hint: Use -f if you really want to add them. / ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.`
findings.userImpact: There is no durable record anywhere of whether Sharp Tracker is populated. The 'Enforce healthy population' gate (verify-sharp-production.yml:167-175) is SKIPPED on every run because the commit step dies first, so the workflow's actual verdict has never once been evaluated. 79 runs, zero successes.

findings.area: Operational audit — scheduled jobs, monitoring, alerting and failure behavior (what is actually RUNNING vs merely configured)
findings.title: The Sharp production smoke polls auth-gated endpoints anonymously — 80/80 attempts return 401
findings.rootCause: `_private_api_gate` 401s every `/api/*` path not on the public allowlist. `/api/sharp/*` is not on it: `_PUBLIC_API_EXACT` (server.py:2732-2767) lists health/status/uptime/metrics/leagues/rankings-sources/auth-*/scaffold-status/draft-capital/news, and `_PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES` (server.py:2788-2796) is only `/api/public/league` and `/api/league/articles`. verify-sharp-production.yml fetches `https://chaseupside.com/api/sharp/cohort` and `/api/sharp/market` with nothing but a User-Agent header.
findings.evidence: verify-sharp-production.yml:55-64 `fetch_json` sends only `User-Agent` and `Cache-Control`. server.py:2801-2809 `_is_public_api_path` returns False for `/api/sharp/cohort`. Actions job 91858761506 result JSON: `"attempts": 80`, ten recorded errors all `{"message": "HTTP Error 401: Unauthorized", "type": "HTTPError"}` for attempts 71-80, `"status": "degraded_timeout"`, `"cohort": {}`, `"ffpcMarket": {}`.
findings.userImpact: The job burns ~40 minutes of runner time on every push to main and every deploy completion, produces a guaranteed-useless result, and has done so 79 times. Worse: because it always ends in `degraded_timeout` and then dies on the gitignore, a genuine Sharp outage and a healthy Sharp are indistinguishable from CI.

findings.title: The '<50% of sites' partial-scrape guard degenerates to 'block only on total loss' because `sites` has exactly 2 entries
findings.rootCause: The guard divides by `total_sites`, but `result['sites']` is populated only by the legacy in-scraper SITES dict, which today is KTC + IDPTradeCalc. The ~20 sources fetched by scripts/fetch_*.py in scheduled-refresh.yml never appear there, so their health cannot influence the guard.
findings.evidence: server.py:2362 `if total_sites > 0 and site_count < total_sites / 2:`. Live payload exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json `sites` = `[{"key":"ktc","label":"KTC","max":9999,"playerCount":500},{"key":"idpTradeCalc","label":"IDPTradeCalc","max":9999.0,"playerCount":900}]` — len 2. Reproduced numerically: total_sites=2 → threshold 1.0 → blocks only when site_count == 0; site_count=1 → `1 < 1.0` is False → promoted.
findings.userImpact: KTC is the anchor board for the entire value scale (it is the TE++ basis anchor per CLAUDE.md step 5a, and one of only two _VALUE_BASED_SOURCES). If KTC dies and IDPTradeCalc survives, the scrape publishes anyway — with a board missing its anchor — and the operator gets no 'PARTIAL SCRAPE NOT PROMOTED' email. docs/ops/failure-handling-and-fallbacks.md tells the operator this case is 'Not promoted — blocked by guard'. It is not.

findings.title: The ops 'scrape success rate < 50%' alert can never fire — it reads a key its input never contains
findings.rootCause: `ops_alerts.check_and_alert` is called with `status_payload=_scrape_status_payload()`, but `scrape_success_rate_24h` is produced only inside the `get_status()` HTTP handler, not in `_scrape_status_payload()`. `.get()` returns None and `_check_scrape_rate` returns on its first branch. Even if the key were added, get_status stamps it as a dict and `float(dict)` raises TypeError, which the except clause swallows into another None.
findings.evidence: src/api/ops_alerts.py:45-50 `rate = status_payload.get('scrape_success_rate_24h'); if rate is None: return None; try: r = float(rate) except (TypeError, ValueError): return None`. server.py:11588 `status_payload = _scrape_status_payload()`. server.py:1266-1304 `_scrape_status_payload` returns `dict(scrape_status)` + stall_threshold_sec + run_timeout_sec + status_summary — no rate key; the scrape_status global's key list contains no such key. `grep -n _scrape_success_rate_24h server.py` → only the definition at 1104 and one call at 4207, inside `async def get_status()`. Reproduced: `float({'total':10,'success':2,'failure':8,'rate':0.2})` → TypeError.
findings.userImpact: The headline operator alert for 'the scraper is failing' is dead. Combined with the finding below (blocked partial scrapes are recorded as successes), there is no email path at all that fires on a sustained ingestion failure. Only the CI staleness watchdog would catch it, ~24h later.

findings.title: A blocked partial scrape is recorded as a SUCCESS in scrape history
findings.rootCause: The R-3 guard path calls `_mark_scrape_success(...)` before returning the old data, and `_mark_scrape_success` calls `_record_scrape_history('success', ...)` and increments `_metrics['scrape_total']`.
findings.evidence: server.py:2380 `_mark_scrape_success(elapsed, player_count, site_count, total_sites)` inside the `if total_sites > 0 and site_count < total_sites / 2:` block, immediately before `return latest_data  # Return existing data, not the partial result` (server.py:2388). `_mark_scrape_success` (server.py definition) sets `last_success_at`, records `_record_scrape_event('scrape_succeeded', ...)` and `_record_scrape_history('success', ...)`.
findings.userImpact: `scrape_success_rate_24h` reads 100% while every single scrape is being rejected as degraded. health-check.yml:88-89 warns only when `rate < 0.5`, so its warning is suppressed too. The one metric an operator would look at to answer 'is ingestion healthy?' is measuring the wrong event.

findings.title: The Sleeper freshness stamp is written by the scraper and read by nothing
findings.rootCause: `_stamp_sleeper_success` writes `data/scrape_state/sleeper_last_success` explicitly so a Sleeper outage 'still trips the existing freshness watchdog'. But both freshness readers iterate `_SOURCE_CSV_PATHS`, whose 22 keys do not include `sleeper` (Sleeper produces no CSV).
findings.evidence: Dynasty Scraper.py:889-892 docstring: 'Stamp data/scrape_state/sleeper_last_success on a successful live fetch so a prolonged Sleeper outage still trips the existing freshness watchdog even though the scrape no longer hard-fails.' `grep -rn sleeper_last_success` across .py/.yml/.js finds ONLY the writer in Dynasty Scraper.py — zero readers. `python -c 'from src.api.data_contract import _SOURCE_CSV_PATHS; print(sorted(_SOURCE_CSV_PATHS))'` → 22 keys, no 'sleeper'. watchdog_freshness.py:66 `for src_key, entry in _SOURCE_CSV_PATHS.items()`; server.py:1584 the same loop. Live file content: `1785815666.7993538`.
findings.userImpact: A total Sleeper outage is invisible to every monitor. The scraper correctly restores the last-good roster block and correctly refuses to stamp — but nothing consumes the non-stamp, so the board silently serves rosters of arbitrary age labelled as current, with no age field anywhere in the contract, no /api/status entry, and no banner. Trade suggestions, the terminal, angle-finder and draft capital all key off those rosters.

The module itself is pure: `def _minimal_raw_payload(): return {"players": {"Josh Allen": {...}}}` (test_data_contract.py:13-36) and its only mention of a live path is inside a docstring ("``rawSourceValues.ktcSfTep`` mirrors ``CSVs/site_raw/ktcSfTep.csv``", :599-600). The same applies to `tests/adapters/test_dlf_scraper.py` (9 tests, loads scripts/fetch_dlf.py and parses HTML strings — no network, no CSV read; its own docstring says 'These tests exercise the offline-safe pure functions') and `tests/scripts/test_fetch_flock_fantasy_rookies.py` (24 tests, all tempfile-based). findings.title: The Sharp Score's entire weight vector is unpinned; every test is an inequality
findings.rootCause: tests/sharp/test_score.py was written to assert product rules (gates fire, no single signal dominates, score != confidence) and never to assert the composition.
findings.evidence: tests/sharp/test_score.py, 256 lines, contains no numeric equality on a score. The strongest numeric assertions are `assert lucky < 0.25` (:133), `assert 0.0 <= entry.confidence <= 1.0` (:142), `assert cfg["qualification"]["minScorePercentile"] >= 0.67` (:244), `assert S.percentile_rank(1.0, [1.0]*10) == 0.5` (:249). Meanwhile src/sharp/score.py:284-313 composes `parts.append((float(sub.get("winPct", 0.30)), p))`, `... ("playoffRate", 0.25)`, `... ("championshipRate", 0.20)`, `... ("medianFinishPercentile", 0.15)`, `... ("pointsForPercentile", 0.10)` and config/sharp/scoring_v2.json carries the same numbers.
findings.userImpact: You could swap the winPct and championshipRate weights, or set them all to 0.2, and the suite stays green. The config's own header admits the weights are 'PRIORS chosen for defensibility, not values validated against an outcome dataset' — so there is neither a validation nor a change-detector. A Sharp Score shown to a user is an unvalidated hand-weighted sum with no regression barrier. Secondary hazard: every weight is duplicated as an inline `sub.get(key, default)` fallback, so a typo in the JSON key silently reverts to the code default with no error.

findings.title: 23 of ~346 module-level numeric constants in src/ have a literal pin; roughly 150 are referenced by no test at all
findings.rootCause: The repo's dominant test idiom is to import the constant symbolically and assert against it, which is right for values that are legitimately refit but makes every threshold change invisible.
findings.evidence: I scanned every `^NAME = <number>` at module scope in src/**/*.py and cross-referenced against the full text of tests/. Literally pinned (23): _ALPHA_SHRINKAGE 0.10, _SINGLE_SOURCE_VALUE_RETENTION 0.30, _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N 500, _MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA 0.0, _HAMPEL_K 2.75, _HAMPEL_MIN_N 4, _HAMPEL_MIN_THRESHOLD 1000.0, _TE_BLANKET_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER 1.10, _TE_BLANKET_NON_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER 1.15, BOARD_TOP_N_FILTER 150, MAX_BALANCERS 2, MAX_GIVE_PLAYER_APPEARANCES 2, MIN_WAIVER_VALUE 500, CARDINAL_MIN_DYNAMIC_RANGE 3.0, DEFAULT_BAND 2, FULL_SEASON_WEEKS 17, MIN_GAMES_FOR_PPG 8, MIN_STORIES_FOR_DIGEST 2, PER_MEMBER_LEAGUE_CAP 25 and four schema versions. Referenced by NO test: MARKET_TOP_N_FILTER 150 (src/trade/finder.py:132), ELITE_MULTI_MIN_RATIO 0.65, MULTI_FOR_ONE_MIN_RATIO 0.55, PACKAGE_ANCHOR_MIN_PCT 0.35, JUNK_THRESHOLD 350, MIN_MARKET_VALUE 500, CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE 5, PARTIAL_MARKET_ARBITRAGE_CAP 8.0, ROSTER_SURPLUS_THRESHOLD 4 (all src/trade/finder.py); FAIRNESS_TOLERANCE 769, HIGH_DISPERSION_CV 0.12, LOW_DISPERSION_CV 0.04, CONSOLIDATION_MIN_UPGRADE_RATIO 0.70, CONSOLIDATION_MAX_OVERPAY_RATIO 0.30, MAX_SUGGESTIONS_PER_TYPE 8 (src/trade/suggestions.py); MATCH_QUARANTINE_THRESHOLD 0.90 (src/identity/matcher.py); DEFAULT_SIMULATIONS 10000, ODDS_SE_TOLERANCE 0.005, DEPTH_VARIANCE_LIFT_MAX 0.15 (src/ros/playoff_sim.py); MARKET_FAIRNESS_TOLERANCE_PCT 12.0, MIN_GAIN_EACH_SIDE 150.0 (src/bdvm/roster.py); IMPROVED_WEIGHT_* (five weights, src/league_comparison/metrics.py).
findings.userImpact: A threshold change — the single most common way a decision system silently changes its answers — is caught in the canonical pipeline and essentially nowhere else. `MATCH_QUARANTINE_THRESHOLD` is the most alarming: it decides whether a fuzzy player match is accepted into the board or quarantined, and no test mentions it.
