findings.area: Testing audit — what is actually pinned vs. test theatre (378 Python test files under tests/, 97 frontend test files under frontend/__tests__/), commit 9c5d972
findings.title: `pytest -x` means a green run proves less than it appears to, and a conflicted PR gets zero checks
findings.rootCause: Both the PR gate and the deploy gate use `-x` (stop on first failure); GitHub cannot schedule a `pull_request` run for a PR whose merge ref will not build.
findings.evidence: pr-validation.yml:161 and deploy.yml:127 both run `python -m pytest tests/ -x -q --tb=short -m "not livedata"`. pr-validation.yml:24-40 documents the second half in its own words: 'When the PR has merge conflicts that ref cannot be created, so the run is never scheduled — the PR sits with NO checks at all, which on the merge page reads identically to checks having passed. Observed on #625 (2026-07-29) ... The mitigation is branch protection, not this file.'
findings.userImpact: `-x` is only a reporting cost (a green run still means everything passed), but it means one flaky failure hides every subsequent failure from the log, which slows exactly the triage that matters. The zero-checks case is the real one and is Not Verifiable from Repository — whether a ruleset requiring the `Validate PR` check exists is a GitHub setting, not a file. Without it, an ungated PR is indistinguishable from a passing one.

findings.area: Constant and configuration audit — every hardcoded number and config file that changes a user-facing decision (commit 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligen
findings.title: The /rankings methodology panel shows users a value formula whose constants exist nowhere in the codebase
findings.rootCause: The methodology list is a hand-written JSX literal that was never updated when the curve constants moved. It quotes midpoint 45 and slope 1.10; the live rank-form constants are 65.4 / 0.910 and the live board is actually built by the percentile-form curve (c=0.11, s=1.11), a different functional form entirely.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/board-sections.jsx:34 — `value = max(1, min(9999, round(1 + 9998 / (1 + ((rank-1)/45)^1.10))))`. Rendered at app/rankings/page.jsx:1311 via `<MethodologySection />`. The live constants are src/canonical/player_valuation.py:82-83 — `HILL_MIDPOINT: float = 65.4` / `HILL_SLOPE: float = 0.910` — and :121-122 `HILL_PERCENTILE_C: float = 0.1100` / `HILL_PERCENTILE_S: float = 1.110`. I grepped the whole repo for a 45 midpoint: the only hits are INTEREST_HALF_LIFE_DAYS = 45.0 and unrelated data.
findings.userImpact: I reproduced both curves numerically. Displayed vs live rank-form value: rank 25 → 6663 vs 7134 (−471); rank 50 → 4766 vs 5653 (−887); rank 100 → 2959 vs 4068 (−1109); rank 200 → 1632 vs 2665 (−1033); rank 800 → 406 vs 931 (−525). A user who checks the published formula against a displayed value will find it disagrees by up to ~1100 points on the 1–9999 scale, and will not be able to tell whether the formula or the board is wrong. The same panel (line 31) also states the confidence rule as "spread ≤ 30 / ≤ 80", which is the retired ordinal rule.

findings.area: Constant and configuration audit — every hardcoded number and config file that changes a user-facing decision (commit 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligen
findings.title: The contract's own methodology.confidenceBuckets block describes a rule the pipeline stopped using
findings.rootCause: The confidence bucket implementation was migrated to a percentile-spread basis but the served methodology block still describes the legacy absolute-ordinal rule. The only test that touches it asserts the key exists, never its content.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:8857-8859 — `"high": "2+ sources, sourceRankSpread <= 30", "medium": "2+ sources, sourceRankSpread <= 80", "low": "single source or sourceRankSpread > 80"`. The live branch is :1896-1900 — `if percentile_spread is not None: if percentile_spread <= _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_HIGH` (0.08) … `<= _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_MEDIUM` (0.20). The 30/80 pair at :113-117 is labelled in code as a "Legacy absolute-ordinal fallback for callers that don't pass a percentile spread". Guard: tests/api/test_trust_confidence.py:450 only does `self.assertIn("confidenceBuckets", meth)`.
findings.userImpact: Any consumer — the UI methodology panel, an API client, a future maintainer — reading the served contract learns the wrong rule. The two rules are not equivalent: an ordinal spread of 25 on a 280-row source is a 0.089 percentile spread (medium), while the same 25 on a 500-row source is 0.050 (high). The documented rule and the live rule can disagree about the same row.

findings.area: Constant and configuration audit — every hardcoded number and config file that changes a user-facing decision (commit 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligen
findings.title: frontend/lib/thresholds.js claims to mirror backend confidence thresholds "exactly" and mirrors the retired ones
findings.rootCause: Same migration as above, from the other side. The frontend copied the ordinal constants and a sync note; the backend then moved its live path to percentiles and the frontend was never revisited.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/thresholds.js:15 — "These mirror the backend confidence bucket thresholds exactly"; :8 — "Python: _CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH (30), _CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_MEDIUM (80)"; :21,:24 declare 30 and 80. They ARE used for a decision: frontend/lib/edge-helpers.js:88 gates the "Consensus asset" signal on `(spread == null || spread <= CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH)`.
findings.userImpact: The "Consensus asset" chip on /rankings is gated on an ordinal spread threshold that the backend no longer uses for confidence, while the same chip also requires `row.confidenceBucket === "high"` which IS percentile-derived. The chip therefore applies two different definitions of the same concept simultaneously — a row can be backend-high-confidence and still lose the chip on the stale ordinal gate. Because deeper sources have larger ordinal spreads for identical relative agreement, this suppresses the chip preferentially on players covered by deep boards.

findings.title: The Monte Carlo trade simulator's uncertainty is a hardcoded ±15% for every asset, because the real band producer has no caller
findings.rootCause: monte_carlo.py was written to consume per-player p10/p50/p90 bands from Phase 4 confidence intervals. That producer was never wired: stamp_bands_on_players has no caller, rank_history_band has no caller, and the value_confidence_intervals flag is False. The `or {}` fallback silently became the model.
findings.evidence: src/trade/monte_carlo.py:372-380 — `# Fallback: synthesize a 15% band around the canonical value.` … `p10=_shifted(cv * 0.85), p50=_shifted(cv), p90=_shifted(cv * 1.15)`. The frontend duplicates it at frontend/components/ui/MonteCarloButton.jsx:55-57 — `p10 = v * 0.85; p50 = v; p90 = v * 1.15;`. The producer's status is recorded in the repo itself: src/api/feature_flags.py:57-63 — "the badge is exported from the ui barrel and imported by no page, ``stamp_bands_on_players`` has no caller, and ``rank_history_band`` has no caller either", `"value_confidence_intervals": False`. I grepped for any other producer of `valueBand`: there is none.
findings.userImpact: Rendered on /trade (TradeMeter.jsx:107) and /waivers (ManualAddDrop.jsx:459) as a win probability. Because every asset gets the same relative width, the simulation carries zero per-player uncertainty information — a rock-solid consensus QB1 and a wildly-disputed rookie are modelled as equally uncertain. The output reduces to a deterministic function of the two side totals and the correlation ladder, dressed as a 50,000-draw simulation. The disclaimer string says it samples "consensus-band samples", which is precisely what it is not doing.

findings.area: Constant and configuration audit — every hardcoded number and config file that changes a user-facing decision (commit 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligen
findings.title: marketConfidence is structurally capped at 0.594 by a stale divisor and is still surfaced as a confidence number
findings.rootCause: `site_score = site_count / 8.0` was sized when ~10 scraper SITES were enabled. Today exactly three numeric dash keys exist (ktc, ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc), so site_count ∈ {1,2,3} and site_score ≤ 0.375, capping the weighted result at 0.375·0.65 + 1.00·0.35 = 0.59375.
findings.evidence: Dynasty Scraper.py:6031 — `site_score = _clampf(float(site_count) / 8.0, 0.20, 1.00)`; :6033 — `conf = _clampf((site_score * 0.65) + (cv_score * 0.35), 0.20, 1.00)`. I measured the live export (exports/latest/dynasty_data.js): n=839, min 0.3447, max 0.5938, median 0.4897 — the observed maximum equals the theoretical cap to four decimals. The diagnosis is already written down at src/api/terminal.py:910-928, where it was used to justify retiring the low_conf_unstable rule.
findings.userImpact: The field flows to the contract as `marketConfidence` (data_contract.py:8312) and to frontend rows as `confidence` (dynasty-data.js:1023, :1201), where PlayerPopup.jsx:164 renders `confidence {Math.round(ros.confidence * 100)}%` for the ROS variant. A metric labelled confidence that can never exceed 59% and whose entire live range is 0.34–0.59 is a broken gauge: it cannot distinguish a well-covered player from a thin one, because site_count barely varies. It also carries a `.get("marketConfidence", 0.5)` default at Dynasty Scraper.py:6197 which, at a live median of 0.4897, would be completely indistinguishable from a real reading if it were ever reachable.

findings.title: The scraper composite weights one vendor's two boards at 70% of the blend, and 11 of its 13 declared weights are inert
findings.rootCause: SITE_WEIGHTS predates the current source set. Its keys are old scraper dash keys; most no longer appear in the payload, so `SITE_WEIGHTS.get(dash_key, 1.0)` silently returns 1.0. The two keys that do appear are `ktc` (weight 1.3) and `ktcSfTep` (no entry → 1.0) — the same vendor's standard and TE++ boards, which are near-identical row by row.
findings.evidence: Dynasty Scraper.py:5609-5622 declares 13 weights; :6102 — `wNorms.append((norm, SITE_WEIGHTS.get(dash_key, 1.0)))`. I enumerated every numeric dash key across all 1074 players in exports/latest/dynasty_data.js: exactly {ktc: 590, ktcSfTep: 464, idpTradeCalc: 898}. Eleven declared keys (dlfSf, dlfIdp, dlfRsf, dlfRidp, draftSharks, dynastyDaddy, dynastyNerds, fantasyCalc, fantasyPros, fantasyProsIdp, yahoo) never appear. On a 3-source player (A.J. Brown: ktc 5008, ktcSfTep 5008, idpTradeCalc 4936, `_sites: 3`) the KTC family carries 2.3/3.3 = 69.7% of the composite.
findings.userImpact: The composite is `values.overall` / `values.finalAdjusted` on the contract (data_contract.py:8184-8194) and is the value the public-league trade grader reads (public_activity_valuation.py:68-78 chain), the finder's fallback branch reads (finder.py:451, :946), and the frontend falls back to for rows the canonical board leaves unranked (dynasty-data.js:951-955). Those surfaces are priced on a board where one vendor has 70% of the vote. CLAUDE.md's statement that blend weights are "all 1.0 by policy" is true of _RANKING_SOURCES and false here, so the policy claim does not cover the pipeline it needs to.

findings.title: Public-league trade grading prices an unpriceable asset at ~zero and still emits a confident grade
findings.rootCause: Assets the canonical pipeline cannot value return 0.0 from the valuation callable, are floored to 1.0, and then enter the alpha-weighted sum as 1^1.65 = 1. Only the case where EVERY side is zero is special-cased.
findings.evidence: src/public_league/activity.py:118 — `total += pow(max(val, 1.0), _GRADE_ALPHA)` with `_GRADE_ALPHA = 1.65` (:49); the zero guard at :123-129 fires only `if max_w <= 0`. The valuation callable returns 0.0 for anything unpriced: src/api/public_activity_valuation.py:78 — `return 0.0`.
findings.userImpact: A 1-for-1 trade where one side received a player the board does not price yields pct = (5000^1.65 − 1)/5000^1.65 × 100 ≈ 100, which lands in the top band: one manager is publicly labelled "Big win" and the other "Fleeced", on the public league activity feed, purely because a name failed to resolve. The comment at :110-117 shows the floor was added for consistency with the private page, which means both surfaces share the hole.

findings.area: Constant and configuration audit — every hardcoded number and config file that changes a user-facing decision (commit 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligen
findings.title: The league-adjusted board pivots on an undocumented 0.5 reference that is indistinguishable from a real measurement
findings.rootCause: `reference_lineup_scarcity` is a keyword default with no comment, no config entry, and no caller override. It is the origin of the entire structural-scarcity axis: positions above 0.5 are lifted, positions below are trimmed.
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/adjustment.py:215 — `reference_lineup_scarcity: float = 0.5,` and :247 — `delta = (value - reference_lineup_scarcity) * sensitivity`. I grepped the repo for any caller passing it: none — src/league_intel/ and src/api/ contain no other reference to the parameter name. `sensitivity: float = 0.20` (:216) is equally undocumented.
findings.userImpact: lineupScarcity is a 0–1 quantity, so 0.5 is a perfectly plausible measured reading. Nothing downstream — not the rationale string, not the explanation payload, not the audit trail — distinguishes "this position sits exactly at the reference" from "nobody ever chose a reference". The axis is the only live per-position input to a board the user can switch to on /rankings and which threads into trade suggestions, the finder, angles, waivers, the terminal and the simulator via valuation_mode. This is the one constant in the overlay that decides its direction, and it is the one with no justification. The surrounding module is otherwise meticulous — every EvidenceTier and every guardrail carries a paragraph — which makes the omission conspicuous rather than typical.

findings.area: Constant and configuration audit — every hardcoded number and config file that changes a user-facing decision (commit 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligen
findings.title: Team-impact verdict thresholds and normalizations decide Accept vs Decline with no stated rationale anywhere
findings.rootCause: The config file and its inline Python fallback were written together and neither carries a _comment. There is no measurement script, no backtest, and no doc reference for any of the seven weights or four verdict bands.
findings.evidence: config/trade/team_impact.json — `"fitNormalization": 4000, "equityNormalization": 2500, "compositeFitWeight": 0.55, "compositeEquityWeight": 0.45` and `"verdictThresholds": {"accept": 20, "leanAccept": 8, "leanDecline": -8, "decline": -20}`. Applied at src/trade/team_impact.py:433-439 — `fit_score = _clamp(100.0 * fit_raw / fit_norm, -100.0, 100.0)` … `composite = cw_fit * fit_score + cw_eq * equity_score`. Rendered at frontend/app/trade/trade-sections.jsx:312 — `const ti = simResult?.teamImpact;`. No test file for this module exists under tests/trade/.
findings.userImpact: The two normalization constants set the exchange rate between roster fit and trade equity, and because both terms saturate at ±100 they also decide which term can dominate. 4000 and 2500 mean a fit swing is worth 0.625× an equity swing of the same board-point size, before the 0.55/0.45 composite weights are even applied. This is the number that flips the verdict a user reads on the trade page, and nobody has written down why it is 4000 rather than 3000 or 6000. Separately, `int(a.get("value") or 0)` at :117, :148 and :219-232 means an unpriced asset contributes 0 to starter value and to the contend index, and the verdict still renders at full confidence.

But the stated derivation is now wrong by a factor of 1.5–2.2, which means the bands no longer sit where the comment says they sit relative to the board: the comment implies the S/D+ boundary at 6000 falls somewhere below rank 12, while on the live curve rank 12 is 8350 and 6000 sits near rank 43. findings.area: Constant and configuration audit — every hardcoded number and config file that changes a user-facing decision (commit 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligen
findings.title: The /draft rookie-pool fallback prefers the scraper composite over the canonical board while asserting they are the same field
findings.rootCause: A defensive fallback chain was written from an incorrect premise about which contract field carries the blended value, and put the composite ahead of rankDerivedValue.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:4241-4243 — "The raw contract stamps the blended value as ``values.overall`` and ``rankDerivedValue``" — then :4249-4255 orders the chain `p?.values?.overall, p?.rankDerivedValue, p?.values?.displayValue, p?.values?.finalAdjusted, p?.values?.full`. But values.overall is `_finalAdjusted` (src/api/data_contract.py:8184-8194), the scraper composite, and src/trade/finder.py:53-58 records the measured offset between the two scales: `BOARD_TO_COMPOSITE_K = 0.875` = median(board/composite), regenerable with scripts/measure_engine_value_divergence.py.
findings.userImpact: Bounded, for two reasons I verified: the path only runs when the server-side rookie pool is unavailable (:4297), and the resulting values are immediately rescaled to the $1200 budget (:4386-4391), so the ~14% level offset washes out. What does not wash out is ORDERING — the composite and the board disagree per-player, not just in level, so the fallback rookie board can rank rookies differently from every other surface in the app. The comment also misinforms the next reader about what values.overall is.

findings.area: Documentation-versus-code forensic audit of decision-support outputs (riskittogetthebrisket @ 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligence-audit-wif47g)
findings.title: The shipped /api/data contract describes a weighting formula the blend does not apply — and contradicts itself two fields later
findings.rootCause: The 2026-07-29 audit corrected methodology.formula (the Hill expression) and added an honest coverageWeight block, but left methodology.description untouched. The description still asserts the depth-scaled weighting as live.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:8768-8774 ships: "blended across sources with a coverage-aware weighted mean: declared weight is scaled by min(1, depth / {min_depth}) so shallow lists contribute less than deep full-board sources". The code at :6988-6991 says the opposite in the same file: "the depth-based ``coverage_weight`` factor stays a stamped diagnostic (``sourceRankMeta.effectiveWeight``) and is NOT applied here", and :7246-7248 stamps it as "the depth-scaled coverage DIAGNOSTIC ... never applied to the blend". The SAME payload contradicts itself at :8834-8842: "DIAGNOSTIC ONLY: ... It is never applied to the blend". I confirmed on a live rebuild that methodology.description carries the false text verbatim.
findings.userImpact: Any consumer of the versioned contract — including a future maintainer reading the payload rather than the source — believes shallow rookie lists are down-weighted. They are not: all 21 sources vote at weight 1.0. Someone 'restoring' the documented behaviour would move 297 of 1094 rows and 221 ranks with zero accuracy evidence, which is precisely the failure docs/open-modeling-decisions.md §1 was written to prevent.

findings.area: Documentation-versus-code forensic audit of decision-support outputs (riskittogetthebrisket @ 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligence-audit-wif47g)
findings.title: The contract publishes the wrong confidence-bucket rule; it misclassifies a third of the board
findings.rootCause: _compute_confidence_bucket has two branches — a percentile branch and a legacy absolute-ordinal fallback. The live call always supplies percentile_spread, so the percentile branch always wins, but the published documentation describes the fallback.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:8856-8860 publishes {"high": "2+ sources, sourceRankSpread <= 30", "medium": "2+ sources, sourceRankSpread <= 80", "low": "single source or sourceRankSpread > 80"}. The live path is :7735-7739, which passes percentile_spread=percentile_spread, so :1896-1899 decides on _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_HIGH=0.08 / _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_MEDIUM=0.20 (:111-112) instead. Measured on a rebuild of exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json: of 712 ranked non-pick rows, the published rule gives a DIFFERENT bucket for 237 (33.3%) — 139 low->medium, 28 medium->low, 28 low->high, 19 high->medium, 14 high->low, 9 medium->high. Worked example: Alex Anzalone has sourceRankSpread 17 (published rule: 'high') but sourceRankPercentileSpread 0.4599, so the code returns 'low'.
findings.userImpact: confidenceBucket gates /edge eligibility (edge-columns.jsx:127, page.jsx:116, :227), the /rankings single-source-risk screen, and the ConfidenceValueScatter. A user or integrator reasoning about why a player is 'low confidence' from the contract's own published rule will be wrong for a third of the board, and will look at the wrong field (sourceRankSpread instead of sourceRankPercentileSpread).

findings.area: Documentation-versus-code forensic audit of decision-support outputs (riskittogetthebrisket @ 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligence-audit-wif47g)
findings.title: The Monte Carlo win probability is computed from a fabricated ±15% band, and the UI tells the user it came from real source disagreement
findings.rootCause: The simulator was designed to consume Phase 4 valueBand, but stamp_bands_on_players was never wired into the contract builder. The frontend's fallback branch — a hardcoded ±15% — is therefore the only branch ever taken, while the user-facing explainer still describes the intended design.
findings.evidence: src/canonical/confidence_intervals.py:224 stamp_bands_on_players has ZERO non-test callers (grep across src/, server.py, scripts/). Measured on a live rebuild: valueBand present on 0 of 1092 playersArray rows. frontend/components/ui/MonteCarloButton.jsx:43-54 therefore always takes the else branch: `p10 = v * 0.85; p50 = v; p90 = v * 1.15;`. The explainer at :231-240 tells the user: "For each player, our 6+ ranking sources don't fully agree on value — a player worth 8,500 by one source might be 7,900 by another. We sample 20,000 times from this disagreement range". src/trade/monte_carlo.py:8 repeats the claim ("each with a ``valueBand`` from Phase 4"). I reproduced the output: a 5000-vs-4500 one-for-one returns winProbA 0.7304; relabelling the 4500 asset as a single-source DL moves it only to 0.7153. Real dispersion on the live board is p10 0.061 / median 0.174 / p90 0.450 (hillValueSpread ÷ rankDerivedValue, 733 rows) — the constant 0.15 is ~2.5x too wide for the tightest decile and ~3x too narrow for the most-contested.
findings.userImpact: '73% chance Side A wins' is rendered on /trade (TradeMeter.jsx:107) and /waivers (ManualAddDrop.jsx:459) as a probabilistic verdict. It is a deterministic function of the value gap and roster shape. A one-source rookie IDP and a twelve-source consensus RB1 carry identical uncertainty. Separately, server.py:11197 states the backend `disclaimer` field is PART OF THE CONTRACT and 'the frontend MUST render the disclaimer somewhere visible' — the frontend never reads it and substitutes its own, stronger, false explanation.

findings.area: Documentation-versus-code forensic audit of decision-support outputs (riskittogetthebrisket @ 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligence-audit-wif47g)
findings.title: /api/draft-capital's non-default-league board is 53.7% invented numbers, indistinguishable from Hill-calibrated ones
findings.rootCause: _pick_value_from_contract falls through to a hardcoded per-round table whenever a pick name is absent from the contract. The 503 guard added in the 2026-07-29 pass only covers 'no contract at all', so a loaded contract that simply does not name next-season slot picks still produces a full board of fabricated values — and the $1200 renormalisation propagates the invention into the real half.
findings.evidence: src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:96-99: `flat = {1: 7000.0, 2: 4000.0, 3: 2000.0, 4: 1200.0, 5: 700.0, 6: 300.0}` returned with no flag. The loop at :174-181 builds picks for `(current_season, current_season + 1)`. Measured against a live rebuild: of the 96 (season, round, slot) tuples, 48 resolve from the contract and 48 fall through — the contract names 2026 slot picks but no 2027 slot picks. Raw totals: 2026 = 147,020, 2027 = 170,400, so the invented half is 53.7% of the pool. :196-200 then scales everything by 1200/317420, so the fabricated values set the denominator for the real ones. Concretely, every 2027 1st is priced at 7000 — above the real 2026 1.02 (6185). server.py:8143-8150 confirms the guard's scope: "SCOPE, DELIBERATELY NARROW. This fires only when there is NO contract". config/leagues/registry.json has two active leagues, so dynasty_new takes this path today.
findings.userImpact: On /draft for the second league, every team's draft-capital dollar figure is driven by a table that says all 2027 1sts are worth the same, and the response carries no field marking which values are real. CLAUDE.md's D-2 note states the invented-numbers case 'is fixed' and 'is the case the 503 covers' — a reader would conclude this is closed.

findings.area: Documentation-versus-code forensic audit of decision-support outputs (riskittogetthebrisket @ 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligence-audit-wif47g)
findings.title: docs/idp-ranking-model.md is materially false about how IDP values are produced — 0 of 740 rows match its published formula
findings.rootCause: The document is the standalone methodology reference for IDP valuation and has not been updated through the percentile-curve migration, the removal of the frontend ranker, or the coverage-weight decision.
findings.evidence: Three independent false claims. (1) :21 names `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js::computeUnifiedRanks` as the frontend fallback mirror — grep for computeUnifiedRanks across frontend/ returns NOTHING; CLAUDE.md records the ~280-line fallback was removed. (2) :105 publishes `value = max(1, min(9999, round(1 + 9998 / (1 + ((rank - 1) / 45) ^ 1.10))))` as the live conversion and :149/:171 claim `rankDerivedValue` is 'Hill-curve value at canonicalConsensusRank'. I tested this against 740 ranked rows on the live board: ZERO exact matches, median absolute error 819.5 on a 1-9999 scale, max 1212. The constants 45 / 1.10 are also the retired ones — the live rank-form pair is 65.4 / 0.910 (player_valuation.py:82-83) and the live board uses the percentile form, not the rank form, at all. (3) :113-129 documents `effective_weight = declared_weight * min(1, depth / 60)` as the blend weight, with the worked consequence 'a top-20 positional list contributes 20/60 ≈ 0.333 of its declared weight' — data_contract.py:6988-6991 states this is never applied.
findings.userImpact: A developer or reviewer reasoning about IDP valuation from the repository's own dedicated methodology document gets the wrong curve, the wrong constants, the wrong blend, and a frontend module that does not exist. This is the document someone would open specifically to check whether IDP numbers deserve trust.

findings.title: FAAB bid diverges between the Python endpoint and the JS client hint on 6.1% of the value range — larger than the register records
findings.rootCause: Byte-identical formulas, different rounding semantics: Python's round() is banker's, JS Math.round() is half-up. The 0.70 and 0.35 multipliers manufacture exact-half products across wide contiguous value bands, so the divergence is not the rare edge case the register implies.
findings.evidence: src/trade/waiver.py:92-94 — `aggressive = max(1, round(league_budget * aggressive_pct)); reasonable = max(1, round(aggressive * 0.70)); lowball = max(1, round(aggressive * 0.35))`. frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js:874-877 is the same expression with Math.round. I swept candidate values 100..9999 at budget 100 / top 9999: 600 of 9900 values diverge. Example: value 3800 gives Python (15, 10, 5) and JS (15, 11, 5) — a $10 vs $11 'reasonable' bid, 10% apart, on a 100-dollar budget. No parity test exists (grep for computeFaabHint under tests/ and frontend/__tests__/ finds only waiver-pool-builder.test.js). Registered as D4 with the description 'Off-by-one bids on exact halves', severity Medium, 'before new features? No'.
findings.userImpact: /waivers renders the client hint on every bestMoves row while the FaabRecommendation panel calls the Python endpoint for the selected pair. The same player can show two different recommended bids on one screen.

findings.area: Documentation-versus-code forensic audit of decision-support outputs (riskittogetthebrisket @ 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligence-audit-wif47g)
findings.title: CLAUDE.md's TE floor claim is contradicted by the pipeline's own ceiling clamp
findings.rootCause: The uplift curve is applied as min(convert(v), 9999.0). For the highest-valued TEs the converted contribution exceeds the scale ceiling and is truncated, so the realised multiplier falls below the curve's measured floor.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:7196-7204 wraps the conversion in `min(float(_convert_te_value(...)), 9999.0)`. config/weights/te_premium_curve.json sets floor 1.209206. CLAUDE.md step 5a states the uplift is "1.209 at the top of the board rising toward 2.05 down it". Measured on the live board: 5 of 552 converted contributions land below 1.2092 — Brock Bowers at 1.1017 across fantasyCalc, pfkDynasty and dynastyDaddySf, 1.168 on otcffbSf, and Trey McBride at 1.185 on pfkDynasty; every one has valueContribution exactly 9999.
findings.userImpact: Small (2 players), and the clamp is deliberate and well-reasoned in code ('the premium must reposition TEs within the scale, not break it'). But it means the elite TEs — the ones a TE-premium correction most affects in trade value — receive systematically less uplift than the documentation states, and the direction is the opposite of what a reader would assume.

findings.title: Three unrelated quantities ship to users under the single word 'confidence'
findings.rootCause: Independent subsystems each named their own quality metric 'confidence' with no shared vocabulary or namespacing.
findings.evidence: (1) src/api/data_contract.py:1896-1899 — board confidenceBucket, decided on percentile spread with 2+ sources. (2) src/trade/suggestions.py:811-818 — `_confidence_from_sources`: >=6 sources 'high', >=3 'medium', else 'low'; a raw count with no agreement term, used at :1067 and :1128 to label trade suggestions and to feed a +2/+1/0 rank_score bonus. (3) src/ros/aggregate.py:243-249 — a 0.45/0.35/0.20 composite of count, agreement and freshness. Plus the retired-but-still-stamped `marketConfidence`, structurally capped at 0.59375. A player can be 'low' confidence on the board (wide percentile spread) and 'high' confidence in a trade suggestion (6+ sources) simultaneously.
findings.userImpact: On /trade a suggestion carries a confidence label produced by a rule that ignores whether the sources agree; the /rankings badge for the same player is produced by a rule that is entirely about agreement. Nothing on either surface distinguishes them.

findings.area: Core live valuation pipeline — `src/api/data_contract.py::_compute_unified_rankings` and everything it calls (rank→percentile→Hill, value-direct voting, scope r
findings.title: The three routed Hill curves are on different scales from the market values they are averaged with — the IDP master pays ~48% of the IDP market at the same rank
findings.evidence:
Measured on a contract rebuilt from the live 2026-08-04 payload. For each row I compared a source's vote at its own effective rank against the retail market value at that same rank:

  IDP master (c=0.083, s=1.110) vs idpTradeCalc raw, n=293:   p10 0.36  median 0.48  p90 0.76
  OFFENSE master (c=0.110, s=1.110) vs ktcSfTep raw, n=391:   p10 0.68  median 0.76  p90 1.00
  GLOBAL master (c=0.112, s=0.725) vs idpTradeCalc raw, n=293: p10 0.88  median 1.34  p90 2.17

The IDP-only sources are ladder-translated into IDPTC's combined-rank space (sharedMarketTranslated: true, method 'exact', on 100% of dlfIdp/idpShow/fantasyProsIdp rows), so these are like-for-like. Dallas Turner, five sources all at the SAME combined rank 117:
  idpTradeCalc  valueContribution 4164  (value_direct, src/api/data_contract.py:7131)
  idpShow       valueContribution 2417  (rank_hill, IDP master)
  dlfIdp 1899   fantasyProsIdp 673   draftSharksIdp 1865 (GLOBAL master)

Root cause is in the fit, not the blend. scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:366-372 fits the IDP master on `_load_idptc_idp_values()` — IDPTC's IDP-ONLY slice — and `_percentile_pairs` (:201-207) renormalizes so the top IDP = 9999 with p = i/(n−1) over that slice (n=370 live, top IDP raw = 6444). At runtime the same curve is evaluated at p = (combined_pool_rank − 1)/499 (src/api/data_contract.py:7108-7113) and its output is averaged against combined-pool values where 9999 means the top OFFENSE player. Two coordinate changes, neither compensated.
findings.userImpact: Every IDP value on the board is produced by averaging numbers that mean different things. The pipeline's own designated IDP anchor is treated as an outlier and discarded on 28% of IDP rows, the blend lands systematically low, and a post-hoc clamp then drags 44% of IDP rows back to the retail number — so the multi-source IDP consensus the product advertises does not survive to the output. Any IDP trade valuation, waiver bid or package sum built on these numbers is arithmetic over incommensurable units.

findings.area: Core live valuation pipeline — `src/api/data_contract.py::_compute_unified_rankings` and everything it calls (rank→percentile→Hill, value-direct voting, scope r
findings.title: The Hampel filter ejects the designated IDP anchor on 28% of IDP rows
findings.evidence:
src/api/data_contract.py:7293-7300 runs `_hampel_filter_per_player` over the mixed-scale value list before aggregation. Per-source drop rates on the live board, restricted to assetClass 'idp':

  idpTradeCalc    82/293 = 28.0%   ← the registry's is_backbone:True, is_cross_market:True IDP anchor
  draftSharksIdp  69/274 = 25.2%   ← the other cross-market anchor

  dlfIdp           1/137 =  0.7%

findings.title: The corridor clamp's hard 0.15 cap binds on 100% of clamps, making the IDP board IDPTradeCalc ±15% by construction

findings.title: The future-year pick discount is applied on top of vendor values that already price the year, in the opposite direction
findings.evidence:
Both pick markets price a 2027 Early 1st ABOVE a 2026 Early 1st:
  CSVs/site_raw/ktcSfTep.csv:     2026 Early 1st 5595,  2027 Early 1st 7061,  2028 Early 1st 5122
  CSVs/site_raw/idpTradeCalc.csv: 2026 Early 1st 5554,  2027 Early 1st 7052,  2028 Early 1st 5034
The pipeline treats 2026 as offset 0 (factor 1.00) and multiplies 0.82 / 0.66 / 0.53 onto later years (src/api/data_contract.py:6027, config/weights/pick_year_discount.json). Live result:
  2027 Early 1st: blended anchor 7056 → published 5786  (−18% vs both markets)
  2028 Early 1st: blended anchor 5078 → published 3351  (−34%)
  2029 Early 1st: cloned 2028 values 5034 → published 2668 (−47%, and no vendor prices 2029 at all)
The stated justification is contradicted by the current data. The code comment at src/api/data_contract.py:3993-3995 asserts 'There is no real future-year discount in the source data — KTC and IDPTC price 2027/2028 picks only marginally below 2026'; the live CSVs show 2027 priced 26% ABOVE 2026.
Compounding this, the two baseline-year resolvers DISAGREE on this build: `_derive_current_draft_year_from_names` returns 2026 (72 '2026 Pick R.SS' rows still present) while the date-derived fallback returns 2027 (today 2026-08-04 is past the May 15 rollover, src/api/data_contract.py:4265-4270). The data-derived value wins, and the market's own relative pricing of 2027 over 2026 is consistent with the date-derived answer being correct.
No backtest, fit or provenance for 0.82/0.66/0.53 exists anywhere in config/, reports/ or docs/.
findings.userImpact: Forward draft capital is systematically under-priced against every source that prices it — 18% on 2027 firsts, 34% on 2028. Any trade in which the user sends future picks is scored as a win by the calculator when the market says otherwise. If the baseline year is also off by one, the error compounds.

findings.title: Every constant in the blend was selected against a stability metric; no accuracy validation of the live board exists
findings.evidence: reports/percentile_reference_n_backtest_full.md, reports/alpha_lambda_joint_backtest_full.md, reports/mad_lambda_backtest_full.md and reports/soft_fallback_backtest_full.md all optimize 'value-weighted rank change' — day-to-day board churn. The α report states the problem outright: 'this metric rewards stability. The stability optimum drifts toward α=0 and λ=0 — use the anchor source alone, ignore the 15 other sources. That's product-bad.' α=0.10 was a product judgement, not a measurement. The percentile-N report recommends 400; the code ships 500 (src/api/data_contract.py:4933). The corridor band 0.15, the single-source retention 0.30, Hampel K=2.75 and its 1000-point floor, the TE-native 1.10, and the pick discounts 0.82/0.66/0.53 have no backtest at all in-repo. The only accuracy-style backtest present — docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md — covers the league-adjusted overlay, not this pipeline.
findings.userImpact: There is no evidence in the repository that any number this pipeline produces is more accurate than reading IDPTradeCalc and KeepTradeCut directly. A stability metric always prefers whatever ignores the most information, which is why every tuned constant has drifted toward the degenerate solution and why the corridor clamp — which reduces the IDP board to one vendor ±15% — reads as an improvement rather than as an alarm.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md's pipeline description is mechanically accurate but omits every place a stage is inert or dominant
findings.evidence:
I checked each numbered claim in CLAUDE.md's 'Live Value Pipeline' against the code and the live payload. CONFIRMED CORRECT: the 500 reference and its tail clamp; value-direct limited to exactly {ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc}; scope routing including ROOKIE routed=False; the TE double-count guard (0 ktcSfTep TE rows carry a tep stamp across 83 TE rows); α=0.10 on IDP and picks only with offense flat; the count-aware n=1/2/3-4/≥5 boundaries; λ=0 retired (madPenaltyApplied null on 1,092/1,092 rows); softFallbackCount diagnostic-only; the 30% single-source haircut; corridor clamp IDP-only (128/128); two-way boost running after the clamp; discount at Phase 3a before the sort and tethering at Phase 5.2b after it; registry weights all 1.0; default_weights.json unread.
GAPS, each material to reading a number off the board:
  1. Step 10 states the 0.15 cap without saying it binds on 100% of clamps, so the documented 'P90 drift band per confidence bucket' is inert in production.
  2. Step 6 says picks use anchor + α-shrinkage; the subgroup is empty on 144/144 live pick rows, so α is never applied to a pick — the stage is mean(KTC, IDPTC).
  3. Step 5a says the TE uplift runs '1.209 at the top of the board rising toward 2.05 down it'; the live observed range is 1.1017 to 1.6367, the low end produced by the 9999 ceiling clamp and 2.05 never reached.
  4. Nothing anywhere records that the three routed curves sit on different scales from the market values they are blended with (F-1).
  5. src/api/data_contract.py:3993-3995 asserts KTC and IDPTC 'price 2027/2028 picks only marginally below 2026'; both CSVs today price 2027 26% ABOVE 2026.
findings.userImpact: A reader following CLAUDE.md would believe the IDP board is a five-source consensus with a light outlier guard. It is IDPTradeCalc ±15%, with three of the five sources voting on a half-scale curve.

findings.title: /api/movers emits absolute per-source ranks under a field the docstring calls a per-source delta, and the "window" is not honored per player

findings.title: Unresolvable assets are silently valued at zero in public trade grading, and the grade thresholds are percentages of an alpha-exponentiated scale, not of value
findings.evidence: src/api/public_activity_valuation.py:172 `return by_name.get(name.lower(), 0.0)` and :162 `return 0.0` when pick probes miss; no unresolved list is returned. src/public_league/activity.py:117 floors each asset at 1 before `pow(max(val,1.0), 1.65)` (:47), so an unpriced asset contributes 1 against a real player's ~2,000,000. The bridge drops every pickGenericSuppressed row (:126) and every row without a positive values bundle; 352 of 1092 live rows are unranked. Threshold semantics: `pct = ((max_w - min_w)/max_w)*100` on exponentiated totals — 5000 vs 4000 (a 20% value gap) gives 1 - 0.8^1.65 = 31.0% -> 'Big win' (>= 25); the 3% 'Fair' band corresponds to a ~1.8% raw gap.
findings.userImpact: A public /league trade where one side received an unpriced player is graded as receiving nothing — an F/'Fleeced' badge on a possibly fair trade. Grades are also harsher than the labeled percentages imply, and nothing on the payload distinguishes a fully-priced grade from a partial one.

Observed directly: invoking build_api_data_contract once on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json during this read-only audit CREATED data/snapshots/ranks_last.json (14,673 bytes) where no data/snapshots directory had existed. findings.area: Canonical Hill-curve valuation primitives + Model Registry (src/canonical/ 7 files, src/model_registry/ 6 files, scripts/auto_refit_hill_curves.py, scripts/fit_
findings.title: The 'held-out' boards are live inputs to the blend the curve serves — the benchmark is not independent of the system it grades
findings.evidence: src/model_registry/holdout.py:74-79 defines the holdout set as FantasyCalc (CSVs/site_raw/fantasyCalc.csv), OTCFFB (otcffbSf.csv), PFKDynasty (pfkDynasty.csv) and FantasyNavigator (fantasyNavigatorSf.csv). All four are registered LIVE BLEND SOURCES: src/api/data_contract.py:1302 ("key": "fantasyCalc"), :1327 ("key": "otcffbSf"), :1361 ("key": "fantasyNavigatorSf"), :1388 ("key": "pfkDynasty"). I enumerated runtime routing from _RANKING_SOURCES + _curve_for_source (data_contract.py:6401-6407): all four route to the OFFENSE master — the exact pair the holdout scores. Player overlap between the six training boards' top-400 and each holdout board's top-400, measured on today's CSVs: FantasyCalc 395/399 (99.0%), OTCFFB 393/398 (98.7%), PFKDynasty 399/400 (99.8%), FantasyNavigator 362/400 (90.5%). FantasyNavigator is worse than 'another market': data_contract.py:548-552 records that its values are KTC-DERIVED (rows carry ktc_player_id), so a transform of a training board is being used as a holdout. The module concedes half the problem (holdout.py:33-40, 'Every holdout source is another consensus market, correlated with the training sources by construction') but never says they are blend inputs; CLAUDE.md drops even that caveat, describing the gate as 'dynasty boards the fit never reads'.
findings.userImpact: Every claim of the form 'the new curve generalizes better' means only 'the curve reproduces the published value shape of four boards whose ranks we already vote into our own board'. It is a self-consistency measurement presented as validation. A user reading /rankings has no way to know the constants behind every displayed value were selected by a benchmark built from the pipeline's own inputs.

findings.area: Canonical Hill-curve valuation primitives + Model Registry (src/canonical/ 7 files, src/model_registry/ 6 files, scripts/auto_refit_hill_curves.py, scripts/fit_
findings.title: The gate rewards precisely the property the pipeline rejected for those same four boards
findings.evidence: All four holdout boards were moved OFF the value-direct path because their published value curves decay faster than our consensus and the Hampel filter discarded most of their votes: data_contract.py:364-381 (fantasyCalc, 'crowd values decay much *faster* down the board than the KTC-anchored Hill consensus', 54.9%→58% drop rate), :395-406 (otcffbSf, 'decay even faster', 55.6%→86%), :548-556 (fantasyNavigatorSf, 'exactly the profile that put fantasyCalc/otcffbSf outside the Hampel window'), :569-580 (pfkDynasty, value scale 'hand-shaped and unvalidated against our consensus decay'). None appears in _VALUE_BASED_SOURCES (data_contract.py:5110-5117 = {ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc} only). The holdout criterion is squared error against exactly those discarded value curves, so minimising it pulls the OFFENSE master toward the decay shape the blend deliberately refuses. I searched the criterion surface (c ∈ [0.060,0.200] × s ∈ [0.60,2.00]): its optimum on today's data is c=0.071, s=1.20 at criterion 480.02 — 319 points better than the champion's 799.48. Under that curve the board deflates by 6.2% at rank 12, 13.5% at 24, 24.0% at 50, 34.0% at 100, 42.0% at 200 and 49.5% at 500. The optimum also makes the one hand-maintained human board WORSE (PFKDynasty 242.3→800.5) while improving the three crowd boards (FantasyCalc 776.8→305.3, FantasyNavigator 1148.5→487.5, OTCFFB 1030.2→326.7) — the unweighted 4-source mean at holdout.py:274 is dominated by the crowd curves. The champion trajectory has moved monotonically toward that optimum: c 0.118 (v1) → 0.110 (v2) → 0.108 (today's fit).
findings.userImpact: The only automated quality signal on the most load-bearing constants in the repo has a systematic preferred direction that contradicts a documented, measured design decision. Followed to its optimum it would cut mid- and deep-board values by a third to a half, silently repricing every trade evaluation, every FAAB bid and every tier boundary.

findings.area: Canonical Hill-curve valuation primitives + Model Registry (src/canonical/ 7 files, src/model_registry/ 6 files, scripts/auto_refit_hill_curves.py, scripts/fit_
findings.title: Six of eight production constants ship on the back of a gate that measures two of them
findings.evidence: src/model_registry/hill_masters.py:206-209: VALIDATED_PARAMS = ('HILL_PERCENTILE_C', 'HILL_PERCENTILE_S'), commented 'only these two of the eight have a genuine out-of-sample check today'. auto_refit_hill_curves.py:255-256 scores only that pair and :265 decides on it. But the recorded challenger carries all eight (:281-291, params=fitted), scripts/model_registry.py:208 promotes the whole ModelVersion, and :244 write_committed_constants(champ.params) writes all eight (hill_masters.py:233-244 iterates CONSTANT_NAMES and raises if any is missing). Meanwhile the drift check deciding whether the gate runs takes the MAX over all four scopes (auto_refit_hill_curves.py:242). I ran the fit on today's CSVs and computed the driver's own drift metric: GLOBAL 0.00, OFFENSE 34.34, IDP 326.57, ROOKIE 275.52. So today the gate opens on a 326-point IDP move and is adjudicated by a 22.4-point OFFENSE improvement. Concretely, today's IDP challenger (c=0.0850, s=0.935) differs from the committed pair (0.0830, 1.110) by −3.5% at rank ~6, +13.3% at ~101, +21.4% at ~151, +33.6% at ~250, +42.6% at ~350 and +52.8% at rank 500.

findings.area: Canonical Hill-curve valuation primitives + Model Registry (src/canonical/ 7 files, src/model_registry/ 6 files, scripts/auto_refit_hill_curves.py, scripts/fit_
findings.title: `model_registry.py validate` performs the unpaired cross-snapshot comparison the design explicitly forbids
findings.evidence: scripts/model_registry.py:190-196 reads BOTH criteria out of the registry file — champ_crit = (champ.holdout or {}).get('criterion'); chal_crit = (challenger.holdout or {}).get('criterion') — then calls decide_promotion. Neither is re-scored. src/model_registry/promotion.py:7-29 states the rule this breaks: 'A rule that compared this week's challenger to last week's champion SCORE would be reading five days of market drift as model quality ... the comparison is always made on ONE snapshot with both curves scored against it.' The registry records having been bitten by exactly this — hill_scope_masters.json:75: 'holdout re-scored 2026-07-29 against that day's boards (849.8 -> 819.7). The prior figure was measured 2026-07-26 and was NOT comparable to challenger v2's 2026-07-28 score: promotion.py requires a PAIRED comparison because the criterion's absolute level drifts ~68 points week to week.' And this is the path the automation hands to humans: auto_refit_hill_curves.py:313-318 prints 'python3 scripts/model_registry.py validate {target}' as step 1 of the promotion recipe. Measured today: the champion's stored criterion is 787.8416 but re-scoring the identical (0.1100, 1.110) on today's CSVs gives 799.4823 — 11.6 points, 46% of the 25-point margin, in 7 days, from data movement alone. Five of six training fingerprints have changed since v2 was fitted.
findings.userImpact: A challenger can clear the promotion margin on market drift rather than model quality, and the human-facing command is the one that permits it. The auto-driver's comparison is correct (it re-scores both at :255-256), so the safe path and the documented path disagree — the worst possible arrangement, because the documented one is the one a human will follow at 2am.

findings.title: The IDP master is fit on sources that never use it and applied to sources it was never fit on — the overlap is zero

findings.title: The OFFENSE master is fit on value columns that the live blend discards
findings.evidence: Training set (holdout.py:58-65, mirroring fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:59-72): KTC(ktc.csv), DynastyDaddy, DynastyNerds, YahooBoone, Fitzmaurice, DraftSharks(draftSharksSf.csv). findings.title: Tier thresholds are hand-set priors with no fitter that can run, and the fitter would not fit them to data anyway

findings.title: Rank-form reconstruction constants are fit to the pipeline's own output and scored on the same rows — the quoted RMSEs are in-sample
findings.evidence: src/canonical/player_valuation.py:71-72: 'Fit by scripts/backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py, per scope, against rankDerivedValue on the served board.' The comparison table at :339-345 reports legacy_scope 83.8 overall against 'best-fit per scope 83.4' and concludes at :353 that 'The re-tuned pair now sits ON the achievable floor'. Both arms are computed on the same 740 rows of the same board — scripts/backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py:38-44 lists candidate 6 as 'a rank-form curve fit to THIS board, reported as the achievable floor'. There is no train/test split and no temporal holdout. To the script's credit it says plainly (:26-33) that this is 'a CONSISTENCY test, not a predictive-accuracy test'.

findings.title: The ROOKIE master silently loses three of its five intended training slices, and would ingest synthetic rank encodings if it found them
findings.evidence: scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:387-406 intends to fit KTC, IDPTC, Boone, Fitzmaurice and DraftSharks rookie slices; _load_rookie_values (:169-198) reads them from the snapshot's `_canonicalSiteValues` dict. findings.title: src/model_registry/__init__.py still describes the removed autonomous-commit behaviour as current

findings.area: Canonical Hill-curve valuation primitives + Model Registry (src/canonical/ 7 files, src/model_registry/ 6 files, scripts/auto_refit_hill_curves.py, scripts/fit_
findings.title: No temporal validation exists anywhere in the calibration path
findings.evidence: Every measurement in this subsystem is computed on one day's scrape. The fit reads CSVs/site_raw/*.csv (fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:56-83) and the gate reads CSVs/site_raw/*.csv (holdout.py:74-79) — the same directory, refreshed by the same job, on the same run. auto_refit_hill_curves.py:255-256 scores champion and challenger against that single snapshot, which is correct for pairing but means there is no out-of-time arm at all. The only forward-looking check in the audited set is board_holdout.py, and it disclaims being one (:15-30): 'this is NOT a forecast test — it cannot tell you whether either board predicts the future ... would need board snapshots taken before a season that this repo does not keep.' The registry's provenance fingerprints prove the data moves (5 of 6 training inputs changed in 7 days) but nothing scores across that movement.
findings.userImpact: Nothing in the registry can distinguish 'this curve describes dynasty markets' from 'this curve described dynasty markets on 2026-07-28'. The 68-point week-to-week criterion drift cited in promotion.py:9-13 is the size of that unmeasured axis, against a 25-point promotion margin.

findings.area: Trade engines: src/trade/ (15 modules, ~8,200 LOC) + src/api/trade_simulator.py + routes /api/trade/{suggestions,finder,simulate,simulate-mc,import-ktc,export-k
findings.title: The trade finder receives no position data on the live path, so its per-market gate is inert and it is still offense-only — the exact regression WS-J F-3 claims to have fixed
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:477 `pos = _norm_pos(pdata.get("position", ""))`, fed from server.py:5947 `players = latest_contract_data.get("players")`. I rebuilt the live contract (build_api_data_contract on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json) and measured: `positions in contract players: [(None, 1092)]` — the legacy players dict carries no `position` key at all. Consequences measured on the real pool: `pool from CONTRACT players: 150 Counter({'ktcSfTep': 132, 'ktc': 18})`, `idp in pool 0`, `positions in pool [('', 125), ('PICK', 25)]`. find_trades metadata on the live payload: `"marketCoverage": {"ktcSfTep": 132, "ktc": 18, "idpTradeCalc": 0}`. Because pos is always "", finder.py:474 always selects OFFENSE_MARKET_KEYS, every defender scores market_value=None, and the top-N gate drops them before scoring — precisely the behaviour the constant's own comment at finder.py:110-131 says was fixed.

findings.area: Trade engines: src/trade/ (15 modules, ~8,200 LOC) + src/api/trade_simulator.py + routes /api/trade/{suggestions,finder,simulate,simulate-mc,import-ktc,export-k
findings.title: The finder's explicit IDP-blindness warning cannot fire, because it reads position from the same empty field
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:992-1004: `league_has_idp = any(_norm_pos(str((p or {}).get("position", ""))) in IDP_POSITIONS for p in players.values() ...)` followed by `if league_has_idp and idp_priced == 0: warnings.append("No IDP asset carries an IDPTradeCalc value ...")`. findings.area: Trade engines: src/trade/ (15 modules, ~8,200 LOC) + src/api/trade_simulator.py + routes /api/trade/{suggestions,finder,simulate,simulate-mc,import-ktc,export-k
findings.title: The finder applies KTC's package Value Adjustment to the market side only, never to the board side — manufacturing arbitrage out of a scale asymmetry
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder_value_adjustment.py:44 `adjusted[index] = replace(adjusted[index], market_value=value + adjustment)` — only `market_value` is replaced; `model_value` is untouched, and finder.py:641-643 sums `_mv(a)` (the board value) raw. Live top result, verified end-to-end: give Josh Allen (board 9,993 / KTC 9,987), receive Joe Burrow + Patrick Mahomes (board 8,428 + 7,488 = 15,916 / KTC 7,395 + 6,307 = 13,702). rawGiveKtcTotal 9,987 → giveKtcTotal 13,850 after marketValueAdjustment +3,863; opponentKtcAppeal +0.011; boardDelta +5,923. Applying the SAME algorithm to the board values gives +1,820, which would cut boardDelta from 5,923 to 4,103. Across all 12 teams: 441 of 449 returned trades (98.2%) carried marketValueAdjustmentApplied.
findings.userImpact: The headline recommendation is "give Josh Allen, get Burrow AND Mahomes — you gain 5,923 board value and the opponent gains 1% on KTC." No manager accepts that. The engine's core comparison is between a consolidation-adjusted market total and an unadjusted board total, so the "gap" it reports is partly just the adjustment.

findings.area: Trade engines: src/trade/ (15 modules, ~8,200 LOC) + src/api/trade_simulator.py + routes /api/trade/{suggestions,finder,simulate,simulate-mc,import-ktc,export-k
findings.title: The finder's multi-piece guards run only in the give-more direction; the 1-for-N direction is completely unguarded and is now 98% of output
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:665 `if len(give) > len(receive):` gates MULTI_FOR_ONE_MIN_RATIO (0.55), ELITE_MULTI_MIN_RATIO (0.65) and PACKAGE_ANCHOR_MIN_PCT (0.35). findings.area: Trade engines: src/trade/ (15 modules, ~8,200 LOC) + src/api/trade_simulator.py + routes /api/trade/{suggestions,finder,simulate,simulate-mc,import-ktc,export-k
findings.title: Monte Carlo "win probability" is computed from an invented ±15% band that exists on zero live rows, and is uncalibrated against anything
findings.evidence: src/trade/monte_carlo.py:362-382: `band = row.get("valueBand") or {}` … fallback `p10=cv*0.85, p90=cv*1.15`. Measured on the rebuilt live contract: `any row with valueBand: False` (0 of 1,092). src/api/feature_flags.py:59 already records that `stamp_bands_on_players` has no caller. The frontend replicates the same fallback at MonteCarloButton.jsx:52-54. Because every asset gets the identical relative width, winProbA is a deterministic function of the percentage gap — measured at 20,000 sims, seed 1: 0% gap → 0.497, 2% → 0.545, 5% → 0.620, 10% → 0.727, 20% → 0.899, 30% → 0.980. Meanwhile each row DOES carry a real `_marketDispersionCV` (A.J. Brown 0.0232) that the simulator never reads.
findings.userImpact: "Side A won 90% of 40,000 simulations" is a restatement of "Side A is 20% ahead on value," dressed as a probabilistic result. The number deserves no independent weight in a decision, and the simulation adds no information the value delta didn't already carry.

findings.title: The frontend strips the Monte Carlo disclaimer the backend contract declares mandatory, and states the result exactly as the disclaimer forbids

findings.title: Monte Carlo picks and any team-less asset are drawn 12% narrower than players; the docstring asserts the opposite
findings.evidence: monte_carlo.py:271 `zt = z_team.get(pl.team, 0.0) if rho_t else 0.0` — the teams set at :257 excludes falsy team strings, so a team-less asset gets zt=0. Var(z_total) is then 0.65 + 0.10 = 0.75 instead of 1.0, so u = Phi(z_total) is not uniform. Measured over 200,000 draws on a 4250/5000/5750 band: teamed sd 642.6 vs team-less sd 564.0 — 12.2% narrower. Verified that live pick rows carry `team = None` (rebuilt contract: `pick row team= None pos= PICK name= 2026 Early 1st`) and that MonteCarloButton.jsx:57 sends `team: r?.team || ""`. The docstring at monte_carlo.py:226-229 claims "its marginal remains U(0,1) per player so the per-player band is preserved on average."
findings.userImpact: Any trade involving draft picks — most dynasty trades — systematically understates the picks' uncertainty relative to the players, biasing the win probability toward whichever side holds the picks.

findings.title: The finder's confidence tier is a constant, because it reads the scraper's site count instead of the board's blend count
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:419 `source_count = _int_or_none(pdata.get("_sites")) or 0`. Measured on the rebuilt live contract: `_sites` distribution is {1: 526, 3: 439, 2: 109, None: 18} while the board's own `sourceCount` reaches 14 ({14: 209, 5: 123, 13: 39, ...}). With CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE=5, source_confidence is capped at 3/5 = 0.6, so confidence = 0.6 and the multiplier is a fixed 0.88. Every one of the 40 live trades returned confidenceMultiplier 0.88 and confidenceTier "moderate". The sibling engine reads the right field: suggestions.py:602-621 uses the post-Hampel effective source set.
findings.userImpact: The confidence label on every arbitrage recommendation is identical and therefore worthless as a discriminator, and it is understated — a 14-source consensus is reported as "moderate."

findings.title: The finder's arbitrage score is 93% own-side gain and 7% opponent appeal — it ranks lopsidedness, not arbitrage
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:728-729 `f_board_edge = board_gain_norm * 50` and `f_ktc_appeal = opp_appeal * 30`. findings.title: find_angles applies a ±5% plausibility gate across two different publishers' boards, narrower than the boards' own documented disagreement
findings.evidence: src/trade/angle.py:465-467 computes `market_gain_pct = 100*(market_val_target − market_val_selected)/market_val_selected` where each value comes from _value_pair (:314-345), which selects idpTradeCalc for IDP and ktcSfTep otherwise. An offense selected player and an IDP target therefore difference a KTC number against an IDPTC number. The module docstring at :69-72 excuses this: "find_angles (the 1-for-1 pivot) is untouched: it compares two single assets, so there is no cross-market sum to constrain." The codebase's own measurement of the cross-board ratio is p10 0.888 to p90 1.054 (CLAUDE.md, finder.py:229-238) — i.e. ±10% routine disagreement, twice the width of the gate being applied.
findings.userImpact: Cross-market Angle candidates pass or fail a 5% plausibility test that cannot distinguish real market disagreement from the two boards disagreeing with each other. The package path computes an uncertainty_band for exactly this reason; the 1-for-1 path does not.

findings.title: _opponent_fit_label's two branches are identical, so the surplus condition is dead and "Strong bilateral fit" is emitted for a one-sided match
findings.evidence:
src/trade/suggestions.py:998-1003:
```
if opp_needs_my_give and opp_surplus_my_recv:
    fitting_teams.append(team_name)
elif opp_needs_my_give:
    fitting_teams.append(team_name)
```
Both arms append the same value, so the expression reduces to `if opp_needs_my_give`. `opp_surplus_my_recv` is computed at :995 and has no effect. The single-team message at :1010 then reads "Strong bilateral fit: {team} needs {pos} and could deal."

findings.title: Trade fairness is a plain value sum with no roster-spot cost, and the roster-shape correction is optional
findings.evidence: src/api/trade_simulator.py:256 `equity = sum(a["value"] for a in receiving) - sum(a["value"] for a in sending)`. The only roster-shape term is teamImpact, and trade_simulator.py:271 gates it on `if resolved_team and roster_settings:` — with no team or no league roster settings, the response carries equity and nothing else. In the finder, board_delta (finder.py:643) is likewise a raw sum with no roster-spot term; suggestions applies KTC's VA to the gap but its giveTotal/receiveTotal remain raw sums.
findings.userImpact: A 3-for-1 that consumes two extra bench spots grades identically to a 1-for-1 of the same totals whenever teamImpact is skipped. Consolidation cost is modelled only where KTC's VA happens to be applied, and that application is inconsistent across the three engines.

findings.title: team_impact's posture classifier double-counts young starters and is biased toward "contender" on full rosters
findings.evidence: src/trade/team_impact.py:238 `contend_index = top10_share - (pick_share + young_share)`. top10_share is the top-10-by-value share of a 50+ asset roster (mechanically large), and a young top-10 starter contributes to BOTH top10_share (positive) and young_share (negative), so the terms are not a partition. Players with no age contribute 0 to young_share (:232-236), biasing further toward contender.
findings.userImpact: posture is reported to the user and drives windowFit; a systematically mislabelled posture inverts the sign of every windowFit score. Mitigated only because windowFit is excluded from the verdict.

findings.area: BDVM — Brisket Dynasty Valuation Model (src/bdvm/, src/api/bdvm_api.py, src/api/bdvm_signal_alerts.py, config/bdvm/, scripts/bdvm_*.py + fetch_clay/fetch_idpsho
findings.title: BDVM has no projection data on disk — every endpoint is currently a 'no_projection_snapshot' stub, contradicting CLAUDE.md's '726 players priced'
findings.evidence: `data/bdvm/` does not exist on this checkout. Verified: `python3 -c "from src.bdvm.projections import latest_snapshot_path, SNAPSHOT_DIR; print(SNAPSHOT_DIR.exists()); print(latest_snapshot_path(2026))"` → `False` / `None`; same for 2025 and 2027. `src/bdvm/events.py:38 EVENTS_DIR` and `src/bdvm/service.py:57 VALUATION_DIR` also absent. `src/bdvm/service.py:281-296` then returns `{"status": "no_projection_snapshot", "players": [], "picks": []}`. `deploy/deploy.sh:676-678` records the same condition on production: "The BDVM refresh had never run once — `journalctl -u dynasty-bdvm-refresh` was empty and `data/bdvm/` did not exist — so `/api/bdvm/*` served nothing while the deploy reported success every time." CLAUDE.md asserts "scripts/bdvm_build_baseline.py writes a real snapshot (2,815 records for 2026) and the engine answers status: \"ok\" with 726 players priced".
findings.userImpact: Every BDVM surface (the /bdvm page, the /rankings and /draft "Fund gap" columns, /api/bdvm/trade-eval, the daily BDVM signal-alert emails) silently renders nothing. The failure is deliberately silent — `frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1179` gates the column on `bdvmIndex`, so a reader cannot tell "no gap" from "engine has no inputs". CLAUDE.md's numbers describe a state this repository cannot currently produce.

findings.area: BDVM — Brisket Dynasty Valuation Model (src/bdvm/, src/api/bdvm_api.py, src/api/bdvm_signal_alerts.py, config/bdvm/, scripts/bdvm_*.py + fetch_clay/fetch_idpsho
findings.title: BDVM's 'exact league scoring' silently drops 6 active reception-band rules — WR fundamentals are ~15% understated, RB ~9%, QB 0%
findings.evidence: `src/nfl_data/realized_points.py:78-99 _SIMPLE_KEYS` has no entry for `rec_0_4`/`rec_5_9`/`rec_10_19`/`rec_20_29`/`rec_30_39`/`rec_40p`, and `compute_weekly_points` (`:323-420`) has no other branch for them. The live league card carries all six at nonzero rates: `rec_0_4=0.17, rec_5_9=0.42, rec_10_19=0.67, rec_20_29=0.92, rec_30_39=1.17, rec_40p=1.92` (exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json → sleeper.scoringSettings). `src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py::describe_gaps` on the live card returns them as UNSCORABLE: 'reception distance bands need play-by-play; weekly stats carry only a reception count'. Measured with the production scorer: a WR line 5rec/70yd/0.4TD/3.5FD scores 13.30; a typical depth mix adds ~0.48 pts/reception → 2.40 missing → 15.3% understated. RB (3 rec) 8.6%. QB 0.0%.
findings.userImpact: Every fundamental value, every replacement level, and every fundamental-vs-market gap is biased AGAINST pass-catchers and IN FAVOUR of quarterbacks, by ~15 percentage points of relative error. This is exactly the failure mode `scoring_coverage.py`'s own docstring warns about ('a partial correction to a relative quantity is a directional bias'). It propagates into BUY/SELL email alerts, the /rankings Fund-gap column, and the trade-eval verdict. `src/bdvm/scoring.py`'s module docstring claims the reuse means 'any league config that scores history correctly scores projections identically' — the premise (that this engine scores this league's history correctly) is false.

findings.area: BDVM — Brisket Dynasty Valuation Model (src/bdvm/, src/api/bdvm_api.py, src/api/bdvm_signal_alerts.py, config/bdvm/, scripts/bdvm_*.py + fetch_clay/fetch_idpsho
findings.title: STRONG_BUY is structurally unreachable in production — `gap_persisted_days` is never passed
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/market.py:200-208`: `persisted = gap_persisted_days is not None and gap_persisted_days >= int(th["gap_persistence_days"])` and STRONG_BUY requires `alpha > strong_buy_alpha and persisted and liquidity > strong_buy_min_liquidity`. The only production call site is `src/bdvm/service.py:557`: `signal = buy_hold_sell(market_out, params, p_collapse_1y=v.probs.get("p_value_collapse_1y"))` — no `gap_persisted_days`. So `persisted` is always False. `tests/bdvm/test_market_isolation.py:108` passes `gap_persisted_days=30` explicitly, so the test proves the function can emit STRONG_BUY but not that production ever does. Config keys `gap_persistence_days: 14` and `strong_buy_min_liquidity: 0.5` (config/bdvm/params_v1.json) are therefore dead.
findings.userImpact: The label set is asymmetric: STRONG_SELL fires (two paths, `market.py:216` and `:221`) while STRONG_BUY never can. `src/api/bdvm_signal_alerts.py:43` lists STRONG_BUY as actionable and the email template renders it — a state the system cannot enter. Users receive a sell-biased alert stream and reasonably read the absence of STRONG_BUY as 'nothing is a screaming buy'.

findings.area: BDVM — Brisket Dynasty Valuation Model (src/bdvm/, src/api/bdvm_api.py, src/api/bdvm_signal_alerts.py, config/bdvm/, scripts/bdvm_*.py + fetch_clay/fetch_idpsho
findings.title: STRONG_SELL fires on any negative alpha when p_collapse_1y > 0.5, bypassing the −900 threshold
findings.evidence:
`src/bdvm/market.py:216-220`:
```
if p_collapse_1y is not None and p_collapse_1y > 0.5 and alpha < 0:
    return {"signal": "STRONG_SELL", ...}
if alpha < float(th["strong_sell_alpha"]):   # -900
```
The collapse branch is evaluated BEFORE the magnitude threshold, so `alpha = -1` with `p_collapse_1y = 0.51` yields STRONG_SELL while `alpha = -800` with a healthy player yields only HOLD. `p_value_collapse_1y = 1 - p_starter_in_1y` (`engine.py:340`), and `p_starter_in_1y = S(1)·Φ((µ₁−R)/σ₁)`. On the reference archetypes the aging RB p4 has p_collapse=0.65 and the rookie WR p12 has 0.38 — i.e. any older or fringe player crosses 0.5 easily.
findings.userImpact: A near-zero mispricing on an aging or fringe player is reported with the model's most severe label, in an email. Combined with the previous finding (no STRONG_BUY), the signal distribution is systematically bearish in a way that has nothing to do with measured mispricing.

findings.title: Option-value surplus assumes ex-post lineup selection and awards positive value to below-replacement projections
findings.evidence:
`src/bdvm/surplus.py:32-37`: `E[max(0, X−R)] = (µ−R)·Φ(z) + σ·φ(z)`, `season_starter_value` multiplies by `games` (`:55`). The justification given at `surplus.py:6-7` is "You are never forced to start a below-replacement outcome" — but a fantasy lineup is set BEFORE the outcome is known, so `E[max(0, X−R)]` prices perfect foresight. Measured with production code (WR, R=6.15, G=17, σ from `sigma_fpg`):
```
µ=6.15 (exactly replacement): option 19.72   truncated 0.00
µ=5.00 (below replacement):   option  8.12   truncated 0.00
µ=8.00:                       option 44.38   truncated 31.45  (+41%)
µ=20.0:                       option 240.55  truncated 235.45 (+2%)
```
The premium is ~0% at the top of the board and unbounded near/below replacement, so it is a systematic re-ranking, not a level shift.
findings.userImpact: High-variance, low-mean assets are structurally overvalued relative to stable starters, and the size of the effect is set entirely by `cv_base` — an unvalidated prior. `surplus.py:8` calls this "the central V1 HYPOTHESIS, not a law" and the `surplusMode` ablation exists, but nothing has ever run the ablation against realized outcomes (see the validation finding), so the champion formulation is unjustified.

findings.title: Rookie-pick values are a frozen prior table that is never anchored to the calibrated player scale, yet the two are summed in one CES package
findings.evidence: Player trade values are pool-calibrated: `src/bdvm/engine.py:227-233 calibrate()` sets `anchors[k] = max_DV / (target_top_value/10000)^(1/γ)` so the top asset always maps to 9800. Measured: 1.01 balanced EV = 4984.0 = 50.9% of the top player; 1.06 = 2420.0 (24.7%); 1.12 = 1582.0 (16.1%). `src/api/bdvm_api.py:334-338` then feeds player `tradeValue[s]` and pick `distribution[s].ev` into the SAME `package_value` call at `:347-348`. Worked example: side A = [top player 9800] → 9800.0; side B = [1.01, 1.02, 1.03] → 10440.6; edge −640.6. Nothing establishes that a 1.01 is worth 51% of the #1 dynasty asset in this model's currency.
findings.userImpact: `POST /api/bdvm/trade-eval` (the "Fundamentals check (BDVM)" panel on /trade) returns a numeric verdict on any player-for-picks trade in which one side's numbers come from a calibrated model and the other side's come from a hand-written table. The verdict looks identical to a fully-modelled one.

findings.title: Roster strategy capitals and the double-positive trade scan exclude picks entirely, despite the module claiming to produce 'pick capital'
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/roster.py:6` docstring: "produces, per roster: strategy capitals ... value-weighted age, pick capital, and a contend/retool/rebuild direction." But `analyze_rosters` builds `assets` only from `roster["playerIds"]` (`:154-171`); `roster["picks"]` is used solely for `"pickCount": len(roster["picks"])` (`:199`). `capitals` (`:172`) sums over `assets` only. The trade scan (`:272-286`) draws `a_assets`/`b_assets` from `ra["assets"]`, so no pick can ever appear in a proposed trade.
findings.userImpact: `nowFutureRatio = contender_capital / rebuilder_capital` (`:186`) is computed with all future draft capital deleted, which is precisely the quantity that distinguishes a rebuilder. That ratio drives `_directions_relative` → `strategy_for_direction` → which currency each side is scored in during the scan. `roster.py:66-74` even documents the resulting saturation ('EVERY roster's contender capital exceeds its rebuilder capital and all twelve rosters would read "contend"') and works around it with a league-median rescale instead of fixing the input. The scan can never suggest the most common real dynasty trade shape (veteran for picks).

findings.title: `liquidity` increases with market DISAGREEMENT and multiplies the gap into alpha — inverted semantics, and it silently rescales every signal threshold by ~0.38
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/market.py:88-96`: `liquidity = clip(0.35 + 1.6·dispersion, 0.2, 1.0)` where `dispersion` is documented at `:54` as a "0-1 cross-source disagreement proxy". More disagreement → higher 'liquidity'. The SAME dispersion is used in the opposite direction two lines later for market precision: `:165` `tau_market *= 1.0 - 0.5·dispersion`. Then `:157` `alpha = gap * liquidity`. Measured on the live export (`_marketDispersionCV`, n=839): min 0.0, p50 0.0208, p90 0.0882, max 0.249 — so liquidity is 0.35–0.75, median 0.383, and 45.2% of rows have dispersion EXACTLY 0.0 → liquidity 0.35. Thresholds are stated in alpha units (`buy_alpha: 400`, `strong_sell_alpha: -900`), so the effective gap thresholds are ≈ +1045 and ≈ −2350, and `strong_buy_min_liquidity: 0.5` is unreachable for 45% of the board even if STRONG_BUY were wired.
findings.userImpact: Two compounding errors. (1) Directionally, a player the market cannot agree on gets his mispricing AMPLIFIED into a stronger BUY/SELL rather than damped. (2) Numerically, the documented thresholds are ~2.6× tighter than the behaviour, so the BUY/SELL bands are far wider than an operator reading params_v1.json would expect.

findings.title: Seven parameter sections in params_v1.json are never read; the most consequential leaves single-source projections with σ_source = 0
findings.evidence: `grep -rn <key> --include=*.py src/ scripts/ server.py` returns 0 hits for: `single_source_projection_sigma_mult` (1.5), `missing_projection_impute`, `equal_weight_shrinkage` (0.3), `trade_value_max` (10000), `lambda_market_fundamental` (0.0), `best_ball_buffer_bump` ({RB:0.5, WR:0.5}), `positions_true`. The σ one is load-bearing: `src/bdvm/projections.py:400-402` computes `var = Σ w·(fpg−µ)²/Σw`, which is exactly 0.0 for a single record, so `sigma_source = 0` and `engine.py:141 sigma_fpg(..., p.sigma_source, ...)` reduces to `CV·µ` with no cross-source term. With only the reconstructed baseline on disk, EVERY player is single-source. `best_ball_buffer_bump` also matters: the live league is `best_ball: 1` (exports/latest → sleeper.leagueSettings) and `league_config.py:210` reads it, but nothing applies the bump.
findings.userImpact: Uncertainty is understated exactly where it is largest (one proxy source), and because σ drives the option-value surplus, the understatement flows straight into value — the effect is largest for near-replacement players. In a best-ball league, replacement levels for RB/WR are set as if lineups were weekly, overstating everyone's surplus.

findings.title: `risk_lambda` moves values by 1–2%: 'risk_neutral' is a near-duplicate of 'balanced' after anchoring, so the four strategy currencies are really three
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/engine.py:196`: `max(0.0, v - lam · 0.35 · disp)` where `disp = sqrt(Σ (d^t·σ_t·G_t·S_t)²)`. Measured on the reference archetypes: p1 raw DV 637.0, dispersion 221.1, penalty 7.7 = 1.2% of raw; p5 1.2%; p12 1.9%. After per-strategy anchoring (`calibrate`), `risk_neutral` (λ=0) vs `balanced` (λ=0.1) differ by 0.06%–2.56% in trade value across all 13 archetypes (p5 −0.00%, p1 +0.06%, p10 +2.56%). findings.userImpact: The /bdvm strategy selector and the trade-eval 'every strategy currency' output present `risk_neutral` as a distinct lens; it is balanced ±1%. findings.title: `range.ceiling_p85` escapes the advertised 0–10000 scale (up to 19,843) and is rendered without a cap

findings.title: Five of the eleven news→event keyword rules produce no effect at all, and their audit trail gives a false reason
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/news_events.py:78-107` maps 11 ontology types. At `_AUTO_CONFIDENCE = 0.45` (`:42`), `src/bdvm/events.py:117-141` suppresses every channel except `sigma_mult`. Five mapped types carry no `sigma_mult` in `config/bdvm/event_types_v1.json`: DEPTH_CHART_PROMOTION, SIGNING, SUSPENSION, CONTRACT_EXTENSION, FRANCHISE_TAG. Measured (`effective_impact` at 3 days old, reliability 0.6): those five return `{}`; the six that do fire return sigma_mult 1.018–1.072 (PRACTICE_LIMITATION 1.0181, INJURY 1.0358, DEPTH_CHART_DEMOTION 1.0367, TRADE 1.0376, SURGERY 1.0599, RELEASE 1.0717). `events.py:170-178` then records `applied: False, reason: "reflected_in_projection_or_fully_decayed"` — neither of which is true; the channels were suppressed by the speculation rule.
findings.userImpact: The auto-ingest lane is advertised (CLAUDE.md, `news_events.py:1-8`) as converting 'a dormant subsystem into a live one that reacts to the real world'. In practice 5 of 11 rules are inert and the other 6 widen σ by at most 7%, decaying with a 14–90 day half-life — which flows into value only through the option term and is dwarfed by the CV prior.
