findings.title: Nothing has ever validated any BDVM output — the backtest harness has no production caller and no measurement exists
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/backtest.py` (336 lines: rolling-origin folds, leakage guard, baselines B0–B4, Spearman/MAE/RMSE/Brier/calibration) is imported by exactly one file: `tests/bdvm/test_backtest.py`, which feeds it synthetic rows (`grep -rn "from src.bdvm.backtest" --include=*.py .`). No script, route or workflow calls `run_backtest`, `s3_calibration` or `compare_surplus_modes`. `src/bdvm/engine.py:399` hardcodes `"provisional": True,  # priors not yet backtested — always true in v1`. `config/bdvm/params_v1.json`'s header states 'EVERY number here is a STARTING PRIOR ... NOT backtested truth'. The 194 tests in `tests/bdvm/` assert shape, monotonicity and reproduction of the reference fixture — none compares an output to a realized outcome.
findings.userImpact: Every number the system emits — trade values, gaps, BUY/SELL signals, trade verdicts — rests on hand-picked constants with zero out-of-sample evidence. The most sensitive of them is labelled as such in the config itself: `replacement.waiver_buffer` is called 'THE most sensitive knob in the model (it sets the origin of the value scale)'. Measured sensitivity on the reference archetypes, shifting every buffer by ±0.5 players/team: R(WR) moves 5.325→7.102, and the veteran WR p6 moves 2631.5→2315.7 (−12%) while the young WR p5 stays pinned at 9800 — i.e. the RELATIVE ordering shifts with an unvalidated prior.

findings.title: `get_bdvm_values` cache key contains `id(contract)`, a reusable CPython address
findings.evidence: `src/api/bdvm_api.py:173-186`: `key = (id(contract), contract.get("generatedAt"), league_key, ...)`. `id()` is the object's memory address; once a contract dict is garbage-collected a later dict can be allocated at the same address. The remaining key components (`generatedAt`, `leagueKey`, `paramSetId`, snapshot path, surplus mode, actuals week, events fingerprint) would normally differ, so a stale hit needs a `generatedAt` collision — but the LRU is only 4 entries (`:39`) so a false MISS from an address change is the common case, silently turning a repeat request into a multi-second cold engine run.
findings.userImpact: Cache effectiveness is tied to object identity rather than content. In the pathological direction (same address, same `generatedAt` — e.g. a `None` generatedAt on a rebuilt contract) a stale board would be served.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: Activity evidence is only collected for managers who already qualified — the cohort is self-reinforcing and the recency gate is vacuous for everyone else
findings.evidence: scripts/crawl_sharp_activity.py:34-44 selects `manager.qualified` managers only, and :63-75 crawls ONLY those: `if not selected: return {"status": "cohort_building", ...}`. Those crawls are the only writer of `asset_movements` for Sleeper sharp managers. src/sharp/platform_records.py:95-117 then derives BOTH `trades_completed` and `days_since_last_activity` from `asset_movements`. Consequences, both verified: (a) `S._activity_component(record_with_no_movements, cfg)` -> `0.0`, so the 0.08 activity weight is permanently zero for every not-yet-qualified manager; (b) `S.check_eligibility(record_with days_since_last_activity=None)` -> `[]` — the `requireRecentActivityDays: 400` gate is skipped entirely because src/sharp/score.py:262 reads `if recent and rec.days_since_last_activity is not None`.
findings.userImpact: Qualification is partly a function of already being qualified. A manager who clears the bar gains activity data, gains up to 8 points of score, and is protected against the recency gate that only fires once you HAVE movement data. A manager who has never been crawled is scored on 92% of the axes and cannot fail the dormancy gate at all. The board's "smart money" cohort is therefore path-dependent on crawl order, not purely on merit. The `abandoned-roster` gate is dead for the same class of reason (see separate finding).

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: Trades between two cohort managers produce exactly zero directional signal while inflating volume and confidence
findings.evidence: src/intel/crawler.py:288 `if not owner or owner not in pool: return` — both sides of a trade are emitted when both owners are in the pool; :315-316 `emit(rid, "add", ...)` / `emit(rid, "drop", ...)` for every player. src/intel/crawler.py:458 `pool = set(members)`, and scripts/crawl_sharp_activity.py:77-82 passes the qualified cohort as `member_ids`. src/sharp/market.py:307-312 then counts `entry["buys"] += 1` for the add and `entry["sells"] += 1` for the drop of the SAME player in the SAME transaction. Result: `net = 0`, `volume = 2`, `uniqueManagers = 2`. src/intel/signals.py:180-186 makes `strength = (0/2) * ... = 0.0`, while src/intel/signals.py:124 promotes the row toward `medium` on volume/manager counts.
findings.userImpact: The better the cohort's coverage inside a league, the more its own trades cancel to a zero signal — the failure mode gets worse exactly as data quality improves. Meanwhile the confidence label moves UP on assets whose direction is meaningless. A user reading the board cannot distinguish "the sharps disagree" from "two sharps traded with each other". The cohort is grown by BFS from a single 13-member seed league (config/sharp/discovery_seeds.json), so cohort members sharing leagues is the expected case, not the edge case.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: multiLeagueConsistency counts season-rows as "independent leagues", and says so in user-facing text
findings.evidence: src/sharp/score.py:370-397 operates on `rec.finish_percentiles`, which src/sharp/platform_records.py:152-156 and src/sharp/records.py:407-413 build with ONE ENTRY PER LEAGUE-SEASON. `min_leagues = block.get("minLeaguesForFullCredit", 4)` is then compared against `len(finishes)` (:390-392), and the contributor string at :394-397 reads `f"Above median in {round(above*100)}% of {len(finishes)} independent leagues"`. Reproduced for a manager in 2 leagues over 3 seasons each: `_consistency_component` -> `(0.9782, ['Above median in 100% of 6 independent leagues'])`. The manager is in TWO leagues.
findings.userImpact: The component the module's own docstring calls "the core anti-luck signal" and "repeated success across INDEPENDENT dynasty leagues" (score.py:363-367, :26-30) is not measuring independence. A 2-league manager with a long tenure gets the same full breadth credit as a 4-league manager, and the variance penalty mixes year-to-year variance inside one league with genuine cross-league variance. The explanation string shown to a user as justification is factually wrong about the number of leagues. This is 22% of the score.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: The cohort is selected on realized end-of-season outcomes and then its historical transactions are served over any window, including 'all'
findings.evidence: Qualification consumes realized outcomes only: `wins/losses/ties` (src/sharp/platform_records.py:149-151), `made_playoffs` and `is_champion` from the completed-season winners bracket (src/sharp/records.py:187-189, :214-216), and regular-season finish (:190, :133-152). src/sharp/records.py:44-50 is explicit that only `is_complete` seasons count. The market then queries movements for exactly that cohort with only a time filter — src/sharp/market.py:446-459 and src/intel/platform_ledger.py:1615-1646 — and `window="all"` maps to `(None, now)` (src/intel/signals.py:84-85), i.e. every movement the ledger retains, including movements made during the very seasons whose final standings certified the manager. There is no point-in-time cohort snapshot anywhere: `cohort_members` is recomputed from the current records on every request (market.py:217-218).
findings.userImpact: For live forward-looking use this is defensible — you are watching today's cohort's moves today. For ANY retrospective claim about the signal ("the sharps were buying X before it rose"), it is textbook look-ahead: the manager was labelled sharp using information that did not exist when the trade was made. Since there is no backtest at all, no such claim is currently made in code — but the `all` window is exposed in the UI dropdown (frontend/app/market/sharp-tracker/page.jsx:7) and produces exactly that mixed-epoch view. There is also no way to reconstruct what the cohort was on any past date.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: Two competing ManagerRecord builders with different gates; the operator/bootstrap tooling uses the looser one
findings.evidence: LIVE path: src/sharp/platform_records.py:72-177, which enforces identity type (`source_identity_type != IDENTITY_GLOBAL_VERIFIED` -> excluded, :46-52), non-null result fields (`_REQUIRED_RESULT_FIELDS`, :15-23 and :57-63), stored `exclusion_reasons_json` (:64-68), and an FFPC-specific recent-activity requirement (:134-135). LEGACY path: src/sharp/records.py:354-438, whose entire filter is `WHERE is_complete = 1 AND sharp_eligible = 1` (:367-372) — no identity check, no null-field check, no exclusion-reason check. server.py:12581 -> src/sharp/service.py:36 uses the LIVE one. But deploy/bootstrap-sharp-records.sh:95-103 (`qualified_count`, whose value gates whether the activity crawl runs at all, :278-283) and scripts/crawl_sharp_records.py:206-220 (`--score`) both call `records.build_manager_records()`. Tests reinforce the split: tests/sharp/test_records.py:238-274 tests the legacy builder, tests/sharp/test_platform_records.py tests the live one; neither compares them.
findings.userImpact: The number an operator sees in the deploy log ("Sharp Tracker has N qualified manager(s)") and the number `/api/sharp/cohort` reports can differ, with the operator number being systematically HIGHER because it skips the identity and completeness gates. Since bootstrap-sharp-records.sh:278 branches on that number to decide whether to run the activity crawl, a false-positive count can trigger an activity crawl whose `qualified_sleeper_ids()` (which uses the strict builder) then returns nothing — the exact 'ran successfully, populated nothing' outcome the five force/trigger workflows exist to chase.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: Four sharp workflows try to `git add` a gitignored path and therefore always fail at their reporting step
findings.evidence: .gitignore:45 is a bare `data/` (only `!data/ros/` is re-included), so `git check-ignore -v data/ops/sharp-production-smoke.json` returns `.gitignore:45:data/`. The commit steps use a plain `git add` on that path with no `-f`: .github/workflows/verify-sharp-production.yml:163, force-sharp-production-now.yml:238, trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml:136, trigger-sharp-now-via-merge.yml:130. GitHub Actions runs `run:` blocks under `bash -e`, and force-sharp/verify additionally set `set -Eeuo pipefail`. Verified in a scratch repo with the same ignore rules: `git add data/ops/x.json` -> `The following paths are ignored ... hint: Use -f`, exit 1. Corroborating evidence that this has never worked: `git ls-files data/ops/` returns nothing and the directory does not exist in the checkout. The `|| exit 0` guards in force/trigger are attached to `git commit`, not to `git add`, so they do not help.
findings.userImpact: `verify-sharp-production.yml` triggers on EVERY push to main outside `data/**` and `exports/**` (lines 4-9). Each run polls production for up to 80 attempts x 30s = 40 minutes (line 85, 149) and then fails at the commit step — before the `Enforce healthy population` step (line 167) ever executes. So the workflow named 'verify Sharp production population' has never verified anything, and the three trigger/force workflows silently lose their diagnostics. This is the direct explanation for why five 'force/trigger/verify sharp now' workflows accumulated: the feedback loop that would have told the operator whether the population run worked is structurally broken.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: Sharp Score has no validation of any kind — no backtest, no holdout, no calibration
findings.evidence: No file under scripts/ references sharp validation: `ls scripts/ | grep backtest` returns eight backtest scripts (backtest_adjusted_board.py, backtest_alpha_shrinkage.py, backtest_ktc_volatility.py, backtest_percentile_reference_n.py, ...), none of them for sharp. `grep -rn 'sharp' src/api src/trade src/canonical src/league_intel src/bdvm` returns nothing. config/sharp/scoring_v2.json:2 says so outright: "Weights are PRIORS chosen for defensibility, not values validated against an outcome dataset." Every constant in the subsystem is hand-picked: 0.36/0.22/0.22/0.12/0.08, subweights 0.28/0.22/0.26/0.14/0.10, priorN 6.0, clamp [0.4,2.5], 0.65/0.35, seasonsForFullCredit 5, tradesPerSeasonForFullCredit 6, maxPenalty 0.25, 0.6/0.4 splits (twice), halfCredit 3.0/3.0, and on the market side _CONFIDENCE_HALF_VOLUME 5.0, _BREADTH_HALF_MANAGERS 3.0, confidence tier cutoffs 12/4/3 and 5/2.
findings.userImpact: There is no evidence anywhere in the repository that a manager with a Sharp Score of 75 makes better trades than one at 55, nor that a high signalStrength precedes a value move. The number is presented to users as a decision aid on a page titled 'Sharp Tracker' with a column labelled 'Signal'. Compare this to the valuation subsystem, which has eight backtests and a model registry with human promotion gates — the contrast makes the absence a deliberate-looking gap rather than an oversight.

findings.evidence: config/sharp/ffpc_sources.json ships `"enabled": true`, `"allowProvisionalPublicInCombinedSignals": true`, `"provisionalPublicWeight": 0.55`, and all ten seed leagues carry `"sharpEligible": false` — so FFPC can never produce an automated qualifier (src/platforms/ffpc/adapter.py:87 reads that flag straight from config into the evidence rows, and src/sharp/platform_records.py:55-56 excludes rows whose `sharp_eligible` is falsy with reason `unknown_or_ineligible_league_format`). `provisional_members` (src/sharp/market.py:176-190) selects EVERY distinct manager_key that appears on any trade in a configured public page — no skill filter, no recency filter, no minimum trade count. src/sharp/market.py:246-247 includes them in the default `qualification="all"` selection, and the page defaults to `qualification: "all"` (frontend/app/market/sharp-tracker/page.jsx:118). The table column header at page.jsx:342 is literally `"Sharp managers"`, rendering `row.uniqueManagers` — which includes provisional members.
findings.userImpact: On a board titled 'Sharp Tracker', a row can be driven entirely by managers whose only qualification is 'their name appeared on a public FFPC league page'. At weight 0.55 they carry ~70% of the influence of the best-evidenced automated qualifier (whose realistic ceiling is ~0.79). The disclaimer at page.jsx:418-424 explains the distinction in body copy, but the column header contradicts it and the default filter includes them.

findings.evidence: (a) `maxAbandonedRosterRate: 0.34` — src/sharp/score.py:256-260 reads `rec.abandoned_rate`, which is `abandoned_rosters / observed_leagues` (:141-144). `abandoned_rosters` is never set by src/sharp/platform_records.py:158-176 or src/sharp/records.py:418-437, so it is always the dataclass default 0 and the rate is always 0.0. (b) `requireRecentActivityDays: 400` — src/sharp/score.py:261-264 short-circuits on `rec.days_since_last_activity is not None`, and that field is None for every manager with no rows in `asset_movements` (platform_records.py:172-174). Verified: `S.check_eligibility(record_with_no_movements)` -> `[]`. docs/intel/SHARP_SCORE.md lists both in the 'Hard eligibility gates' table with rationales ('Abandoned rosters are the opposite of sharp', 'A dormant manager is not a live signal'). tests/sharp/test_score.py:74-79 passes only because it sets both fields by hand.
findings.userImpact: Two of seven advertised safety gates are decorative. Dormant and roster-abandoning managers are not excluded — they are simply invisible to the checks. The tests give false assurance because they never exercise the shipped record shape.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: 'Median finish' is regular-season standing, but code comments and docs call it final standing
findings.evidence: src/sharp/records.py:133-152 `_finish_ranks` — "Regular-season finish order, 1 = best. Sleeper publishes no `rank`, so it is derived the way a league standings page does: wins, then points-for as the tiebreak." That value becomes `finish_rank` (:218) and then `finish_percentiles` (platform_records.py:152-156). But src/sharp/score.py:115 labels the field `# Per-league final-standing percentile (0 = last, 1 = first)`, and docs/intel/SHARP_SCORE.md's platform-neutral evidence list requires "final standings". Playoffs and championships come from a DIFFERENT source in the same row (the winners bracket, records.py:187-189), so the two are genuinely inconsistent within one record.
findings.userImpact: A 7-7 team that wins the championship records a mediocre finish percentile, which feeds both the 0.14 medianFinishPercentile sub-weight AND the entire 0.22 multiLeagueConsistency component. Playoff-run skill is systematically discounted in the two largest realized-results terms, while being credited in the smaller championship terms. A reader of score.py or the docs would not know this.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: The percentile qualification bar has no minimum-population floor, so a small evaluable set labels up to half its members 'top quartile'
findings.evidence: src/sharp/score.py:633-637 computes `entry.score_percentile = percentile_rank(entry.score, raw_scores)` and qualifies on `>= 0.75`. With the midpoint tie handling at :201-203, for N evaluable managers with distinct scores, the k-th from the bottom has percentile (k+0.5)/N, so the number qualifying is N - ceil(0.75N - 0.5): N=4 -> 1 (25%, correct), N=3 -> 1 (33%), N=2 -> 1 (50%), N=1 -> 0. Only `maxCohortSize: 2500` bounds the top (:639-643); there is no floor. config/sharp/scoring_v2.json documents the bar as "Top 25% (top quartile) of the EVALUABLE population".
findings.userImpact: Sharp Tracker is explicitly a growing network — src/sharp/service.py:104-107 treats `cohort_building` as a normal state. During the ramp, when only a handful of managers have enough crawled history to be evaluable, the system will label half of them 'sharp' and weight their trades at score/100 on the public board, with no signal that the cohort is statistically meaningless.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: /api/sharp/cohort and /api/sharp/market each rebuild and re-score the entire manager population two to three times per request
findings.evidence: src/sharp/service.py:75-76 calls `load_manager_records()` (a full `manager_seasons` scan plus two aggregate queries at platform_records.py:86-117) then `score_managers`; then :125 calls `_records_coverage()` -> `platform_records.coverage()` (:208-209) which calls `build_manager_records` AGAIN. src/sharp/market.py:437-441 calls `cohort_members(...)` (build + score) and then :530-534 calls `cohort_members(qualification="all")` a SECOND time purely for the coverage block — even when the request already asked for `qualification="all"`. Each `score_managers` is O(n^2) because `percentile_rank` (score.py:191-203) is O(len(pop)) and is called ~4 times per manager plus once for the final percentile. config/sharp/discovery_seeds.json sets `maxUsersPerRun: 20000`.
findings.userImpact: Violates the repo's own Performance Rules ('Eliminate duplicated calculations, repeated fetches'). At a few hundred managers this is invisible; at the tens of thousands the discovery graph is designed to reach, a single /api/sharp/market request performs four full population scorings with quadratic percentile work, on a request thread (server.py:12581 wraps it in run_in_threadpool, so it consumes a worker rather than blocking the loop — but it still consumes one for the duration). The 60s frontend auto-refresh (page.jsx:21) makes this recurring.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: Market routes are registered by import side-effect and re-registered from inside a GET handler
findings.evidence: src/sharp/service.py:251 calls `_register_http_routes()` at module import; src/sharp/service.py:57 calls it AGAIN from inside `cohort_status()` — the comment at :52-56 says this exists as a 'production self-heal' because the routes had previously been silently absent. `_server_app()` (:151-164) hunts `sys.modules` for `server` or `__main__` because production starts with `python server.py`. So `/api/sharp/market` and `/api/sharp/market/audit` exist only if the import succeeded against the right module name, or if someone first hit `/api/sharp/cohort`. Only `/api/sharp/cohort` is declared normally (server.py:12571).
findings.userImpact: Two of the three sharp endpoints have no static declaration: they will not appear in the OpenAPI schema generated at startup, cannot be found by a route-table grep of server.py, and their existence depends on request ordering. The retry logic on the frontend treats 404 as retryable (frontend/app/market/sharp-tracker/page.jsx:22) — which is a workaround for exactly this, and it means a genuinely missing route is indistinguishable from a transient failure. `check-sharp-production-now.yml:56` also calls `service._register_http_routes()` manually before inspecting, which is another workaround.

findings.title: docs/intel/FFPC_UNIFIED_SHARP.md says FFPC is 'disabled by default'; the shipped config enables it and turns on provisional contribution
findings.evidence: docs/intel/FFPC_UNIFIED_SHARP.md:93 — 'The first implementation is deliberately **public-only, read-only, and disabled by default**' — and its example config block shows `"enabled": false`. config/sharp/ffpc_sources.json ships `"enabled": true`, `"allowProvisionalPublicInCombinedSignals": true`, `"provisionalPublicWeight": 0.55`, and ten enabled seed leagues. tests/sharp/test_ffpc_production_config.py:12-16 asserts the ENABLED state, so the test suite pins the opposite of what the doc states.

In fact ten public FFPC leagues are collected daily (deploy/systemd/dynasty-ffpc-sharp.timer, 05:20 UTC) and their managers contribute to the default market view at weight 0.55. Per CLAUDE.md rule 6, this is exactly the class of divergence that should have been called out.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: Championship credit is counted twice — as a shrunk rate inside performance and again as a bonus on top
findings.evidence: src/sharp/score.py:298-303 gives championships a 0.26 sub-weight inside the performance component (which itself carries 0.36), and src/sharp/score.py:586, :594 adds `title_bonus` (0 to 0.12) directly to the same total. Combined maximum contribution from titles: 0.36*0.26 = 0.094 via performance plus 0.12 bonus = 0.214 of a 1.0-scale score, i.e. ~21 points of a 100-point scale — and ~27% of the 78.6-point production ceiling. The config's own comment (config/sharp/scoring_v2.json, `weights._comment`) acknowledges the bonus is outside the sum, but nothing acknowledges that the same evidence already appears inside it.
findings.userImpact: A single title is worth roughly a third of a standard deviation more than the weights table implies, and the config comment at `performance.championshipShrinkage` — 'one title in one season is mostly luck, not proof' — is undercut by an unshrunk raw-count bonus applied on top of the shrunk rate. The bonus uses `rec.championships` directly (:442), with no shrinkage.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: The activity crawl runs in a separate process from the API but relies on an in-process threading lock to serialize Sleeper crawls
findings.evidence: src/intel/service.py:43 `_REFRESH_LOCK = threading.Lock()`, and `refresh_intel` (:163-164) documents it as 'Rejects concurrent runs via a non-blocking process lock — one crawl at a time regardless of league, so two leagues can never double Sleeper load'. scripts/crawl_sharp_activity.py:77-82 calls `intel_service.refresh_intel(...)` from a standalone systemd oneshot (deploy/systemd/dynasty-sharp-activity.service.template), which is a DIFFERENT OS process from the uvicorn backend that also calls `refresh_intel` for Insider Trading. A `threading.Lock` provides no cross-process exclusion.
findings.userImpact: The stated 'one Sleeper crawl at a time' invariant does not hold between the sharp-activity job (06:30 UTC, budget 2500) and any concurrent Insider Trading refresh. Both crawls can hit Sleeper simultaneously, doubling the request rate against a documented 1000/min ceiling that the code otherwise deliberately stays at half of (config/sharp/discovery_seeds.json `_rateLimitNote`). The 06:30 slot is close to the 05:20 FFPC and 04:50 records slots, and `RandomizedDelaySec=900` on each widens the overlap window.

findings.area: Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/` + `config/sharp/` + sharp crawl scripts + `/api/sharp/*` + `/market/sharp-tracker` + 6 GitHub workflows) at commit 9c5d972
findings.title: Longevity and the activity rate are computed per league-season row rather than per calendar season
findings.evidence: `completed_seasons` is set to `len(seasons)` where `seasons` is the list of league-season ROWS (src/sharp/platform_records.py:160, src/sharp/records.py:421). src/sharp/score.py:406 `clamp(seasons/(seasons + 2.5))` therefore treats a manager in 3 leagues for 2 years (6 rows) as more tenured than one in 1 league for 5 years (5 rows). src/sharp/score.py:415 divides a lifetime trade count by the same number, so the same behaviour reads as a lower per-season trade rate for a multi-league manager. The eligibility gate `minCompletedSeasons: 2` is likewise satisfiable by one calendar year in two leagues.
findings.userImpact: Breadth leaks into two components that are supposed to measure tenure and per-season engagement — the same conflation as the multiLeagueConsistency defect, at lower weight (0.12 + 0.08). The score.py module docstring rule 1 states 'Being in many leagues is not skill — it is availability. League count feeds only the consistency and confidence terms', which is not what the code does.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: tradeCount is computed by summing per-asset transaction counts, inflating it by the number of assets in each trade
findings.evidence: src/intel/lead_service.py:90-93 — `counts = {uid: sum(int(r["tradeCount"] or 0) for r in rows if str(r["userId"]) == uid) for uid in per_user}` where `rows` comes from `ledger.manager_asset_activity(...)`, which is `GROUP BY user_id, asset_id` (src/intel/ledger.py:903) with `tradeCount = COUNT(DISTINCT tx_id)` per group. Identical pattern at src/intel/service.py:783 — `trade_count = sum(r["tradeCount"] for r in rows)`. Reproduced against a real SQLite ledger: one 4-for-4 trade between users A and B produced 8 movements; the sum yielded A=4, B=4 against a truth of 1 each, while `ledger.counts(user_ids=['A'])` on the same rows correctly returned `{'tradeCount': 1, 'assetMovementCount': 4, ...}`. docs/intel/METRICS.md defines `tradeCount` as 'Distinct tx_id values. Counts transactions.' and opens with 'Most counting bugs in this domain come from silently converting one into another.'
findings.userImpact: GET /api/intel/member/{owner_id} publishes a `tradeCount` that overstates a manager's trade volume by the mean assets-per-trade (typically 2-6x). Worse, the same inflated number is the `trades_completed` input to both `leads.activity_fit` and `roster_intel.partner.assess_partner` inside the lead score. The inflation is NOT a common scale factor: five 1-for-1 trades read as 10 while five 3-for-3 trades read as 30, so a manager who makes big multi-asset deals is ranked as ~3x more active than an equally frequent trader of singles. That distorts both the 0.10 activity term and partner.py's shrunk history logit, and the inflated raw count is shown to the user verbatim in the reason string 'Active trader — N trades observed' (leads.py:309).

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: The documented roster-clog guard (starter_value_floor) is inert on the live path
findings.evidence: src/intel/roster_shape.py:67 declares `starter_value_floor: float = 0.0`; :93 gates on `if value_by_player is not None and starter_value_floor > 0:`. The only production caller is server.py:12208-12210 — `roster_shape.team_signals(teams, positions, league_cfg.roster_settings, value_by_player=values)` — which passes `value_by_player` but never `starter_value_floor`, so the filter never executes. The module docstring at roster_shape.py:71-74 states the opposite: 'A player counts toward a position only if their value clears `starter_value_floor` — roster clog is not depth, and counting it would make every deep bench look like a surplus.' `grep -rn 'starter_value_floor' --include=*.py .` shows the only place a non-zero floor is supplied is tests/intel/test_lead_service.py:207.
findings.userImpact: Every rostered body counts as positional depth, so surplus is systematically overstated and deficit understated for every manager. This propagates into the 0.18 positionalNeed term of the lead score in BUY mode (which reads `surplus`) and into `roster_intel.partner.assess_partner`'s need alignment, which itself carries 0.26 of the score. The lead list ranks managers on a roster shape that counts waiver flotsam as starters.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: Positional need is ordinal within a roster and carries no magnitude, but is summed into a cross-manager ranking
findings.evidence: src/intel/leads.py:257-259 — `strongest = max(pool); fit = magnitude / strongest if strongest > 0 else 0.0`. Verified numerically through the full scorer with all other inputs held constant: deficits {QB: 0.1, RB: 0.05} and deficits {QB: 3.0, RB: 0.5} both yield `positionalNeed = 0.180` and an identical lead score of 33.1, and both emit the reason string 'QB is one of their biggest gaps'. The docstring at leads.py:257-258 claims the normalisation exists 'so a roster with mild needs everywhere does not read as desperate' — it produces exactly that outcome. tests/intel/test_leads.py:147 (`test_need_is_normalised_against_their_own_gaps`) pins this as intended behaviour.
findings.userImpact: The 0.18-weighted term is a within-roster rank, not a need measure, so it is not comparable between the managers it is being used to rank. A manager whose deepest hole is 0.1 starter slots is credited the same 18 points as one who is three starters short at that position. The reason string tells the user 'QB is one of their biggest gaps' about a roster with no meaningful gap at all — inference from a normalisation artefact presented as a fact about the manager.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: The value-match term is saturated for essentially every lead and contributes no ranking information
findings.evidence: src/intel/leads.py:289-290 — `if best <= tolerance: return 1.0, [...]` with `tolerance = 0.18`, against `their_matchable_values` = every priced player on their roster (src/intel/roster_shape.py:123-143, no floor). Monte-Carlo over the live board's actual value distribution (exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json, 1074 priced assets, `_finalAdjusted` as the 0-9999 scale proxy), 3000 random 25-player rosters drawn from the top 400: P(valueMatch == 1.0) = 45.3% for a rank-1 asset, 77.9% at rank 10, 99.0% at rank 50, 100.0% at rank 150 and rank 300 (mean 1.000). Real rosters carry deep-bench values too, which only widens coverage.
findings.userImpact: For any target outside roughly the top 20 of the board — i.e. almost every query — the 0.12-weighted term adds a constant +12 points to every league-mate and discriminates between none of them. It inflates the headline number without informing the ranking, and the breakdown row 'Value-matched assets +12.0' (InsiderLeads.jsx:47) reads to the user as a discovered fact about that specific manager when it is true of everyone.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: The lead score has no error rate, no calibration and no disclosed reachable range, while rendering a no-evidence manager as an amber 33/100
findings.evidence: All five weights and both penalty caps are hand-picked literals (src/intel/leads.py:68-79) with no calibration artifact anywhere: no backtest script, no holdout, no config under config/. Verified score behaviour with ZERO demonstrated interest (the common case — the payload itself reports `leadsWithObservedInterest`, lead_service.py:179): a manager whose top positional gap happens to be the asset's position scores 33.1; a secondary gap scores 21.1; no gap at all scores 15.1. InsiderLeads.jsx:52-56 `scoreColor` renders >= 30 as `var(--amber)` and ScoreBar (:58-86) fills a bar as a percentage of 100. The verified reachable maximum with every term maxed is 80.7. `describe_limitations()` (leads.py:395-419) states 'not a probability' and a coverage caveat, but never states an error rate, a reachable range, or that a score in the 15-33 band can be produced with no observed evidence about the asset at all. Contrast: this repo ships docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md + scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py for the league-adjusted board, and the same module goes to the trouble of normalising partner fit against ITS reachable max (leads.py:349).
findings.userImpact: A number that ranks the people a user is about to negotiate with is presented on an implied 0-100 scale, coloured amber at 33, with no statement of what a good score is or how often the ranking is right. Because the two terms that fire without any evidence (valueMatch, saturated at 12; positionalNeed, ordinal) sum to 30 before any real signal, the display cannot distinguish 'this manager wants him' from 'this manager exists and has a roster'.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: The component breakdown does not reconcile with the displayed score whenever the zero floor bites
findings.evidence: src/intel/leads.py:361 `total = max(0.0, total - contradiction - low_sample)` clamps, but :364-372 writes the UNCLAMPED components including the negative penalties. Verified: for `buys=0, sells=2` in sell mode, `score = 0.0` while `components` = {demonstratedInterest 0.0, contradictionPenalty -0.20, lowSamplePenalty -0.048} — a sum of -0.248. For a manager with no data at all, `score = 0.0` with `lowSamplePenalty = -0.12`. frontend/components/InsiderLeads.jsx:88-118 renders every component x100 as an audit breakdown of that score.
findings.userImpact: Expanding a 0.0-scored lead shows rows totalling -24.8, which no reader can reconcile with the 0.0 headline. The expander is explicitly labelled 'Score breakdown' and is the feature's transparency mechanism, so an unreconcilable breakdown undermines the one thing it exists to provide.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: The board page claims it shows trades made in 'OTHER Sleeper leagues' but the board applies no home-league exclusion
findings.evidence: frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx:481 renders the subtitle `Trades your league-mates made in their OTHER Sleeper leagues — ...`. src/intel/service.py:541-548 calls `ledger.asset_signals(since_ms=..., until_ms=..., tx_types=..., user_ids=pool, ...)` with no league exclusion, and `asset_signals` has no `exclude_league_ids` parameter at all (ledger.py:702-712). By contrast the LEADS path does exclude it — lead_service.py:127 passes `exclude_league_ids=home_league_ids`, and ledger.manager_asset_activity supports it (ledger.py:862, 889-891), with the reason spelled out at lead_service.py:52-56 and pinned by tests/intel/test_lead_service.py::TestHomeLeagueExclusion.
findings.userImpact: Home-league trades are counted on the board. Per AUDIT.md §3 both counterparties in a home-league trade are always tracked, so those movements contribute volume, manager counts and league counts while netting to exactly zero — inflating the confidence tier and the volume column for assets whose only activity was inside the user's own league, which the user already knows about and which the page promises is excluded.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: The contradiction penalty's asymmetry is a no-op ternary — the stated intent is never implemented
findings.evidence: src/intel/leads.py:209-211 — `# A manager who both bought and sold him is genuinely ambiguous; / # one who ONLY moved him against us is a negative lead. / return MAX_CONTRADICTION_PENALTY * share * (1.0 if wanted else 1.0)`. Both branches of the ternary are `1.0`. Verified: `buys=0, sells=2` (only adverse) and `buys=2, sells=2` (genuinely ambiguous) are penalised by the share ratio alone with no additional weighting.
findings.userImpact: A manager who has only ever moved the asset AWAY is treated identically to one who has been on both sides, contradicting the module's own stated model. Combined with `demonstrated_interest` returning early at leads.py:168-169 (before building cautions) when `wanted <= 0`, such a manager renders with no reason AND no caution — the adverse evidence is silently absorbed by the max(0,.) floor and never shown.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: The FAAB rival-bid intel index reproduces defect D1 (waiver adds counted as trade adds) and silently crosses leagues
findings.evidence: src/trade/faab_contention.py:169-171 filters only on `if e.get("action") != "add": continue` and `if str(e.get("assetType") or "player") != "player": continue`. There is no `txType` check, although the crawler stamps it on every event (src/intel/crawler.py:307) and docs/intel/AUDIT.md D1 records exactly this omission as the headline defect, marked 'Fixed'. There is also no `leagueId` check anywhere in the function, and the snapshot's `events` list spans every league the crawl reached. The output feeds `intel_factor` -> 1.25/1.10 multipliers -> `exp_bid` (faab_contention.py:398-401) -> the recommended clearing bid.
findings.userImpact: A rival's estimated FAAB bid is raised 25% because they acquired that player in a TRADE (in a different league), which is not evidence they will bid on him on waivers here. The 1.10 position-level factor fires on any positional add anywhere in the last 14 days. The result is a dollar figure the user spends real budget against, built on cross-league evidence of a different transaction type, with the mechanism undocumented in the module's own docstring (which says only 'this owner added THIS player in another league recently').

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: The player drill-down is hardcoded to the 30d window and its movement receipts cannot audit the 90d counts
findings.evidence: src/intel/service.py:665-677 fetches `per_member` and `movements` using `signals.window_bounds(signals.INSIDER_DEFAULT_WINDOW, now_ms)` (30d) with `limit=100`, while `window_names = list(signals.INSIDER_WINDOWS)` (:647) renders 7d/30d/90d counts; `payload['window']` is hardcoded to the default at :751. server.py:12328-12371 (get_intel_player) accepts no `window` parameter. The board's drill-down fetch (page.jsx:143-145) sends only `playerId` and `leagueKey`, so switching the board to 90d leaves the drill-down showing '30d'. docs/intel/METRICS.md §'Time windows' claims 'a drill-down transaction list lets any number be audited back to its movements.'
findings.userImpact: A user who selects the 90-day board window and clicks a row sees member-exposure counts and a movement list scoped to 30 days, labelled 30d, next to 90d aggregates that cannot be reconciled from the receipts shown. The auditability guarantee METRICS.md advertises does not hold for two of the three windows.

findings.title: ledger.coverage() exists and is documented as the honesty mechanism, but no /api/intel/* route serves it
findings.evidence: src/intel/ledger.py:974-1018 builds a coverage block (earliest/latest observation, movement/league/manager/transaction counts, movementsByTxType, retentionDays, `complete: false`, and a coverageNote). docs/intel/METRICS.md §'Coverage honesty' presents it as how the products avoid implying global Sleeper coverage. `grep -rn 'coverage()' --include=*.py .` shows the only callers are src/sharp/service.py:60 and scripts/migrate_intel_ledger.py:97 — no /api/intel/* handler and no intel service function calls it (`grep -n coverage src/intel/service.py src/intel/lead_service.py` returns nothing). The leads payload carries only a prose `limitations.coverageCaveat` (leads.py:414-418) with no numbers.
findings.userImpact: The Insider Trading board, drill-down, member profile and lead list all present counts with no statement of how many leagues, managers or days of history actually back them. A user cannot tell whether '0 buys observed' means the manager doesn't want the player or that the crawl only reached two of their nine leagues — which is precisely the distinction the coverage block exists to make and which `describe_limitations` verbally warns about while withholding the numbers.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: No intel data store exists in this checkout — the entire subsystem is unverifiable against live inputs
findings.evidence: `ls data/intel/` -> 'No such file or directory'. `find . -name '*.sqlite3*' -o -name 'snapshot_*.json'` (excluding node_modules) returns nothing. `data/` contains adamidp_normalized.json, comparison, identity, idp_fit_snapshots, legacy_data_2026-03-22.json, player_map, raw, raw_sources, ros, scrape_state, snapshots — no intel. `grep -n intel .gitignore` returns nothing, so the directory is not explicitly ignored; per CLAUDE.md most of data/ is gitignored, so absence here is consistent with a checkout artifact rather than proof of an empty production store.
findings.userImpact: Not Verifiable from Repository whether the ledger has ever been populated, how many leagues/managers/movements it holds, or how fresh it is. Every count, signal and lead score in this subsystem is therefore validated only against synthetic test fixtures. The 400-day retention, the 90d window's answerability, and the claim that the crawl reaches ~150 leagues for a 12-member pool (crawler.py:16-19) are all unverified assertions here.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md documents none of src/intel/ — a ~6,300-line subsystem with seven routes and a daily cron
findings.evidence: `grep -c 'src/intel|api/intel|insider' CLAUDE.md` returns 0. CLAUDE.md's `src/` tree lists adapters, api, bdvm, canonical, identity, league_intel, model_registry, scoring, league, trade, data_models, utils — while `ls src/` shows 26 packages including intel, sharp, roster_intel, platforms, public_league, playerctx, news, nfl_data, pool, backtesting, league_comparison, maintenance, ros. findings.userImpact: The repository's primary orientation document gives no indication this subsystem exists, so a change to `_resolve_league_for_request`, `latest_contract_data`, `league_registry`, or the playersArray schema can break five intel endpoints with nothing in CLAUDE.md pointing at them. The intel routes' 503 `data_not_ready` semantics also differ from the table CLAUDE.md publishes for other league-scoped endpoints and are documented nowhere central.

findings.title: server.py's intel section header still documents the retired trendScore sort

findings.title: signalStrength, velocity, and two of the six allow-listed sorts are computed and shipped but never rendered
findings.evidence: server.py:11972 — `_INTEL_ALLOWED_SORTS = ("net", "volume", "buys", "sells", "strength", "velocity")`. frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx:33-38 offers only net/volume/buys/sells. `grep -rn 'signalStrength|velocity' frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx frontend/components/InsiderLeads.jsx` returns nothing — neither field is displayed. findings.title: Two of the seven intel routes have no consumer of any kind

Frontend intel consumers are exactly: `/api/intel/summary` (page.jsx:409), `/api/intel/player` (page.jsx:145, PlayerPopup.jsx:202) and `/api/intel/leads` (InsiderLeads.jsx:260).
findings.userImpact: The waiver-interest endpoint exists to give waiver churn its own honest label so it can never render as a trade buy — but nothing renders it, so waiver activity is collected, stored and never shown. The member profile (a manager's cross-league footprint) is likewise unreachable from the UI.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: AUDIT.md defect D10 (movement_id embeds the attributed owner) remains open in code as documented
findings.evidence: src/intel/crawler.py:290 — `event_id = f"{tx_id}:{owner}:{action}:{asset_id}"` where `owner` comes from `rid_to_owner` (crawler.py:287), which is rebuilt each run from live /rosters and prefers a pool co-owner over the primary owner (crawler.py:157-166). That eventId becomes the ledger's `movement_id` PRIMARY KEY (ledger.py:39-48). docs/intel/AUDIT.md:134 and §7 record this as 'Open' with the reason stated. No fix is present.
findings.userImpact: If co-ownership changes on an already-crawled transaction, the same underlying movement re-keys and is inserted a second time, permanently double-counting that manager's buys/sells for that asset. Narrow (requires a co-ownership change) but silent and unrecoverable without a re-key pass. Correctly disclosed by the audit doc — reported here as confirmation, not as a new claim.

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: Partner fit is normalised by its reachable maximum but not offset by its reachable minimum
findings.evidence: src/intel/leads.py:349-350 — `reachable_max = getattr(partner_model, "FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MAX", 50.0) or 50.0; fit_score = max(0.0, min(1.0, (fit_raw or 0.0) / reachable_max))`. Computed live: `FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MIN = 7.24`, `FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MAX = 43.12` (src/roster_intel/partner.py:573). Both bounds are exported; only the max is used.
findings.userImpact: A partner assessed at the worst attainable fit contributes 7.24/43.12 x 0.26 = 0.0437, i.e. 4.4 display points, on every lead where a roster snapshot exists. Since that applies uniformly, it inflates the whole board rather than distorting the order — but it means 'terrible fit' and 'no fit computed' differ by 4.4 points in the wrong direction (no assessment scores 0.0, a bad assessment scores 4.4).

findings.area: src/intel/ — Insider Trading (league-scoped Sleeper league-mate intelligence): crawler → JSON snapshot → SQLite ledger → /api/intel/* (summary, player, member,
findings.title: The sample-confidence docstring's stated calibration does not match its constant
findings.evidence: src/intel/signals.py:67-69 — 'Volume at which sample-size confidence reaches ~0.5. Tuned so a single observation is visibly weak (~0.09) and a dozen is strong (~0.86)... _CONFIDENCE_HALF_VOLUME = 5.0'. Computed: `sample_confidence(1) = 1/6 = 0.1667` and `sample_confidence(12) = 12/17 = 0.7059`. The quoted 0.09 and 0.86 correspond to a half-volume near 10, not 5.
findings.userImpact: None directly — the values are not user-facing. But the comment is the only stated justification for the constant, and it describes a different constant, so anyone re-tuning it would be reasoning from a wrong baseline.

findings.area: Roster & Trade Intelligence (src/roster_intel/), Terminal aggregation (src/api/terminal.py + GET /api/terminal), Gameplan API (src/api/gameplan.py + GET /api/ga
findings.title: Two shipped systems give the SAME team opposite contention labels: /phases says "Win-now", /api/gameplan says "rebuild"
findings.evidence: Owner 831633191830933504 ("Collin"). Backend: `src/roster_intel/window.py:league_competitiveness` (lines ~300-330) takes the championship-odds percentile; measured live run → `comp=0.188, mostLikely='rebuild', confidence=0.388` while `lineup_score=673.0` (4th-highest of 12). Frontend: `frontend/lib/team-phase.js:83-90` `if (isHighValue && isYounger) return PHASES.WIN_NOW;` — measured live: Collin top-25 value 95,993 vs league median 91,579.5 (high) and median age 25 vs league 26 (younger) → **Win-now**. Both are reachable to the same signed-in user; neither cites the other.
findings.userImpact: A manager reading /phases is told to buy win-now talent; the same platform's gameplan engine classifies them as a rebuild and its partner model uses that to pick counterparties. There is no CONFLICT state and no reconciliation — whichever page they open last wins.

findings.area: Roster & Trade Intelligence (src/roster_intel/), Terminal aggregation (src/api/terminal.py + GET /api/terminal), Gameplan API (src/api/gameplan.py + GET /api/ga
findings.title: Competitive window ranks 8 of 12 rosters on one scale and 4 on an incomparable other, then presents both in one five-state vocabulary
findings.evidence: `data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json` contains 8 rows for a 12-team league (verified: `len(playoffOdds)==8`; missing ownerIds `{1208452010173538304, 1002085133723299840, 1303549304882892800, 712035316776669184}`). `src/roster_intel/window.py:league_competitiveness` percentiles championshipOdds *over the rows it was given* (`below/ties over len(champ)`), else falls back to `lineupScoreRank` over all 12. Measured live: `1002085133723299840` → comp 0.958 via lineupScoreRank → `championship_contender`; `472206636534984704` → playoffOdds 1.0 but championshipOdds 0.0 → comp 0.188 → `rebuild`. `src/api/gameplan.py:520-536` emits a note about this but `_league_summary` (gameplan.py:757-800) still sorts all 12 together and stamps `mostLikely` on each.
findings.userImpact: A team certain to make the playoffs (playoffOdds 1.0) is labelled `rebuild`. A team with no simulation at all is labelled `championship_contender` on lineup rank alone. Cross-team comparison — the only thing a 12-row table invites — is invalid, and the payload's own note is the only place that says so.

findings.area: Roster & Trade Intelligence (src/roster_intel/), Terminal aggregation (src/api/terminal.py + GET /api/terminal), Gameplan API (src/api/gameplan.py + GET /api/ga
findings.title: Championship odds are degenerate: 4 of 8 simulated teams are exactly 0.0 and tie at the same percentile, collapsing three different rosters onto one label
findings.evidence: `data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json`: championshipOdds = [0.3815, 0.3185, 0.0, 0.001, 0.2955, 0.0035, 0.0, 0.0]; six of eight rows carry playoffOdds exactly 1.0 and two carry 0.0 with `playoffSeeds: 6`, `n_simulations: 2000`, `converged: true`. The three 0.0 rows tie → `pct = (0 + 0.5*3)/8 = 0.1875` for all three. Verified live: owners 831633191830933504 (lineupScore 673.0), 711452264774041600 (553.1) and 472206636534984704 (486.7) all receive comp 0.188 and all label `rebuild`.
findings.userImpact: A 186-point spread in lineup strength is flattened to one identical label. `playoffOdds` carries zero information (6/8 are 1.0) so the only discriminating field is championshipOdds, and half of it is a floor.

findings.area: Roster & Trade Intelligence (src/roster_intel/), Terminal aggregation (src/api/terminal.py + GET /api/terminal), Gameplan API (src/api/gameplan.py + GET /api/ga
findings.title: tradePartnerFitScore ships a reachable range of [7.24, 43.12] that is unreachable through the only wiring that serves it; measured live ceiling is 16.37
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/partner.py:536-573` `_reachable_fit_bounds()` derives the published bounds assuming `max_conf=0.40` (HISTORY_INFORMED) and full 3/3 structural coverage. `src/api/gameplan.py:915-926` constructs `PartnerInputs` with **no** `shape`, no `trades_completed`, no `league_mean_trades`, no `pair_trades_completed` → `_fairness_term` and `_history_term` both abstain → tier is SHAPE_ONLY (0.30), `measured = 2/3` → `confidence = 0.30 * (0.55 + 0.45*0.6667) = 0.2550` for every partner, always. Measured live (real 12-team bundle, owner 468418790212759552): all 11 partners have `acceptanceConfidence == 0.255` exactly, and fit scores span 10.48 … 16.37 against the shipped `tradePartnerFitScoreRange` of `{min: 7.24, max: 43.12}`.
findings.userImpact: The bounds were added specifically so a renderer would not draw a good partner as a failing grade — and under the real wiring the best partner draws at 38% of the shipped gauge. `acceptanceConfidence` is a constant wearing a score's clothes: it varies with nothing.

findings.title: waiver_scarcity is structurally always None — the scarcity multiplier and the SCARCITY corroborator are dead everywhere, while the payload advertises scarcity as a live corroborator
findings.evidence: `src/league_intel/replacement.py:452-465` only populates the `waiver` tier from the `free_agents` argument; `waiver_scarcity=_safe_drop(best_ball, waiver)` (line 657). `grep -rn free_agents src/ scripts/ server.py` returns **only the definition** — no caller anywhere supplies it. `src/api/gameplan.py:490` calls `compute_replacement_levels(rep_teams, slots, endogenous=endogenous)`. Measured live: every ScarcityComponents has `'waiverScarcity': None`. Consequently `src/roster_intel/targets.py:468-471` returns `1.0, "no scarcity data — position scarcity multiplier inert"` on every position, and `targets.py:804-807` (`ValueSignal.SCARCITY`) can never fire. Yet `src/api/gameplan.py:855-861` tells the consumer "the only admissible corroborators are measured lineup fit and positional scarcity".
findings.userImpact: Half the advertised corroboration gate does not exist. Every one of the 6 recommended targets on the live run carries `signals: ["rosterFit"]` — the gate is single-signal in practice, which is exactly the "model agreeing with itself" failure the gate was written to prevent.

findings.area: Roster & Trade Intelligence (src/roster_intel/), Terminal aggregation (src/api/terminal.py + GET /api/terminal), Gameplan API (src/api/gameplan.py + GET /api/ga
findings.title: Target-position confidence credits scarcity as "supplied" when the scarcity term abstained, inflating every confidence by 0.15
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/targets.py:658-665`: `supplied = sum(... (scarcity or {}).get(pos) is not None ...)`. The object is present for all 8 positions but the only field consumed — `waiver_scarcity` — is None (see prior finding), so `_scarcity_multiplier` returns the abstention note. Measured live: RB target confidence = 0.85 (`0.40 + 0.15*3`) where the honest value is 0.70. The module's own comment two lines above says "a defaulted input is an abstention and must cost confidence rather than pass silently."
findings.userImpact: Priority scores are 21% higher than the evidence supports, and the confidence field — the thing a reader would use to discount them — is the field that is wrong.

findings.area: Roster & Trade Intelligence (src/roster_intel/), Terminal aggregation (src/api/terminal.py + GET /api/terminal), Gameplan API (src/api/gameplan.py + GET /api/ga
findings.title: Every differentiating multiplier in both target engines is 1.0 under the live wiring; `priority` is a constant rescale of lineup gain
findings.evidence: `targets.py:698` `priority = realistic * window_mult * scar_mult * eff_mult * confidence`. Measured live (owner 468418790212759552, real contract with 661/666 ages): RB is the only viable position, `realisticGain 15.08 × winNowWeight 0.8755 × scarcityMultiplier 1.0 × eff_mult 1.0 × confidence 0.85 = 11.222` — matches the emitted `priority` exactly. `eff_mult` is 1.0 because `market_prices` is deliberately never supplied (`gameplan.py:945` comment). `scar_mult` is 1.0 always (prior finding). For players, `targets.py:866-869`: `edge_mult = 1.0` (edge None), `avail_mult = 0.7 + 0.6*0.5 = 1.0` (avail None), `scar_mult = 1.0`, `confidence = 0.35 + 0.15*1 = 0.5` → measured: travis etienne gain 16.18 → priority 8.09 = gain/2 exactly, for all 6 recommendations.
findings.userImpact: `priority` reads as a composite score that weighed scarcity, market efficiency, availability and the competitive window. It is `lineupGain × 0.5` for players and `realisticGain × 0.85 × horizonWeight` for positions. Ordering by priority and ordering by raw gain are the same list.

findings.title: `_position_severity` computes fragility × marginal_points — the exact product `engine.py`'s docstring documents as producing the QB inversion
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/targets.py:474-486`: `return max(0.0, float(profile.fragility)) * max(0.0, float(profile.marginal_points))`, docstringed "Current cost of the weakness". `src/roster_intel/engine.py:22-40` states: "A consuming agent derived 'deficit' as fragility x marginal and got QB reported as the biggest need on a QB-STRONG roster… Multiplying those reports the roster's greatest STRENGTH as its greatest need." `targets.py:719-721` sorts every non-viable position by `-severity`, so it is what orders the "biggest unfixable weakness" list. Measured live (owner 468418790212759552): WR fragility 0.2143 × marginal 156.6 = 33.6 — the highest severity on the roster — while WR's actual deficit is 0.0 and its contribution (156.6) is more than double its replacement level (76.6).
findings.userImpact: The non-viable target list is headed by the roster's strongest position, presented as its costliest weakness. Two modules in one package hold contradictory definitions of the same quantity.

findings.title: The `elite` tier is unreachable for every player on every roster — `analyze_roster` never forwards `league_position_values`
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/profiles.py:build_position_profiles` computes `elite_cut = elite_threshold((league_position_values or {}).get(pos, ()))` and `classify_tier` ignores `elite` when it is None. `src/roster_intel/engine.py:analyze_roster` calls `build_position_profiles(pool_list, slots_list, replacement=..., player_meta=..., marginals=marg)` — the `league_position_values` parameter is never passed, and `analyze_roster` has no parameter to accept it. Measured live over all 12 rosters × 8 positions: **total elite-tier players = 0**. Every `tierCounts` reads `{'elite': 0, 'starter': n, 'depth': m, 'developmental': k}`.
findings.userImpact: A four-tier ladder that can only produce three tiers. The docstring's careful explanation of the elite promotion rule describes behaviour that never runs.

findings.area: Roster & Trade Intelligence (src/roster_intel/), Terminal aggregation (src/api/terminal.py + GET /api/terminal), Gameplan API (src/api/gameplan.py + GET /api/ga
findings.title: trend7 and trend30 are the same number whenever the rank-history log is shallower than 7 days, making the SELL rule's "sustained" qualifier vacuous
findings.evidence: `src/api/terminal.py:_window_trend` (lines ~332-343): `baseline` is the FIRST point with `t >= cutoff` — i.e. the oldest point in the log when the log is shorter than the window — and returns `baseline.rank - latest.rank`. So for any series spanning fewer than 7 days, `_window_trend(points,7) == _window_trend(points,30)`. `terminal.py:588-593` states the log is "currently ~2 days deep". The SELL rule (`terminal.py`, priority 80) is `trend7 <= -3 and trend30 is not None and trend30 <= 0`; with equal trends it degenerates to `trend7 <= -3`. SELL is in `signal_alerts.ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS` — it emails.
findings.userImpact: A player who dropped 3 ranks on a single scrape gets an emailed SELL described as "7d trend -3 continues a 30d trend of -3", stating a 30-day fact the data cannot support. The chip labelled "30d" on `BuySellHold.jsx` shows a 2-day number.

findings.title: Buy-low card is named and described as "short drop, long steady" but neither implementation tests any long-term trend
findings.evidence: `src/api/terminal.py:1105-1133`: the only tests are `rank <= 150`, `value >= 3000`, and `rc = _row_rank_change(r); if rc is None or rc > -3: continue` — `rankChange` is the delta from the *last scrape*, not a 7d or 30d trend. Emitted as `"metric": "short_drop_long_steady"`. `frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:452-455` carries the comment "7d trend ≤ -3 (dipped), 30d trend still ≥ 0 (long-term fine)" above code that filters on `Number(r.rankChange)` only. findings.title: The two Buy/Sell/Hold engines share a pinned rule table but consume divergent inputs, and only the Python side emails
findings.evidence: `tests/api/test_signal_engine_parity.py:41-56` explicitly states it pins the RULE TABLE only and lists the known builder divergences. Concretely: (a) `src/api/terminal.py::_row_value` falls back to `rank_to_value_for_scope(rank, scope)` when both value fields are absent, while `signal-engine.js::buildContext` uses `Number(row?.rankDerivedValue || row?.values?.full || 0)` with no fallback — this changes the `elite_stable` `value >= 7000` test; (b) `terminal.py::_history_lookup` (lines ~366-393) builds `lower_base` with `setdefault`, so a display name spanning two asset classes resolves to whichever key was iterated first, while `frontend/lib/value-history.js:297-302` returns `[]` on the same collision (`if ((nameVariantCount.get(lowered) || 0) > 1) return []`).
findings.userImpact: Divergent trend inputs produce divergent verdicts from identical rules. The Python verdict is the one fed to `signal_alerts.process_user_alerts` (ACTIONABLE = RISK/SELL/BUY/MONITOR), so the failure mode is "you were emailed a SELL the Signals panel does not show". Measured mitigation: 0 display names currently span more than one assetClass on the live board (550 offense / 398 idp / 144 pick), so (b) is latent today.

findings.title: team-phase classification is a forced median quota with no absolute anchor and no hysteresis; on live data zero teams classify as Rebuild
findings.evidence: `frontend/lib/team-phase.js:83-90` classifies on `totalValue > leagueMedians.value` and `medianAge < leagueMedians.age`, both medians taken over the same 12 snapshots — so exactly 6 teams are "high value" by construction regardless of league quality. Reproduced on the live contract + live rosters: medians value 91,579.5, age 26.0 → **5 Win-now, 1 Contender, 6 Mixed, 0 Rebuild**. Ages are integers so 4 of 12 teams sit exactly at median age 26.0; `isYounger` uses strict `<` (line 80) so ties are silently pushed to "older". Margins are thin: Collin +4,414 on 95,993 (4.6%) and Ed −4,414 — a ~5% board move swaps both labels, and there is no hysteresis or confidence field anywhere in the module.
findings.userImpact: A page titled "Win-now vs Rebuild" never says Rebuild. Half the league is labelled by a coin-flip on the age axis. The classification flips on ordinary scrape noise with no indication that it was close.

findings.title: team-phase label vocabulary is inverted relative to the quadrant it names — an old, weak roster is called "Mixed", a young, strong one "Win-now"
findings.evidence: `frontend/lib/team-phase.js:83-90`: `high value × younger → WIN_NOW`, `high value × older → CONTENDER`, `low value × younger → REBUILD`, `low value × older → MIXED`. Live: "Kich", top-25 value 76,514 (10th of 12) with median age 29 — the oldest roster in the league and near the bottom on value, i.e. the textbook rebuild — is classified **Mixed** (tone `warn`). "Brent", the highest-value roster in the league (136,198), is classified **Contender** — the second-tier label — because its median age is 27. The header text `TeamPhasePanel.jsx:88-91` presents this as "classified by top-25 roster value × median age" with no legend explaining the mapping.
findings.userImpact: The label a manager acts on points the wrong way for the two quadrants that most need clear advice.

findings.title: Client `normalizePos` omits 7 IDP aliases the server maps, silently dropping those players' value from the positional stack while keeping it in the total
findings.evidence: `frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:57-62` maps only DB/LB/DL/DE/DT/CB/S → "IDP". `src/api/terminal.py:_normalize_pos` (lines ~84-101) additionally maps EDGE, NT, OLB, ILB, MLB, FS, SS. findings.area: Roster & Trade Intelligence (src/roster_intel/), Terminal aggregation (src/api/terminal.py + GET /api/terminal), Gameplan API (src/api/gameplan.py + GET /api/ga
findings.title: `urgent_need` and `RosterSignal.deficit` are structurally blind to 3 of the league's 21 starter slots
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/profiles.py::_required_slots` skips FLEX / SUPER_FLEX / IDP_FLEX / BN by design (the comment cites LI-5 endogeneity). The live league's slots are `('QB','RB','RB','WR','WR','WR','TE','TE','FLEX','FLEX','SUPER_FLEX','K','DL','DL','DL','LB','LB','LB','DB','DB','DB')` — 18 attributed, 3 (2×FLEX + SUPER_FLEX, 14%) unattributed. Measured live: every team reports QB `required_slots = 1` and `urgent_need = False` despite this being a superflex league where a second startable QB is the dominant structural need. Separately `_URGENT_FRAGILITY = 0.75` (profiles.py) is cleared by essentially nothing: measured max QB fragility across 12 rosters is 0.707; the only position hitting 1.0 is K (one kicker rostered).
findings.userImpact: The need model cannot see a superflex hole, and its second trigger (fragility ≥ 0.75) fires almost exclusively on kickers. `urgent_need` is therefore close to a kicker detector.

findings.area: Roster & Trade Intelligence (src/roster_intel/), Terminal aggregation (src/api/terminal.py + GET /api/terminal), Gameplan API (src/api/gameplan.py + GET /api/ga
findings.title: `rank_history.jsonl` and `source_value_history.jsonl` are absent from the repository; every trend, volatility, signal and delta in the terminal is unverifiable offline
findings.evidence: `src/api/rank_history.py:74` `HISTORY_PATH = <repo>/data/rank_history.jsonl` and `src/api/source_history.py:49` `HISTORY_PATH = <repo>/data/source_value_history.jsonl` — neither file exists in this checkout (`ls data/*.jsonl` → no such file). They are written at runtime by `server.py:1868 _rank_history.append_snapshot(contract_payload)`, one entry per UTC date, retention `MAX_SNAPSHOTS = 365*3`. With no file, `_history_lookup` returns `[]` for every name → `trend7 = trend30 = None`, `_volatility = None`, every signal is HOLD/`default_hold`, every `delta*d` is None with `reason: "low_history_coverage"`, and `biggestRisk` / `tradeChip` return null.
findings.userImpact: None of the signal, volatility, trend or delta numbers can be validated from the repository. The depth of the production log (terminal.py's own comment says "~2 days") is Not Verifiable from Repository, which is what makes the trend-window finding above severe rather than theoretical.

findings.title: Playoff and championship "odds" are structurally degenerate out of season — every team is 100% or 0%, cached and served as current
findings.evidence: `src/ros/playoff_sim.py:704` `schedule = _remaining_schedule(snapshot)` returns [] when the last loaded season is complete (offseason). The sim loop at `:721` then adds nothing to `sim_wins`, which was seeded from realized wins at `:719`, so every one of the 2,000 draws produces the identical ranking. Live output `data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json`: `{'n_simulations': 2000, 'converged': True, 'worstPlayoffOddsSe': 0.0}` with `playoffOdds` exactly 1.0 for six owners and 0.0 for two, and `expectedWins` at integer values 6.0/7.0/9.0/11.0 (no fractional part = zero simulated games). Same in `data/ros/sims/dynasty_new_playoff.json`. `computedAt: 2026-08-04T03:57:31` — the file is 4 hours old and the numbers are last season's final standings. There is no preseason guard anywhere in `playoff_sim.py` or `championship.py`; `power_v2.py:195-223` has one (`_is_preseason`), so the codebase knows the state exists and only one of three consumers handles it.
findings.userImpact: Every ROS contender surface (/league → Championship, /league → Trade Deadline, the ROS Fit panel on /trade) shows fabricated certainty: six teams at a 100% playoff chance and the rest at 0%, in August, before a single 2026 game. `converged: true` and a Wilson CI of [1.0, 1.0] actively assert the number is trustworthy.

Executing `build_team_directions()` against the committed data on disk returns: `Brent | po 0.0 | co 0.0 | pct 1.0 | Seller` — Brent is ranked #1 of 12 on `teamRosStrength` (646.85, next best 536.79) and is told to sell. findings.title: Rank scores are normalized against each source's own board size, so an IDP-only board and a 978-player board are blended as if commensurable
findings.evidence: `src/ros/parse.py:43-46` `rank_to_score` divides by `ln(total_ranked + 1)`, where `total_ranked` is whatever the source published. `aggregate.py:181` scores every row this way and `:230` takes a plain weighted mean across sources. Live consequence for Aidan Hutchinson in `data/ros/aggregate/latest.json`: `draftSharksRosSf rank 98 of 978 → score 33.42`; `fantasyProsRosIdp rank 1 of 219 → score 100.00` — a 2.99x disagreement produced entirely by board size, for the same player from two boards that both contain him. Reproduced numerically: `(33.42*1.375 + 100.00*0.9371)/(1.375+0.9371) = 60.41`, matching the file exactly. Result: Hutchinson sits at `rosRankOverall: 13`, above Ja'Marr Chase (67.07), Lamar Jackson (64.26) and Christian McCaffrey (65.54). Position counts in the aggregate top 50: LB 7, DL 3 — ten IDP in the top 50 of a board whose only IDP source ranks 219 players. `confidence` does not protect against this: it computes to 0.425 for Hutchinson (`0.45*0.5 + 0.35*max(0, 1-33.289/30) + 0.20` — the agreement term floors at 0), and nothing downstream gates on confidence.
findings.userImpact: `teamRosStrength` sums these values over the optimal lineup (`team_strength.py:157`), so a roster of top-of-the-IDP-board defenders scores like a roster of elite offense. That composite sets the projected reverse-standings draft order behind the Pick Projector (`pick_projection.py:112`), the ROS Power v2 top component (`power_v2.py:66`, weight 0.38), and the playoff-sim mean shift (`playoff_sim.py:523`). The distortion propagates to every ROS decision surface.

findings.title: fantasyProsRosIdp stamps total_ranked as its row count while rank comes from a larger board — 13 IDP players silently score 0 and vanish
findings.evidence: `src/ros/sources/fantasypros_ros_idp.py:44` reads `rank_field = raw.get("rank") or raw.get("Rank") or raw.get("effectiveRank")`. `CSVs/site_raw/fantasyProsIdp.csv` has no `rank`/`Rank` column (header: `name,originalRank,effectiveRank,derivationMethod,family,normalizedValue,matchedSourceName,position,team`), so it always takes `effectiveRank`, which runs to 362. Line `:75-77` then sets `total_ranked = n` where `n = len(rows) = 219`. `parse.py:41-42` returns 0.0 when `r > n`, and `aggregate.py:182-183` `if score <= 0: continue` drops the row without a log line. Measured on the committed data: `data/ros/sources/fantasyProsRosIdp.csv` has 218 distinct names but only 205 appear as `fantasyProsRosIdp` contributors in `data/ros/aggregate/latest.json`. The 13 dropped are all rank > 219: bobby okereke (350), bobby wagner (288), drue tranquill (344), germaine pratt (362), trenton simpson (282). `rank_to_score(288, 219) = 0.0`, verified.
findings.userImpact: Bobby Wagner appears verbatim in `data/ros/team_strength/latest.json` under Brent's `unmappedPlayers` — the UI tells the user "no ROS source ranked this player" when a source did rank him and the arithmetic threw it away. Those players contribute exactly 0.0 to `teamRosStrength` (`team_strength.py:123`), biasing the composite and the draft-order projection built on it. Every surviving IDP score is also normalized against 219 instead of the real ~362 board, inflating them.

findings.title: Non-default league sims read the DEFAULT league's team-strength file, apply zero ROS blend, and still stamp rosStrengthAvailable: true
findings.evidence: `src/ros/playoff_sim.py:423`, `:277` and `:191` all hardcode `path = ROS_DATA_DIR / "team_strength" / "latest.json"` — the default league's file — with no `league_key` parameter, while `scrape.py:402-403` iterates `active_leagues()` and calls the sim for each. `:520-523` then does `ros_score = ros_strength_map.get(owner_id)`; when the owner isn't in the default league's map the blend is skipped. Measured: `data/ros/sims/dynasty_new_playoff.json` has 8 owners, of whom 0 appear in `data/ros/team_strength/latest.json` (12 dynasty_main owners) and only 3 appear in `data/ros/team_strength/dynasty_new.json`. Yet `:818` stamps `"rosStrengthAvailable": bool(ros_map)` — True, because the default file exists — and the file records `rosStrengthAvailable: true`. `_load_team_depth_ratios` and `_load_team_rosters` have the same hardcoded path, so a best-ball non-default league would presim the wrong rosters entirely.
findings.userImpact: A ROS-branded playoff projection for a second league is not ROS-influenced at all, and the payload asserts the opposite. Per CLAUDE.md's leagueKey rule this is exactly the cross-league collapse the architecture forbids.

findings.title: Adapter failure does NOT keep last-known-good values in the aggregate; the doc, the CI comment and the test docstring all claim it does
findings.evidence: `scrape.py:588` `snapshots.append(_build_snapshot(src, result))` builds the snapshot from `result.rows` — the in-memory adapter return — and `_build_snapshot:412-426` never reads a CSV. `aggregate.py:129-130` `if not snap.rows: continue` then skips the source outright, so `has_valid_cache` and the 0.5 `availability_multiplier` (`parse.py:158-166`) are unreachable when rows are empty, which is the only state a failure produces. Claims to the contrary: `scrape.py:13-16` "the previous CSV stays on disk so the aggregate keeps the last-known-good values"; `docs/ros-engine.md` "The previous CSV is never deleted... so the aggregate continues with last-known-good values. `tests/ros/test_scrape_failure_resilience.py` pins this guarantee"; `.github/workflows/scheduled-refresh.yml:423` "orchestrator keeps yesterday's CSV per source". Opening the named test: it has two cases, `test_existing_csv_preserved_when_adapter_returns_no_rows` and `test_has_valid_cache_reports_correct_state`, which call `_write_csv` and `_has_valid_cache` directly. Neither invokes `run_all` or `aggregate`, and neither asserts anything about aggregate output.
findings.userImpact: If DraftSharks (1.375 effective weight, ~34% of an offense player's blend) fails one cycle, every player it uniquely ranked drops out of `rosValue` entirely rather than holding yesterday's number, and `staleFlag` stays false so nothing warns. Operators reading the doc will not investigate.

findings.area: Rest-of-Season (ROS) engine — src/ros/ (15 modules, 5,031 lines) + src/ros/sources/ (5 adapters), the /api/ros/* router, the four /league lazy sections (rosTeam
findings.title: freshness_multiplier and staleFlag are structurally unreachable — the timestamp compared against "now" is always this run's own completion time
findings.evidence: `scrape.py:437` `scraped_at=result.completed_at or None`, and `:576` `result.completed_at = result.completed_at or _now()` — adapters set `completed_at` to the moment they finished. `parse.py:120-123` then computes `age_hours = (now - when)/3600`, which is always ~0, so `:124` returns 1.0 unconditionally. Confirmed against live data: every contributor weight in `data/ros/aggregate/latest.json` reproduces exactly with freshness=1.0 (fantasyProsRosSf 0.85×1.10 = 0.935 ✓, draftSharksRosSf 1.25×1.10 = 1.375 ✓, fantasyProsRosIdp 1.05×0.8925 = 0.9371 ✓, fantasyProsRosOverall 1.15×0.95 = 1.0925 ✓, ffc2qbAdp 0.70×1.10×0.85 = 0.6545 ✓). Likewise `aggregate.py:131` `is_stale_source = snap.status not in ("ok","partial") and snap.has_valid_cache` — a failed source has zero rows and is skipped at `:129`, so `is_stale_source` can never be True. Live check: 0 of 1,085 aggregate rows have `staleFlag: true` and 0 of 4,270 contributor entries have `stale: true`.
findings.userImpact: The staleness half of the source-weight model is inert. A source whose upstream CSV is two weeks old (as `footballGuysRosIdp`'s was) would carry full weight, and the `confidence` field's 0.20 freshness term is a constant 0.20 for every player — it contributes nothing to discrimination.
