findings.title: No historical validation, calibration or backtest exists for any ROS output
findings.evidence: `tests/ros/` (15 files, 2,653 lines) contains only unit tests that re-implement the formula under test — e.g. `test_team_strength.py:83 test_composite_uses_documented_weights` computes `0.72*starting + 0.18*depth + 0.05*coverage + 0.05*health` and asserts equality with the code's output; `test_aggregate.py:126 test_two_sources_blend_correctly` asserts only that the result is in [0,100] and that the higher-weighted source's rank-1 player outranks the other. No file anywhere joins ROS values or team-strength ranks to realized weekly scoring. `pick_projection.py:52-57` states this explicitly for its own horizon ceilings: "These ceilings are a STATED ASSUMPTION, not a measurement. Backtesting them needs multi-season team-strength snapshots joined to realized final standings, and `data/ros/team_strength/` holds only the current snapshot per league — there is no history to fit against." Confirmed: `data/ros/team_strength/` contains exactly two files, overwritten every 2h. Contrast the dynasty side, which has `docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md` and `scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py`. `frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:761` concedes the gap for one flag: "Defaults off until you've validated v2 against a few weeks of standings" — validation delegated to the user, by eye.
findings.userImpact: Every constant in this subsystem — the 0.72/0.18/0.05/0.05 composite, the 0.85/1.25/1.05/1.15/0.70 base weights, the 0.45/0.35/0.20 confidence split, the 18.0 volatility threshold, ROS_BLEND 0.20, the 1.10 variance bump, the nine power-v2 weights, every tag and direction threshold — is an unvalidated prior presented as a measurement. There is no evidence any ROS number predicts anything.

findings.title: stale_after_hours is declared in both registries, mirrored to JS, documented as driving availability — and read by nothing
findings.evidence: `src/ros/sources/__init__.py` declares `stale_after_hours` on all five entries (`:69, :92, :111, :136, :154`) and documents it at `:31` as "freshness threshold; older → marked stale". `frontend/lib/ros-sources.js` mirrors it. `docs/ros-engine.md` states "Each source declares `stale_after_hours` in the registry. A source older than that threshold has its `availability_multiplier` reduced from 1.0 → 0.5". A repo-wide grep for `stale_after_hours|staleAfterHours` outside tests returns only the declarations plus one pass-through copy into run metadata at `scrape.py:149`. `parse.py:158` `availability_multiplier(status, has_valid_cache)` takes no age argument and has no age logic.
findings.userImpact: An operator tuning `stale_after_hours` to make a source decay faster gets no effect, and `tests/ros/test_sources_registry_parity.py` will keep the dead field in lockstep across two languages forever.

findings.title: Two independent championship-odds calculations disagree by up to 4.8 percentage points; the one the UI reads is the unseeded, non-convergent one
findings.evidence: `playoff_sim.py:759` runs its own bracket (`_simulate_bracket`, re-seeding each round, adaptive sim count) and stamps `championshipOdds` per owner. `championship.py:227` runs a different bracket (`_simulate_bracket` at `:63`, pop(0)/pop(-1) with no re-seeding, fixed `n_simulations=10000` at `:203`, unseeded `rng` at `:177`) and stamps `championshipOdds` for the same owners. Live comparison of the two committed files: Joey 0.3815 vs 0.4085 (Δ2.70pp), Jason 0.3185 vs 0.3390 (Δ2.05pp), Eric 0.2955 vs 0.2474 (Δ4.81pp). `trade_deadline.py::_load_championship_map` reads the `championship.py` file; `simulate_trade_impact` reads the `playoff_sim.py` number. Additional defects in the championship bracket: `:80` hardcodes the field size to 6 (`seeded_owners.index(s) < 6`) so the `playoff_seeds` parameter at `:167` is dead, and `:94` `bye_set` is assigned and never used.
findings.userImpact: Eric is a "Favorite" (≥0.20, `championship.py:50`) on one number and would round differently on the other. Which championship probability a surface shows depends on which file it reads, and neither is labelled.

findings.title: team_ros_strength's "weights" are coefficients on incommensurable quantities — coverage and health are labelled 5% and contribute 0.77%
findings.evidence: `team_strength.py:33-36` sets `WEIGHT_STARTING=0.72, WEIGHT_DEPTH=0.18, WEIGHT_COVERAGE=0.05, WEIGHT_HEALTH=0.05` and `:156-161` sums them. But `starting_lineup_score` is an unbounded SUM over ~21 slots (`lineup.py:363`) while `positional_coverage_score` and `health_availability_score` are bounded 0-100 (`lineup.py:411, 516`). Computed on the live top team: 0.72×833.21 + 0.18×205.19 + 0.05×100.0 + 0.05×100.0 = 646.85 (matches the file exactly), of which starting = 92.74%, depth = 5.71%, coverage = 0.77%, health = 0.77%. Across all 12 teams `positionalCoverageScore` ranges only 90.87–100.0 and `healthAvailabilityScore` is 100.0 for 11 of 12. `frontend/app/league/sections/ros-team-strength.jsx:181-183` prints the coefficients to the user as "72% starting lineup + 18% best-ball depth + 5% positional coverage + 5% health". `tests/ros/test_team_strength.py:83` re-implements the same expression and asserts equality — it validates the arithmetic, not that the weights mean what they say.
findings.userImpact: A reader is told health and coverage are 10% of the number. They are 1.5%. Any attempt to tune the composite by moving those coefficients will appear to do nothing. Health is also double-counted — injured players are already multiplied by 0.4 inside starting_lineup_score.

findings.title: The "rest-of-season" board is 23-41% multi-year dynasty rankings, and nothing in the output discloses the horizon mix
findings.evidence: Two of five sources are registered `source_type: "dynasty_proxy", is_ros: False`: `fantasyProsRosSf` points at `dynasty-superflex.php` (`src/ros/sources/__init__.py:56-72`) and `fantasyProsRosIdp` reads `CSVs/site_raw/fantasyProsIdp.csv`, the dynasty IDP board (`src/ros/sources/fantasypros_ros_idp.py:24`). A third, `ffc2qbAdp`, is redraft ADP (`is_ros: False`). Computed shares of effective weight on the live blend: for a 4-source offense player, dynasty proxy 0.935/4.057 = 23.0%, ADP 16.1%, true ROS 60.9%. For an IDP player there are only two contributors and the dynasty proxy is 0.9371/2.312 = 40.5%. The output field is named `rosValue`, the endpoint is `/api/ros/player-values`, and `frontend/app/league/sections/ros-team-strength.jsx:181` says only "Composite team strength for the rest of the season."
findings.userImpact: A user acting on "who is strongest right now" is partly acting on multi-year dynasty rankings, most heavily for IDP where 40% of every value is a dynasty board. The registry knows (`is_ros: False`) and the information never reaches the surface.

findings.title: Distinct NFL players collide onto one canonical name; the second is silently dropped from the blend
findings.evidence: `data/ros/sources/draftSharksRosSf.csv` contains `byron murphy` twice (Vikings CB Byron Murphy Jr. and Seahawks DT Byron Murphy II are different players); `data/ros/sources/fantasyProsRosIdp.csv` contains `byron young` twice (Rams DE and Raiders DT). `aggregate.py:187-194` keeps the first scoring row and logs a warning that the source "emitted %r more than once", framing a real identity collision as a vendor duplicate. `mapping.py:104` returns the normalized string with no positional or team disambiguation, and `resolve_player` is only invoked at `scrape.py:552` when `canonicalName` is empty — which is always, since all five adapters emit `"canonicalName": ""`. `_build_default_canonical_universe` (`scrape.py:479-510`) builds the universe from Sleeper full names alone, so both Byrons collapse to one universe entry too.
findings.userImpact: One of each pair gets the other's ROS value in `team_strength`'s join (`team_strength.py:98-102` uses `setdefault`, first wins), and the other is reported as unmapped and scored 0.0 toward its owner's composite. In an IDP league both pairs are startable defenders.

findings.title: The "Seller cash-out" tag compares a 0-9999 dynasty value against a 0-100 ROS value and can never fire in production
findings.evidence: `src/ros/tags.py:76` `if veteran and is_strong and dynasty_value is not None and dynasty_value < ros_value * 0.7`. `is_strong` requires `ros_value >= 60.0` (`:63`), so the threshold is at most 70. The live callers pass a dynasty value on the canonical 0-9999 scale: `frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:142` `const dynastyValue = row.values?.full ?? row.rankDerivedValue ?? null` and `frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:127` the same. `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1166` `full: backendValue || rawValues.full` where `backendValue` is `rankDerivedValue`. A player with `rankDerivedValue < 70` on a 0-9999 board cannot simultaneously be a strong-ROS veteran. The pinning test `tests/ros/test_direction_and_tags.py:142-150` passes `ros_value=70, dynasty_value=40` — a combination the production call sites cannot produce — so it passes while the live tag is dead.
findings.userImpact: One of nine advertised tags never renders. `tag_descriptions()` (`tags.py:96`) still documents it and `frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:39` still assigns it a colour, so the feature reads as shipped.

findings.title: The tag classifier exists in three hand-maintained copies with no parity test, and the backend copy is dead
findings.evidence: `src/ros/tags.py:70-96`, `frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:61-83`, and `frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:95-116` each implement the same nine rules. `RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:58-60` says "mirrors src/ros/tags.py::tags_for_player... Stays in sync via the parity test (PR-future)" — the parity test does not exist; the only relevant file is `tests/ros/test_direction_and_tags.py`, which tests the Python copy alone and never parses the JS. `tags_for_player` has zero non-test callers (grep), so the shipped behaviour is whichever JS copy renders. findings.userImpact: The backend definition of the tags is dead code and the two live definitions can drift independently. A tag rule fixed in one popup will silently not apply on /trade.

findings.title: Sim cache TTL and health-page age are computed from file mtime, so a deploy or checkout resets them and reports stale sims as fresh
findings.evidence: `playoff_sim.py:843` `age = os.path.getmtime(path)` then `:848` `if (time.time() - age) > _SIM_CACHE_TTL_SEC: return None`; `championship.py:283` identical; `api.py:250` `return time.time() - os.path.getmtime(path)` feeding `sims.playoffAgeSeconds` / `championshipAgeSeconds`. The payloads carry a real `computedAt` field (`scrape.py:369, 373`) which none of these read. Observable in this working tree: `data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json` has `computedAt: 2026-08-04T03:57:31` but an mtime of `Aug 4 06:56` — three hours apart, from the checkout. Since these files are git-tracked, any `git pull` on the production VPS rewrites the mtime and makes an arbitrarily old sim look freshly computed. `api.py:254-261 _iso_to_age_seconds` reads the ISO timestamp correctly and is used for the aggregate — the right helper exists two functions away.
findings.userImpact: /tools/ros-data-health colours the sim tiles green (`ageColor` threshold 6h) on age data that a deploy resets, and `build_section` serves a cached sim past its intended TTL without re-running.

findings.title: simulate_trade_impact runs the full best-ball presim three times per call; simulate_playoff_odds recomputes distributions it was handed
findings.evidence: `playoff_sim.py:688-691`: when `distributions` is passed in, the function still calls `_build_team_distributions(...)` in full, discarding the distributions and keeping only `pf_by_owner`. `_build_team_distributions:491-496` runs `_bestball_presim`, which per `:411` draws up to `BEST_BALL_PRESIM_MAX_WEEKS = 1200` weeks per team, each solving a full `solve_optimal_assignment` over a 44-58 player roster (`lineup.py:224`). `simulate_trade_impact:968` calls it once, then `:993` and `:1003` call `simulate_playoff_odds` with explicit distributions — each of which triggers `:689` again. Three full presims per trade evaluation, two thrown away.
findings.userImpact: Trade-impact odds are computed on a request path. On the 12-team best-ball league this is 3 × 12 × up to 1200 exact assignment solves before the Monte Carlo starts.

findings.title: data/ros is force-committed to git with no retention: 792 aggregate snapshots and 4,633 run files, 872 MB, against a documented "rolling 30-day archive"
findings.evidence: `src/ros/__init__.py:26` and `docs/ros-engine.md` both call `data/ros/aggregate/history/` a "rolling 30-day archive". `scrape.py:615-616` writes a new archive every run and there is no prune anywhere (grep for prune/cleanup/unlink under `src/ros/` and `scripts/` returns nothing). `.gitignore:59-68` ignores these paths, but `.github/workflows/scheduled-refresh.yml:521` `git add -f -- "$p"` over a list including `data/ros/` force-adds them. findings.userImpact: Every clone and every CI checkout pulls ~872 MB of ROS scratch data plus its full commit history.

findings.title: The aggregate's league context is hardcoded, so a non-IDP league is served a payload asserting idp_enabled: true

findings.title: The IDP format bonus is decided once per source from the first row's position, not per player
findings.evidence: `aggregate.py:136` `sample_position = next((r.position for r in snap.rows if r.position), None)` then `:137-153` computes ONE weight for the whole source and applies it to every row at `:203`. `parse.py:76-79` decides the 1.05 IDP bonus from that single sampled position. `draftSharksRosSf` carries 424 IDP rows (per its fetcher's docstring) but its first row is Josh Allen (QB), so none of its IDP rows get the bonus; `fantasyProsRosIdp`'s first row is a DE, so all 219 rows get it. findings.userImpact: The one format adjustment that could partially offset the IDP normalization problem is applied to the wrong rows.

findings.title: _PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION is dead code and its docstring states a rosValue→points divisor of 17 against the live value of 2.7
findings.evidence: `playoff_sim.py:113-127` defines `_PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION` and `_DEFAULT_PLAYER_CV`; grep shows no reference to either name anywhere in `src/ros/`. findings.title: draftSharksRosSf normalizes against a denominator larger than the population that survives into the blend
findings.evidence: `src/ros/sources/draftsharks_ros.py:90-93` sets `total_ranked = len(rows)` = 978 from the raw CSV. `scrape.py:562` then drops rows whose canonical name did not resolve and `:563` recomputes `player_count`, but never revisits `total_ranked`. findings.userImpact: Small systematic distortion of the score curve — the denominator claims a deeper board than the one being blended. Magnitude is modest on a log curve, but it is a silent inconsistency between two counts describing the same population.

findings.title: direction.py's documented band table does not match its fallthrough order
findings.evidence: `direction.py:62-74` documents "Hold: 0.35 <= playoff < 0.55 with low championship odds" and "Selective Seller: 0.20 <= playoff < 0.40". The code checks Strong Buyer, Buyer, Selective Buyer (`:92`, 0.45–0.60), Strong Seller (`:98`), Seller (`:104`, `playoff < 0.25 and champ < 0.02`), Selective Seller (`:107`, 0.20–0.40), else Hold. findings.userImpact: Anyone tuning the thresholds from the docstring will produce different labels than expected.

findings.title: Bye-week handling is advertised but hardcoded off
findings.evidence: `src/ros/scrape.py:224` sets `"bye": False` for every hydrated roster player, unconditionally. `lineup.py:219-220` `elif player.bye: base *= 0.0` therefore never executes, and `lineup.py:373` `"flagged": "injured" if pick.injured else ("bye" if pick.bye else None)` can never emit "bye". findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: The league-adjusted factor is NOT a function of position alone — CLAUDE.md and publish.py both assert a property production violates
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md: "The adjustment factor is a function of position alone and never reads the consensus value". src/league_intel/publish.py:21-27: "The factor depends only on **position** — it never reads the consensus value." But src/league_intel/adjustment.py:312-323 states the opposite in code: `reception_fit_axis` — "The only per-player axis in the model. Every other axis is a function of position, which is what lets them compose against a re-weighted board; this one is not". src/api/gameplan.py:1333 passes `reception_fit=_resolve_reception_fit(league_key)` into the payload builder unconditionally, and `reception_scoring_fit` defaults True (src/api/feature_flags.py:204). The repo's own production measurement proves the violation: docs/measurements/adjusted-board-backtest-2026-07-28.json `factorShape` shows RB `distinct: 45`, TE `distinct: 49`, WR `distinct: 96` — 190 distinct per-player factors on one board. I reproduced the position-uniform case only by passing `reception_fit=None`: 8 distinct factor values for 931 moved rows.
findings.userImpact: An auditor or maintainer reading CLAUDE.md concludes the overlay can never reorder players within a position and that the batch monotonicity guard is decorative. It is not: reception fit reorders WR/RB/TE against each other, and it is the only axis that can. Any reasoning built on "position-uniform, therefore order-preserving by construction" is wrong for three of eight positions.

findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: structuralScarcity is computed from a log-rank index with an arbitrary zero, so every factor moves when the ROS source universe changes size
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/replacement.py:609-613 `_safe_drop(top, bottom) -> 1 - bottom/top`, used at :655 as `lineup_scarcity=_safe_drop(top, starter)`. Both operands are `rosValue`. src/ros/aggregate.py:171-173: "``rosValue`` is therefore a normalized log-rank index on 0-100 — not points, and not projection-aware." src/ros/parse.py:43-46: `return 100.0 * (log(n+1) - log(r)) / log(n+1)` where `n = total_ranked`. A ratio requires a true zero; this index's zero is "rank N of whatever the ROS sources happened to publish". I held every player's rank fixed and only re-scored under a different universe size N (live N=1085 from data/ros/aggregate/latest.json): N=1085 factors {DB 1.0149, DL 1.0533, K 0.9878, LB 1.0199, QB 1.0179, RB 1.0407, TE 1.0115, WR 1.0254}; N=2000 {DB 0.9916, DL 1.0339, K 0.9617, LB 1.0033, QB 1.0071, RB 1.0272, TE 0.9933, WR 1.0112}; N=500 {DB 1.0636, DL 1.0877, K 1.0340, LB 1.0483, QB 1.0353, RB 1.0624, TE 1.0516, WR 1.0496}. DB, TE and LB flip from lift to trim purely on universe size.
findings.userImpact: Because picks are exempt (factor 1.0), the mean player factor is the level of the whole player-vs-pick reprice. On the live board that level is +2.5% (offense) / +3.3% (IDP) at N=1085, but would be +0.5% at N=2000 and +5.5% at N=500 with identical player rankings. A ROS source being added, dropped, or publishing a longer board silently changes every trade valuation under the adjusted lens, in a direction nobody chose. Positions can flip from "scarce" to "deep" with no change in the league.

findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: lineupScarcity measures top-heaviness, not scarcity, and the resulting lift is applied uniformly to every player at the position including replacement-level ones
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/replacement.py:655 `lineup_scarcity=_safe_drop(top, starter)` = `1 - median(marginal starters) / max(pool)`. Live dynasty_main: DL top 60.41, starter level 14.095 → 0.7667 → factor 1.05334; TE top 41.88, starter 18.525 → 0.5577 → factor 1.01153. The quantity is the *steepness of the positional value curve*, i.e. how far the best player at the position is above the last starter. src/league_intel/adjustment.py:250 applies `1.0 + delta` to every row at that position via src/league_intel/publish.py:171-179 and src/league_intel/overlay.py:92-93. The docstring at adjustment.py:218-228 calls it "positional scarcity implied by THIS league's measured lineup", which is a different concept.
findings.userImpact: A steep drop-off at a position is a VORP argument for paying up for the ELITE player at that position — it is an argument for paying LESS for the replacement-level one, since the gap is exactly what makes the marginal starter cheap. The current implementation does the opposite: the deepest priced DL on the board gets the same +5.3% as the best one. Under the adjusted lens a trade calculator overprices positional roster clog at exactly the positions where clog is least valuable.

findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: scoringFit and receptionFit are measured against a Sleeper league that is not in the registry, then cached per league key as if they were league-specific
findings.evidence: src/api/gameplan.py:1180-1181 and :1272-1273 both do `cfg = _load_config(); mine_id = str((cfg.get("my_league") or {}).get("id"))` from config/league_comparison.json, whose `my_league.id` is `"1312736351547850752"`. The registry's leagues are `1312006700437352448` (dynasty_main) and `1320092771247222784` (dynasty_new); the canonical LI snapshot config/league_intel/sleeper_league_snapshot_2026-07-26.json carries `"league_id":"1312006700437352448"`. Grepping the whole tree, `1312736351547850752` appears in exactly one file — config/league_comparison.json. The `league_key` argument is used ONLY as the cache key (gameplan.py:1159-1160, :1247-1248); it never reaches the measurement.
findings.userImpact: The IDP positional multipliers (DL 1.0421 / DB 0.9971 / LB 0.9608 per scoring_fit.py:60-66) and every per-player reception tilt are derived from a league whose scoring settings nobody in this repo has cross-checked against dynasty_main's. Both then get applied to dynasty_main AND dynasty_new. If `my_league` is a stale or test league, the entire scoringFit axis is priced off the wrong rate card while presenting as `SCORING_MEASURED` evidence tier (confidence 0.70).

findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: The TE++ target basis is a hardcoded constant that is wrong for dynasty_new, and the corrective overlay axis is deliberately absent — the mispricing is documented and unmitigated
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:5681 `_BOARD_TE_BASIS: str = "tepp"`, applied at :7192-7207 to every non-TEP source's TE contribution. `src.league_intel.te_premium.measure_te_demand` returns `targetBasis: "tepp"` for dynasty_main (2 mandatory TE starters) and `targetBasis: "base"` for dynasty_new (1) — I ran it against config/leagues/registry.json. Both leagues share scoringProfile `superflex_tep15_ppr1`, so they share one board. src/league_intel/publish.py:45-70 names the problem and leaves `tePremium` ABSENT; src/league_intel/adjustment.py:371-396 returns an ABSENT axis unconditionally. A/B on the live export (RISKIT_FEATURE_TE_BASIS_CONVERSION=1 vs 0, 86 TE rows): median TE value ratio 1.1672, range 1.007–1.2708; median TE rank improvement 50 slots, max 202.
findings.userImpact: dynasty_new is a one-TE league being served a board where tight ends carry a two-TE premium worth a median +17% in value and ~50 board slots. Every trade evaluation, waiver bid and draft board for that league systematically overpays for TEs, and there is no toggle, note, or overlay that takes it back off.

findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: apply_valuation_factors is a third copy of "apply factors and re-rank" and it drops the coherence guard the other two have
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/publish.py:186-191 claims "ONE implementation of 'apply factors and re-rank', shared with the server-side engine path (``src.league_intel.overlay``). Two copies of this would drift, and the failure would be silent." But src/api/data_contract.py:8999-9040 `apply_valuation_factors` is a third implementation, reached from server.py:3782 via `build_rankings_delta_payload(..., valuation_factors=...)`. It multiplies and calls `compact_ranks_and_tiers` at :9036-9040 but never calls `assert_ranking_coherence`, which src/league_intel/overlay.py:119-125 uses to return None and force a market-board fallback. It also returns 0 on no-move while server.py:9143-9150 still stamps `"applied": True`.
findings.userImpact: The one path that combines custom source weights with the league-adjusted lens — the most novel board the server can produce, and therefore the most likely to be incoherent — is the only path with no coherence check. A board whose displayed ranks contradict its displayed values ships to /rankings with no warning, exactly the state overlay.py refuses to serve.

findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: The server-side adjusted contract scales only rankDerivedValue, leaving offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue and values.* at market — suggestions.py mixes both scales in one comparison
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/overlay.py:88-95 scales exactly one field: `copy["rankDerivedValue"] = int(round(base * factor))`. The client-side applier does more — frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1911-1917 also scales `values.overall|finalAdjusted|displayValue` and :1946 `_finalAdjusted`. Meanwhile src/trade/suggestions.py:626-643 reads `row["offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue"]` into `offense_only_value`, and :765-769 `_eff_val` returns that unscaled number for offensive positions while returning the SCALED `display_value` for IDP positions (:1089-1099, :1251-1294 pass `pos_oo = pos not in _IDP_BASE_POSITIONS`). On the live contract 607 of 1092 rows carry a positive `offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue`.
findings.userImpact: CLAUDE.md's central justification for the whole overlay design — "every engine reads exactly one value — rankDerivedValue" — is false. Under `valuationMode=leagueAdjusted`, the upgrade and depth searches in trade suggestions compare adjusted IDP values against unadjusted offense values, a scale mismatch of up to 5.3% that silently biases which upgrades and sweeteners are proposed.

findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: The rankings overlay is unreachable for the non-default league while the engines still serve it — two boards in one session, the exact failure the feature exists to remove
findings.evidence: server.py:5361-5374 (`GET /api/valuation/league-adjusted`) returns 503 `data_not_ready` whenever `latest_contract_data.meta.leagueKey != league_cfg.key`. But `/api/terminal` (server.py:10332) and `/api/trade/simulate` (server.py:10582) deliberately resolve WITHOUT `require_loaded_contract=True` and then call `_valuation_scoped_contract` (server.py:10443, :10653), which computes factors from the requested league's own rosters and serves an adjusted board. The client swallows the 503 silently: frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1822-1830 logs a console warning and returns null.
findings.userImpact: On a single-instance deployment holding dynasty_main's contract, a dynasty_new user with the toggle ON sees a market-priced /rankings page (silently, no banner) and a league-adjusted terminal and trade simulator. That is precisely the split-board confusion documented in src/league_intel/overlay.py:12-15 as the reason this feature was built.

findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: reference_lineup_scarcity = 0.5 and sensitivity = 0.20 are hand-picked defaults that are never overridden, never configured, and never calibrated
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/adjustment.py:215-216 `reference_lineup_scarcity: float = 0.5, sensitivity: float = 0.20`; :247 `delta = (value - reference_lineup_scarcity) * sensitivity`. `build_board_adjustments` calls `structural_scarcity_axis(position, pos_scarcity)` at adjustment.py:764 with no keyword arguments, so the defaults always apply. Grepping src/, scripts/ and config/ for `reference_lineup_scarcity` or `sensitivity=` returns only these three lines in adjustment.py — no config file, no calibration script, no test that varies them. Live dynasty_main lineupScarcity values are 0.4392–0.7667, i.e. only kickers sit below the 0.5 reference; seven of eight positions get a lift.
findings.userImpact: Because the reference is below the observed distribution and picks are exempt, the axis has a net LEVEL effect rather than a purely relative one: I measured +2.52% on offense value, +3.28% on IDP value, +0.00% on picks across the live 1092-row board. That systematic player-over-pick inflation is an artifact of picking 0.5, not a measurement. `sensitivity = 0.20` is the sole scale factor on the only live cross-position axis and rests on nothing.

findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: The backtest's paired bootstrap resamples players, but the across-position claim has 8 degrees of freedom — the reported power is overstated for the scalars
findings.evidence: src/model_registry/board_holdout.py:156-172 `paired_bootstrap` draws `idx = [rng.randrange(n) for _ in range(n)]` over the 572-player population. docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md:165-168 concludes "the CI half-width is about 0.009 ρ, so this design detects a difference of roughly ±0.015". But the artifact's own `factorShape` (docs/measurements/adjusted-board-backtest-2026-07-28.json) shows DB/DL/LB/QB/K each receive ONE scalar, so the entire cross-position signal is 8 numbers. Resampling players i.i.d. treats each of 572 rows as independent evidence about those 8 scalars. The bootstrap also holds the factors fixed and therefore carries no uncertainty from the 12-roster scarcity measurement that produced them.
findings.userImpact: The doc's headline power claim is only valid for the within-position (reception fit) arm. For the positional-scalar arm — which is the arm every trade valuation depends on, and the arm three of four framings lean negative on — the true interval is wider than reported, so "a null here is a real null at the effect sizes the current axes produce" is not established for the scalars.

findings.area: src/league_intel/ — league-adjusted valuation overlay (positional scarcity, replacement levels, scoring/reception fit, TE premium), GET /api/valuation/league-ad
findings.title: cross_market.py's module docstring states it has zero production importers; three production modules import it
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/cross_market.py:11-17: "The honest count of production importers of THIS file is **zero**. ``value_package`` / ``compare_packages`` are consumed only by ``tests/league_intel/test_cross_market.py``. ``src/trade/angle.py`` is the intended call site and is **not rewired yet**". Actual importers: src/trade/angle.py:78 `from src.league_intel.cross_market import (...)`, src/roster_intel/packages.py:77 same, src/api/gameplan.py:128 `from src.league_intel.cross_market import DEFAULT_GATE_PCT`.

findings.title: Public trade letter grades apply linear-calibrated thresholds to an α=1.65-transformed gap — a 6% trade grades "Robbery"

A=[5000,3000] B=[7500]     wA=1.815e6 wB=2.477e6  alpha-pct=26.73%  linear-pct=6.25%   -> A+ Big win / D Robbery
A=[9000] B=[4000,4000]     wA=3.346e6 wB=1.756e6  alpha-pct=47.53%  linear-pct=11.11%  -> A+ Big win / F Fleeced

findings.title: A single 0.00-point roster-week silently removes that owner from the all-play population, breaking the luck metric's pigeonhole identity

as luck.py SEES it      sum expectedShare = 5.5  n=11

findings.area: News + player context + NFL data (src/news, src/playerctx, src/nfl_data) with routes /api/news, /api/playerctx/player, /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized, /api/a
findings.title: A keyword-matched RSS headline directly discounts a user-facing player value by up to 5%, and the severity is not player-specific
findings.evidence: src/api/injury_impact.py:80-84 `BASE_DISCOUNT_PCT = {"alert": 4.0, "watch": 2.0, "info": 0.5}`; :281 `discount = base * pos_mult * age_mult * decay`; :331 `adjusted = int(round(base_value * impact["adjustedPct"] / 100.0))`. The severity comes from src/news/providers/_rss.py:97-102 `if _ALERT_RE.search(text): return "alert", "injury", "negative"` — a regex over the CONCATENATED headline+description (_rss.py:180 `classify(f"{title}\n{description}")`), with alert keywords including `questionable`, `doubtful`, `arrest`, `suspended` (_rss.py:28-46). Mentions are attached by plain substring match over the whole known-name list (_rss.py:144 `if key in haystack`), so one headline listing five players in an injury report attaches the SAME alert severity to all five. Wired live at src/api/terminal.py:1562 `injury = _injury_impact.apply_injury_impact(row=r, news_for_player=player_news, now_ms=now_ms)` and rendered at frontend/components/terminal/BuySellHold.jsx:319 `<InjuryChip impact={entry.injuryImpact} adjustedValue={entry.injuryAdjustedValue} />` and frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:763-764.
findings.userImpact: Worked example (my computation, reproducing the module's constants): alert + RB + age 30, fresh news -> 4.0 x 1.20 x 1.20 x 1.0 = 5.76 -> capped 5.00% -> a 9000 value renders as 8550. `info` severity means NO keyword matched at all — ordinary neutral news — and still discounts: info + RB + age 33 -> 0.5 x 1.20 x 1.40 = 0.84% -> 9000 renders as 8924. A user sees a repriced number driven by the mere existence of a headline that mentions the player's name as a substring.

findings.title: classify() stamps impact="positive" on every WATCH item — including "released" and "waived" — which produces a BUY recommendation and silently kills injury_impact's entire watch tier
findings.evidence: src/news/providers/_rss.py:99-101 `if _WATCH_RE.search(text): kind = ...; return "watch", kind, "positive"`. `_WATCH_KEYWORDS` (_rss.py:47-63) contains `released`, `waived`, `traded`, `claim`. I ran it: `classify('Jones released by Bears')` -> `('watch','transaction','positive')`; `classify('Team waived WR Smith')` -> `('watch','transaction','positive')`. Two live consequences: (1) src/api/terminal.py:950-956 `if pos > 0 and (rank_change is not None and rank_change > 0): add(38, "BUY", "pos_news_rising", ...)`; (2) src/api/injury_impact.py:256-266 `has_positive = any(... p.get("impact") == "positive" ...); if has_positive: continue` — since every RSS watch item marks all of its mentions positive, and Sleeper's only watch items are trending-ADDs (also positive, sleeper.py:_row_to_item `impact = "positive" if direction == "add"`), no watch item can ever reach the discount arithmetic. `BASE_DISCOUNT_PCT["watch"] = 2.0` is unreachable code.
findings.userImpact: A headline announcing a player was cut is scored as positive news; combined with any positive rank change it emits a BUY signal reading 'Positive news with rank rising'. Separately, the entire mid-grade injury tier (2.0 base) never fires, so a hamstring/high-ankle story produces zero discount while an unrelated neutral headline produces 0.4-0.84%.

findings.evidence: server.py:11069-11076: the route resolves `league_cfg = _resolve_league_for_request(request)` and then reads `sleeper_block = (latest_contract_data or {}).get("sleeper") or {}` / `scoring_settings = sleeper_block.get("scoringSettings") or {}` — no check that the loaded contract's leagueKey matches league_cfg.key, despite the response stamping `"leagueKey": league_cfg.key` (server.py:11138). findings.area: News + player context + NFL data (src/news, src/playerctx, src/nfl_data) with routes /api/news, /api/playerctx/player, /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized, /api/a
findings.title: A news headline raises a player's BDVM fundamental value through the sigma channel — the documented safety property covers the mean, not the value
findings.evidence: src/bdvm/news_events.py:13-17 promises 'Headlines can widen uncertainty; they can never move a player's mean.' True for mu. But src/bdvm/surplus.py:32-37 `expected_positive_surplus(mu, sigma, replacement) -> (mu - replacement) * norm_cdf(z) + sigma * norm_pdf(z)` is strictly increasing in sigma, and src/api/bdvm_api.py:165 `surplus_mode: str = "option"` makes that the DEFAULT board. The chain: news item -> keyword rule (news_events.py:78-90, e.g. INJURY on /injur|placed on ir|concussion|hamstring/) -> event at confidence 0.45, reliability 0.6 -> src/bdvm/events.py:122-131 `scaled = math.exp(math.log(value) * scale)` with `scale = confidence * reliability * 2^(-days/half_life)` (events.py:100-101) -> sigma_mult applied at events.py:185-186.
findings.userImpact: I computed it: INJURY carries `sigma_mult: 1.15` (config/bdvm/event_types_v1.json), scale = 0.45 x 0.6 = 0.27 on day 0, so effective multiplier = 1.15^0.27 = 1.0405. For mu=12, R=10, sigma=6 the option surplus goes 3.5254 -> 3.6173 (+2.61%); for a sub-replacement player (mu=10, R=12) 1.5254 -> 1.6173 (+6.02%); for an elite player (mu=18, R=10, sigma=7) +0.72%. An injury headline therefore makes a marginal player look MORE valuable, and it does so unevenly across the board — a relative distortion, not a level one.

findings.title: opportunity_score ignores the position argument it takes and saturates at 100 far below its documented calibration point
findings.evidence: src/nfl_data/opportunity_stats.py:231 `def _compute_opportunity_score(bucket: dict[str, int], position: str) -> float:` — `position` is never referenced in the body (:243-249), yet the module docstring at :31 advertises 'opportunity_score: float # composite 0..100 per-position'. The docstring at :239-241 claims 'a player with 20+ RZ touches, 10+ GL touches, 60%+ 3D conv rate lands near 100'. Formula: `score = (rz_touches * 3.0) + (gl_touches * 6.0) + (conv_rate * 30.0)`, then `min(100.0, max(0.0, score))` (:248-249).
findings.userImpact: I computed the docstring's own example: 20*3 + 10*6 + 0.60*30 = 138, clamped to 100 — it does not 'land near 100', it blew through the ceiling by 38%. RZ touches alone hit the cap at 33.3, which most starting RBs clear, so every high-volume back ties at exactly 100 and the metric cannot rank the group it exists to rank. Currently harmless: nothing outside tests/nfl_data/test_opportunity_stats.py imports this module.

findings.title: usage_windows z-scores use a population standard deviation over as few as two prior observations, producing |z|>=4 on ordinary week-to-week snap-share noise
findings.evidence: src/nfl_data/usage_windows.py:99-104 `def _stdev(values): if len(values) < 2: return 0.0; mean = ...; var = sum((v - mean) ** 2 for v in values) / len(values); return math.sqrt(var)` — divides by n, not n-1. The gate for emitting a z at all is only two prior weeks (usage_windows.py:171-176 `if len(w_snap) >= 2`). Thresholds that consume it are src/news/usage_signals.py:39-40 `_BUY_Z = 2.0` / `_SELL_Z = -2.0`.
findings.userImpact: I reproduced it: prior window [0.60, 0.64], current 0.70 -> mean 0.62, population sd 0.02, z = +4.0 — a 6-percentage-point snap-share move on a stable starter clears the BUY threshold twice over. With a 4-week window [0.70, 0.72, 0.68, 0.74] and current 0.80 the z is +4.02. This is the mechanism behind the repo's own measured 17.8%-of-active-players-per-week fire rate (src/api/feature_flags.py:83-92). Not currently reachable — nothing in src/ or server.py calls detect_usage_transitions (pinned by tests/news/test_usage_signal_calibration.py:97).

findings.area: News + player context + NFL data (src/news, src/playerctx, src/nfl_data) with routes /api/news, /api/playerctx/player, /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized, /api/a
findings.title: The freshness guard returns True on Saturday and Sunday of the in-flight week — the exact window it exists to exclude
findings.evidence: src/nfl_data/freshness.py:30 `_SAFE_WEEKDAY = 3` (Thursday) and :75 `return now_n.weekday() >= _SAFE_WEEKDAY` for the `stat_week == season_current_week` branch. Python's weekday() is Monday=0..Sunday=6, so `>= 3` is true for Thursday(3), Friday(4), Saturday(5) AND Sunday(6). The module docstring at :10-15 states the rule as "don't trust current-week data until Thursday local NFL day" and explains the hazard as 'between Sunday evening and Tuesday/Wednesday the data you pull back for last week is provisional'.
findings.userImpact: During the current NFL week, Sunday — mid-slate, when box scores are actively being written — is treated as safe to fire alerts on. The companion week_is_in_flight (:96) has the same inversion, so the UI would also label Sunday data as final.

findings.title: Player mention tagging is a plain lowercase substring match, so a prefix name is tagged on every article about its suffixed namesake, and never flagged ambiguous
findings.evidence: src/news/providers/_rss.py:143-145 `key = name.lower(); ... if key in haystack: out.append(PlayerMention(name=name, impact=impact))`. The docstring at :127-131 justifies it: 'The known-names set is already curated ... so full-word matching would be overkill'. I ran it: `match_players('Marvin Harrison Jr. torches secondary', known_names=['Marvin Harrison','Marvin Harrison Jr.'])` returns BOTH mentions, neither with ambiguous=True. Contrast the PFK provider, which does build an explicit ambiguity flag for normalized-key collisions (src/news/providers/pfk.py:120-131 `ambiguous=len(names) > 1`) — the RSS path has no equivalent, and PlayerMention.ambiguous defaults False (base.py:64).
findings.userImpact: The false mention is then treated as authoritative everywhere downstream: _enrich_player_mentions stamps it with the wrong player's position/team (service.py:212-224 only skips already-flagged ambiguous mentions), it produces a digest entry (digest.py:88-90 skips only ambiguous), and — most consequentially — it feeds apply_injury_impact (terminal.py:1562), so a headline about the son discounts the father's value.

findings.title: injury_impact's own docstring contradicts its constants: it advertises a 60% cap and severity tiers that the classifier cannot produce
findings.evidence: src/api/injury_impact.py:63-64 'Values are capped at 60% total discount'; :175 the return-shape docstring says `"appliedDiscountPct": float (0-60)`. The actual constant is :91 `_MAX_DISCOUNT_PCT: float = 5.0`. The same docstring at :44-48 defines the tiers as 'alert -> severe, career-impacting (Achilles, ACL, spinal); watch -> mid-grade (high-ankle, hamstring Gr 2, concussion); info -> soft-tissue / day-to-day', but the only thing that assigns severity is _rss.classify, where `concussion` is an ALERT keyword (_rss.py:37), `questionable`/`doubtful` are ALERT keywords (:41-42), and `info` means no keyword matched at all — i.e. not a soft-tissue injury but no injury information whatsoever.
findings.userImpact: Anyone reading the module to decide whether to trust injuryAdjustedValue gets a description of a body-part-aware severity model that does not exist; what exists is a 19-keyword regex over an entire RSS description.

findings.title: Snap-share percentage is 0-100 in src/playerctx and 0-1 in src/nfl_data, with no shared constant
findings.evidence: src/playerctx/normalize.py:395-397 `pcts = [g[pct_key] * 100.0 for g in games]` -> `"pct": round(season_mean, 1)` (0-100; docs/playerctx.md confirms 'per-player mean snap % (0-100)'), rendered as `{Number(snaps.pct).toFixed(1)}%` in frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx. Meanwhile src/nfl_data/actuals_store.py:466-471 stores pcts 'as 0..1 fractions ... which is the scale ``usage_signals._ACTIVE_STARTER_SNAP_PCT`` already assumes', and src/news/usage_signals.py:41 `_ACTIVE_STARTER_SNAP_PCT = 0.50` compares against it directly (usage_signals.py:159).
findings.userImpact: Any future code joining the two snap surfaces (e.g. wiring the depth-chart cross-check that depth_charts.py:263 documents as taking 'raw pct' with min_snap_delta_pct=0.05) is one line away from a 100x error. usage_confirms_slot_change already takes a snap_share_delta_pct whose scale is stated only in prose.

findings.area: News + player context + NFL data (src/news, src/playerctx, src/nfl_data) with routes /api/news, /api/playerctx/player, /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized, /api/a
findings.title: Sleeper trending items stamp fetch time as the event timestamp, so they never age and always sort to the top
findings.evidence: src/news/providers/sleeper.py::_row_to_item -> `ts=to_iso_utc(now)` where `now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)` is taken once per fetch. The upstream row carries only {player_id, count} with a lookback window, no event time. The service sorts by (severity_rank, ts) (service.py:157-171) and drops items older than 7 days (service.py:127-147).
findings.userImpact: Trending adds/drops are structurally the freshest items in every feed and can never be aged out, so they crowd genuine reporting out of the top of the ticker and the digest ordering. They also always score decay=1.0 in injury_impact (injury_impact.py:266-273), maximising a trending-DROP item's 0.5-base discount.

findings.area: News + player context + NFL data (src/news, src/playerctx, src/nfl_data) with routes /api/news, /api/playerctx/player, /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized, /api/a
findings.title: PFK articles with no <lastmod> are stamped at the Unix epoch and therefore dropped, contradicting the code comment that says they merely sink
findings.evidence: src/news/providers/pfk.py comment 'Newest first; undated entries sink to the bottom rather than masquerading as fresh news on every refresh' followed by `ts=to_iso_utc(lastmod) if lastmod else to_iso_utc(epoch)` where `epoch = datetime.fromtimestamp(0, tz=timezone.utc)`. src/news/service.py:141-146 then drops anything older than `now - 7*86400`, so every undated PFK article is discarded, not sunk.
findings.userImpact: PFK coverage silently loses any article whose sitemap entry lacks a lastmod. The provider reports ok=True with a lower count, which is indistinguishable from a quiet publishing week.

findings.title: /api/news computes playerDigests over up to 100 items, then truncates items to ?limit, so digests can cite item ids absent from the response
findings.evidence: server.py:4623 `payload = aggregated.to_dict()` — to_dict builds `"playerDigests": build_player_digests(self.items)` (service.py:118-122) from the already-capped-at-100 list. server.py:4625-4627 then `payload["items"] = payload["items"][:limit]; payload["count"] = len(payload["items"])`. playerDigests is left untouched, and each digest carries `"itemIds": [s.id for s in stories]` (digest.py).
findings.userImpact: A caller requesting ?limit=20 receives digests whose storyCount and itemIds reference stories not in the payload. The /news page's coverage strip compares filteredDigests.length against coverage.digests (page.jsx:205-220), so the counts can disagree. Low impact today because the only frontend caller requests the full 100 (news-service.js NEWS_FETCH_LIMIT = 100).

findings.title: /api/admin/nfl-data/flush reports twice the true number of evicted cache entries

Every cache entry is two files — src/nfl_data/cache.py:53-55 `return cache_dir / f"{h}.json", cache_dir / f"{h}.meta.json"`. I verified on disk: data/nfl_data_cache/ holds 3 entries and 6 files.

findings.title: injury_impact's age ladder is inert for its highest-impact case, and the test that claims to prove otherwise asserts only >=
findings.evidence: src/api/injury_impact.py:281 `discount = base * pos_mult * age_mult * decay` with `_MAX_DISCOUNT_PCT = 5.0` (:91). For alert+RB: age 29-31 gives 4.0 x 1.20 x 1.20 = 5.76 and age 32+ gives 4.0 x 1.20 x 1.40 = 6.72 — both clamp to 5.00, so the 29-31 vs 32+ distinction has no effect. tests/api/test_injury_impact.py:109-125 test_aging_rb_gets_heavier_discount compares age 22 against age 33 and asserts `old["appliedDiscountPct"] >= young["appliedDiscountPct"]`, which passes on equality and would keep passing if the age ladder were deleted.
findings.userImpact: The documented age sensitivity (injury_impact.py:56-61) is unreachable for the position most sensitive to injury, which is the case the model was built for.

findings.title: injury_impact's unit tests construct severity/impact combinations the production pipeline cannot emit, which is why the dead watch tier survived
findings.evidence: tests/api/test_injury_impact.py:39-53 `_season_news(severity, ..., impact: str | None = "negative", ...)` — every fixture defaults to impact="negative", including the watch item at :180 `_season_news("watch", hours_ago=2, headline="Hamstring")`. No production provider emits (severity="watch", impact="negative"): _rss.py:99-101 returns "positive" for every watch item and sleeper.py returns "positive" for every add (its only watch kind). Every test in the file drives compute_injury_discount with hand-built dicts; none imports src.news.providers._rss.classify.
findings.userImpact: The full watch tier (BASE_DISCOUNT_PCT 2.0) is unreachable in production and the suite reports it working. The same fixture gap hides the fact that info severity — no keyword match — is the tier that actually fires most often.

findings.evidence: src/nfl_data/injury_feed.py:45-56 _ACTIVE_STATUSES includes "INJURED_RESERVE" and "PHYSICALLY_UNABLE", but the membership test at :219 runs on the OUTPUT of _normalize_status (:83-104), which maps INJURED_RESERVE -> "IR" and PHYSICALLY_UNABLE -> "PUP". findings.title: fetch_opportunity_stats re-scans the full multi-year play-by-play list once per requested year
findings.evidence: src/nfl_data/opportunity_stats.py `for year in years: stats = build_opportunity_from_pbp(pbp, season=year); all_stats.extend(stats)` — pbp holds every requested year's rows, and build_opportunity_from_pbp filters by season internally (`if season is not None and play_season != season: continue`). Three seasons of pbp is roughly 150k plays, so this is a 450k-iteration walk to produce the same result as one pass.
findings.userImpact: None today (module unreachable outside tests), but it is a 3-5x avoidable cost on a path the docstring positions as a nightly aggregate.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: Sleeper-derived draft capital: 53.7% of every non-default league's $1200 board is a hardcoded constant, and pick ownership assumes roster_id == draft slot
findings.evidence: src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:96-99 — `flat = {1: 7000.0, 2: 4000.0, 3: 2000.0, 4: 1200.0, 5: 700.0, 6: 300.0}; return flat.get(round_num, 100.0)`. :175 — `for season in (current_season, current_season + 1):`. :178 — `original_rid = slot  # stand-in: slot N = original owner roster N`. Live data check: exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json carries 72 rows named '2026 Pick R.SS' and ZERO rows named '2027 Pick R.SS' (2027 exists only as 18 'Early/Mid/Late Nth' tier rows). Every 2027 pick therefore takes the flat table. I summed the real 2026 R1-R4 rankDerivedValues from a freshly built contract: 147,020. The fabricated 2027 half: (7000+4000+2000+1200)*12 = 170,400. Fabricated share of the normalized budget = 53.7%. A fabricated 2027 R1 renders at $26.46 against a real 2026 1.01 at $29.60 — 89% of the best pick in the draft. Separately, data/sleeper_last_good.json shows roster_id 12 = 'Blaine' holding pick '2026 1.02', so roster_id and draft slot differ; the slot-as-roster-id assumption mislabels owners AND looks up the wrong slot's value.
findings.userImpact: Any user on a non-default league sees a draft-capital board where more than half the dollars are invented round constants and the team names attached to picks are wrong whenever roster_id != draft slot. The payload is labelled only 'Sleeper-derived, flat per-round valuation' — nothing distinguishes the fabricated rows from the Hill-curve-calibrated ones, which is exactly the failure tests/api/test_draft_capital_data_not_ready.py was written to prevent.

findings.title: FAAB bid desk computes its share-of-pool denominator over draft picks, understating every recommended bid by ~2.6x versus the same formula elsewhere
findings.evidence: server.py:4967-4983 — `for row in arr: ... if rname in rostered_norms: continue ... if v > top_pool_value: top_pool_value = v`, with no asset-class, position, or value filter; passed at server.py:5139 as `top_value_in_pool=top_pool_value`. Draft picks live in playersArray and are never in a team's `players` name list, so they always survive the filter. I computed the pool from the live contract joined against data/sleeper_last_good.json (665 rostered names): top_pool_value = 7831, and the row is '2026 Pick 1.01'. The best actual free agent is Marlin Klein (TE) at 1905. Feeding both through src/trade/waiver.py:88-94: with top=7831, share = 0.2433 -> aggressive_pct = 0.1108 -> aggressive $11, reasonable $8. With top=1905 (the denominator src/trade/waiver.py:191-194 uses for the identical concept), share = 1.0 -> aggressive $30, reasonable $21. Ratio 2.62x.
findings.userImpact: The headline number on /waivers — the FAAB bid desk — recommends $8 where the same formula on the same board recommends $21. Users following it lose contested claims by a factor of two and a half. Because the denominator is a pick that no waiver pool contains, the error is invisible to inspection.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: Three divergent implementations of one FAAB formula, two of them rendered side by side on /waivers
findings.evidence: The same `0.05 + 0.25*share` formula exists at src/trade/waiver.py:80-95 (Python), and is ported verbatim to frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js:864-879 (JS, comment at :851 says 'JS port of src/trade/waiver.py::_compute_faab_bid'). Each caller supplies a different denominator: server.py:4967 = all unrostered rows incl. picks (7831 live); src/trade/waiver.py:191 = filtered candidates (1905 live); frontend/app/waivers/page.jsx:166-175 = max over the ~20 bestMoves rows currently rendered. The frontend also hardcodes `leagueBudget: 100` at waivers/page.jsx:213 and :219, while the backend resolves the real budget at server.py:5051-5060. And `league_budget` means REMAINING dollars in one Python caller (src/trade/waiver.py:202 passes `user_faab_remaining`) but LEAGUE budget in the other (src/trade/faab_recommender.py:322-326).
findings.userImpact: On the /waivers page the 'FAAB hint' column and the bid desk below it disagree for the same player. Because the frontend denominator is the max of the displayed batch, the top row of that column always reads exactly $21 no matter who the player is — an artifact users will read as a real number. A user in a $200 league gets frontend hints computed against $100.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: League position calibration collapses a 19x player-value spread into a 1.12x bid spread
findings.evidence: src/trade/faab_recommender.py:191-194 — `blended = 0.5 * float(avg_for_pos) + 0.5 * float(bid_estimate)`, gated only on `count_for_pos >= 3` (:186). `avg_for_pos` comes from src/api/faab_analytics.py, which appends every winning bid for that position across every season with no player-quality stratification. Worked example using the test suite's own TE average of $30 and the live endpoint denominator: value 1905 -> baseline $8 -> blended $19; value 1500 -> $18; value 1000 -> $18; value 700 -> $18; value 500 -> $18; value 300 -> $17; value 100 -> $17. A 19.05x range in player value produces a 1.12x range in recommended bid.
findings.userImpact: Once a position has three historical bids, the recommendation stops discriminating between a genuine league-winner and a dart throw — it returns the position's historical average plus or minus a dollar. That is worse than the uncalibrated formula, because the number now looks league-aware.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: A blocked partial scrape is recorded as a success, so monitoring reports 100% health while the board is frozen
findings.evidence: server.py:2364 `if total_sites > 0 and site_count < total_sites / 2:` — the not-promoted branch — calls `_mark_scrape_success(elapsed, player_count, site_count, total_sites)` at server.py:2380 before `return latest_data`. _mark_scrape_success (server.py:1013-1051) sets last_success_at, clears `error`, sets current_step 'complete', increments scrape_count, records `_record_scrape_history('success', ...)` and bumps `_metrics['scrape_total']` without touching `scrape_failures`. Consequently `_scrape_success_rate_24h` (server.py:1104-1125) counts it as a success and /api/health's `is_ok` (server.py:4426-4431) sees no last_error.
findings.userImpact: The exact failure the guard exists to catch — sites down or blocking — produces a green dashboard. The only signal is a send_alert email, which is subject to the global 1h cooldown described below.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: The partial-scrape promotion gate's denominator is 2, not the 22 sources that build the board
findings.evidence: server.py:2358-2364 counts `site_count` and `total_sites` over `result.get('sites', [])`. Live export exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json has `sites` = [('ktc', 500), ('idpTradeCalc', 900)] — two entries. I built the canonical contract from that export and counted canonicalSiteValues coverage: 22 distinct sources contribute (idpTradeCalc 911, ktc 609, ktcSfTep 501, pfkDynasty 475, fantasyProsSf 473, fantasyNavigatorSf 455, otcffbSf 450, flockFantasySf 415, draftSharks 415, fantasyCalc 393, yahooBoone 376, dynastyDaddySf 364, idpShow 349, draftSharksIdp 301, fantasyProsFitzmaurice 299, dynastyNerdsSfTep 293, dlfSf 280, fantasyProsIdp 211, dlfIdp 171, dlfRookieSf 110, flockFantasySfRookies 76, dlfRookieIdp 29). server.py:4200-4204 already acknowledges the `sites` list 'cannot detect a degraded board' for source_health, but the promotion gate was never updated with it.
findings.userImpact: A scrape in which all 20 CSV-fed sources silently went stale but KTC and IDPTC responded passes the gate and promotes. The board's blend quality can collapse without the guard ever firing.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: Custom `value_crosses` alerts are level tests, not crossing tests — they re-fire every 24 hours forever
findings.evidence: src/news/custom_alerts.py:230-232 — `crossed = (direction == 'above' and v >= threshold) or (direction == 'below' and v <= threshold)`. No prior value is stored: mark_fired (:280-286) writes only `{'lastFiredAt': ...}` and _is_cooldown (:149-160) only compares that timestamp against COOLDOWN_HOURS = 24. The module docstring at :5-8 says 'fires when rankDerivedValue CROSSES a target' and 'the rule fires once per cooldown window when the threshold is crossed in the configured direction'.
findings.userImpact: A user who sets 'alert me when Player X goes above 7000' gets an email and a push notification every single day for as long as the player stays above 7000. With 50 rules allowed per user (server.py:10031), a handful of satisfied rules turns the daily sweep into a spam engine, and users will disable notifications entirely — losing the signal alerts too.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: /api/movers anchors on the first snapshot present rather than the requested window, so the labelled '14d' delta can be a 2-day delta
findings.evidence: server.py:3390 `history = _rank_history.load_history(days=window + 1)`, and src/api/rank_history.py:369 implements that as `windowed = entries[-max(1, int(days)):]` — the last N SNAPSHOTS, not N days. server.py:3445 then takes `anchor = series[0]` with no date check whatsoever; the entry's `date` field is read only for `asOf` at :3501. The frontend renders the result as 'Rank deltas vs. {windowDays}d ago' (frontend/components/terminal/MoversPanel.jsx:166).
findings.userImpact: For any player who entered the board recently, or during any period where scrapes were missed (the log is appended only on fresh-scrape promotion, server.py:1858), the reported delta covers an unknown and shorter or longer interval than the label claims. A 20-spot rise 'over 14 days' may have happened in 2 days, or over 40 days if the log has gaps. The panel is presented as buy-low / sell-high guidance.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: Movers panel labels risers as buy-low and fallers as sell-high — inverted
findings.evidence: server.py:3444-3449 defines `delta = r_then - r_now` with rank-smaller-better, so `delta > 0` means the player's rank IMPROVED and they are appended to `risers` (server.py:3494-3495). frontend/components/terminal/MoversPanel.jsx:192-193 renders that list under 'Risers — buy-low candidates', and :207-208 renders `fallers` (rank got worse) under 'Fallers — sell-high candidates'.
findings.userImpact: The panel tells the user to buy players who have just appreciated and sell players who have just depreciated — the opposite of the strategy the labels name. This is a direct trade recommendation on the terminal.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: Signal alerts mark themselves delivered before delivery is attempted, so a failed send is silently dropped for 12 hours or forever
findings.evidence: src/api/signal_alerts.py:198-201 sets `new_state[state_key] = {'signal': signal, 'notifiedAt': now}` inside detect_signal_transitions, and :211-231 persists it to user_kv unconditionally. process_user_alerts (:290-323) only THEN calls `delivery(...)` and, on exception, returns `{'delivered': False, 'reason': 'delivery_error:...'}` (:319-323) without any state rollback. The `no_email` (:298) and `no_delivery_configured` (:304) branches have the same shape.
findings.userImpact: An SMTP outage during the daily sweep loses that day's signal alerts permanently. Because the state now records the new signal, the 'signal != prev_signal' condition at :171 will not re-fire unless the signal changes again. Silent, and there is no retry.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: send_alert uses one global 1-hour cooldown across all subjects, and /api/health burns it on backup staleness
findings.evidence: server.py:227 `ALERT_COOLDOWN_SEC = 3600` and server.py:236-239 `if now - _last_alert_time < ALERT_COOLDOWN_SEC: log.info(f'Alert suppressed (cooldown): {subject}'); return` — a single module-level `_last_alert_time` shared by every caller. server.py:4472-4478 calls send_alert from inside get_health whenever `newestBackupAgeHours` is None or > 36. /api/health is polled every 60s by the frontend StaleDataBanner (per the comment at server.py:1524-1526) and every 300s by the uptime watchdog.
findings.userImpact: With backups stale — which is exactly when other things are likely wrong — a scrape failure (server.py:2447-2450), a partial-scrape block (server.py:2369-2379), a disk-space emergency (server.py:2402-2411) or an uptime outage (server.py:2528-2538) will be silently suppressed. The operator gets one backup email an hour and nothing else.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: The rookie dollar board silently reshapes by up to +65% when the Draft Data workbook cannot be read
findings.evidence: server.py:7109-7131 — `_read_sheet_spine_and_floor` wraps the whole read in `try/except Exception: return [1.0] * n, 0` and _load_draft_workbook (server.py:7083-7107) returns None on `ImportError` for openpyxl. A flat spine makes `excess[i] = max(0, 1.0 - 1) = 0` for every row (server.py:7186), so `term2` is all zeros and the 0.4-weighted half of server.py:7194 vanishes. I ran both paths on the live rookie board: with the workbook spine, picks 1-12 are [135.5, 105.5, 91.5, 82.0, 76.0, 68.5, 60.0, 53.0, 48.0, 43.0, 39.0, 34.5]; without it they are [122.0, 101.0, 92.0, 86.0, 82.0, 77.5, 73.5, 68.0, 65.5, 62.0, 59.5, 57.0]. Pick 12 moves from $34.50 to $57.00, +65%. sum(C) drops from 1200.0 to 753.6, but the R1-carryover mechanism at server.py:7228-7237 absorbs the shortfall so the TOTAL still reads exactly 1200 and nothing in the payload changes. openpyxl is listed in requirements.txt:33 but is not installed in this audit environment, so the degraded path is reachable in practice.
findings.userImpact: A missing dependency or an unreadable workbook produces a completely different auction board that passes every visible invariant (sums to $1200, monotone, correct row count). Nothing in the response distinguishes it. Users bid real money off it.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: _ktc_decay_curve is off by one slot, overvaluing every extrapolated rookie by exp(k)
findings.evidence: server.py:6825-6826 — `k = (math.log(v1) - math.log(vn)) / (n - 1)` then `A = v1 * math.exp(k)  # A = v1 / e^(-k*0) adjusted so pick index 0 → v1`. The comment asserts the curve passes through v1 at i=0, but A*exp(-k*0) = v1*exp(k) != v1. Numeric check on a realistic 40-rookie board (v1 9999, vn 800): k = 0.06476, exp(k) = 1.0669, curve at i=0 = 10,668 not 9,999. Synthetic picks 41-48 come out [800, 750, 703, 659, 617, 579, 542, 508] where the correct fit gives [750, 703, 659, 617, 579, 542, 508, 477] — each extrapolated pick receives the value belonging to the slot above it. Systematic +6.7% overvaluation.
findings.userImpact: Only reachable when _our_rookie_pool is empty (rookieSource == 'ktc_fallback'), which is not the live case today — the live contract has 127 rookies with playerIds. But when it fires, the tail of the rookie board is uniformly inflated and the ordering relative to real KTC entries is distorted at the boundary.

findings.area: server.py inline decision logic (routes, thresholds, and math implemented directly in the 12,683-line FastAPI monolith), plus the src/ modules those routes call
findings.title: /api/health computes any_breaker_open after deciding the status, so an open circuit breaker never degrades health — contradicting the comment beside it
findings.evidence: server.py:4426 `is_ok = (...)` and server.py:4432 `status = 'ok' if is_ok else 'degraded'` both execute before server.py:4455 `circuits = _circuits_safe()` and server.py:4457 `any_breaker_open = any(c.get('state') == 'open' for c in circuits)`. The comment on server.py:4456 reads 'Any breaker in OPEN state flips overall status to degraded.' The variable is only emitted as a response field at server.py:4501 and never read.
findings.userImpact: An open circuit breaker on a source or an external dependency leaves /api/health returning HTTP 200 'ok'. Any monitor wired to the status code — including the uptime watchdog at server.py:2466-2486, which treats 200-399 as up — sees a healthy service.

findings.evidence: server.py:7173-7180 — `decay_rate = max(0.03, min(0.08, 0.6 * head_std / head_mean))`. findings.title: The unified mapper's fuzzy fallback accepts demonstrably different players at its default threshold
findings.evidence: src/identity/unified_mapper.py:359-361 `if best_p and best_score >= min_confidence: return _to_resolved(best_p, confidence=best_score, method='fuzzy_name')` with `min_confidence: float = 0.85` at :246 and _fuzzy_score returning a raw difflib SequenceMatcher ratio (:188). Measured with the module's own function on normalized names: 'mike williams' vs 'mykel williams' 0.8889 (WR vs DL); 'brian thomas' vs 'ian thomas' 0.9091 (WR vs TE); 'cedric gray' vs 'eric gray' 0.9000 (LB vs RB); 'tyler allgeier' vs 'tyler alger' 0.8800. docs/identity-audit-2026-07.md:210-211 independently verified the first three as DIFFERENT players. findings.title: resolve_many rebuilds the entire Sleeper directory index on every row, contradicting its own docstring
findings.evidence: src/identity/unified_mapper.py:269 `idx = _index_directory(players_dir)` sits inside resolve_player, so it runs per call, and resolve_many at :417 calls resolve_player once per input row. Its docstring at :409-411 states the opposite: 'Used by nightly jobs ... so the mapper's internal index is built once, not per-row.' src/playerctx/normalize.py:551 independently documents the problem ('resolve_player re-indexes the pool on every ...') and builds its own indexes to avoid it. Secondary: at :95 `if _OVERRIDES_PATH_CACHE == target and _OVERRIDES_CACHE` — an empty override map is falsy, so an empty-but-present overrides file causes a disk read on every call.
findings.userImpact: A batch resolve over N rows against Sleeper's ~11k-player directory is O(N × 11000) index construction. For a nightly ingest of a few thousand rows that is tens of millions of redundant dict writes. The docstring actively misleads anyone deciding whether resolve_many is safe to call in a loop.

findings.title: The pool builder merges players by name with no position guard, discarding the loser's Sleeper ID
findings.evidence: src/pool/builder.py:451-459: on a pool_normalize_lookup collision the second Sleeper entry is merged into the first, and `if not row.sleeper_id and entry.get('sleeper_id')` (:456) means the second player's id is kept only when the first had none. KTC rows merge on the same bare key at :480-486 while carrying `position: ''` by construction (:298), so a KTC value can attach to the wrong same-named player. pool_normalize_lookup strips Jr/Sr/II/III (:208), so 'Marvin Harrison Jr.' and 'Marvin Harrison' produce one key. findings.title: The dynamic weight fitter cannot distinguish a good source from an anti-predictive one
findings.evidence: src/backtesting/dynamic_weights.py:71 `weights_raw = {a.source: math.exp(max(0.0, a.spearman_rho + 1.0)) for a in eligible}` then :73 `normalized = {s: max(floor, w / total) ...}` with floor 0.05, then renormalize. Reproduced numerically with 22 sources spanning Spearman rho +0.9 to −0.9: best source weight 0.06216, worst (rho −0.9, systematically wrong) 0.041396 — a 1.50:1 ratio. With 5 sources spanning rho 0.9→0.5: 0.2205 vs 0.1805, a 1.22:1 ratio. The exp(rho+1) shift compresses the whole possible accuracy range into a factor of e² = 7.39 before the floor compresses it further.
findings.userImpact: If the flag were flipped on, a source that ranks players backwards would keep about two-thirds the influence of a perfect source. The mechanism cannot deliver the stated goal in docs/backtest_methodology.md §7-12. tests/backtesting/test_dynamic_weights.py:17-29 asserts normalization and the floor but never asserts any minimum separation between a high-rho and a low-rho source, so the weakness is not pinned.

findings.title: Four parameter 'backtests' optimize board stability, which is maximized by discarding sources
findings.evidence: scripts/backtest_alpha_shrinkage.py:87-113, backtest_percentile_reference_n.py:72-91, backtest_soft_fallback.py:84-102 and backtest_alpha_lambda_joint.py all use a byte-identical stability_metric = mean |rank_t+1 − rank_t| over top-200 players. There is no outcome label anywhere. The published results prove the objective is degenerate: reports/alpha_shrinkage_backtest_full.md recommends 'Promote α = 0.00' (pure anchor — 20 other sources discarded); reports/soft_fallback_backtest_full.md recommends distance 0.00; reports/alpha_lambda_joint_backtest_full.md states it outright — 'this metric rewards stability. The stability optimum drifts toward α=0 and λ=0 — "use the anchor source alone, ignore the 15 other sources." That's product-bad'. scripts/backtest_percentile_reference_n.py:150-155 is prepared to print 'The design-choice justification (KTC pool size, retail market scale) is empirically validated' on the strength of that churn metric. None of the four resamples or reports an interval. A player absent from the next snapshot is silently skipped (alpha_shrinkage.py:101-102), so a parameter that pushes players off the board scores better.
findings.userImpact: Three produce a printed 'Recommendation' a reader would take as an empirical result. Two of the three were correctly ignored in production (_ALPHA_SHRINKAGE is 0.10 at data_contract.py:5025, not 0.00; _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N is 500 at :4933, not 400), so the live constants are hand-picks with a misleading paper trail behind them. One WAS adopted: _MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA = 0.0 at :5059 — a live mechanism switched off on the strength of a churn metric, and reports/mad_lambda_backtest_full.md itself flags the gap ('Consider whether a different optimization target (e.g. KTC alignment) would favour a non-zero λ before committing to remove the feature').

findings.title: Every stability sweep is permanently irreproducible because retention prunes its inputs
findings.evidence: All four sweeps read data/dynasty_data_*.json (backtest_alpha_shrinkage.py:60-61 and identical loaders in the other three). `ls data/dynasty_data_*.json` returns 'No such file or directory'. src/maintenance/retention.py:25-27 and :410 prune that glob at 45 days. The four published reports all state 'Snapshot count: 25, Date range: 2026-03-23 → 2026-04-16' — a window that has been deleted. reports/ktc_volatility_backtest_full.md is worse: its header records 'Hill constants: midpoint=48.44, slope=1.149', no longer the live values (src/canonical/player_valuation.py:82-83 reads 65.4 / 0.910). reports/backtest_blend_params.md is fully orphaned: it tunes _BLEND_MEAN_WEIGHT, _BLEND_ROBUST_WEIGHT and _VOLATILITY_COMPRESSION_FLOOR/CEIL — none of which exist in src/api/data_contract.py — and reports an optimal RANKING_SOURCES[idpTradeCalc].weight of 3.0 when the live registry has all 21 sources at 1.0; the generating script is not in the repo.
findings.userImpact: Seven markdown reports sit in reports/ with tables of numbers, no staleness marker, and no way to re-derive them. A reader cannot check any of them, and at least two describe parameters since removed from the codebase.

findings.title: The VA formula calibration fits and scores 12 candidate families on the same 152 points, with regularization chosen by in-sample error
findings.evidence: scripts/calibrate_va_formula.py:920-1223. Every family is grid-searched to minimize in-sample RMS (grid_search(..., metric='rms')) and all 12 are then ranked on that same in-sample RMS at :1200-1222. A grep for holdout / cross_val / train / split / leave_one over the file finds only the word 'training' inside a docstring at :596. For V11, :1136-1141 sweeps ridge alpha over (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 5.0, 25.0, 100.0) computing `rms = objective(predict_v11, params, metric='rms')` on the training data, then :1146 selects `min(v11_results, key=lambda r: r[2])` — the alpha with the lowest IN-SAMPLE error, which always favours alpha=0, labelled by the code itself as 'plain OLS (max overfitting risk on 46 training points × 8 features)'. V12 is KTC's published formula with zero free parameters, ranked head-to-head against 11 families collectively searching 3,838,056 combinations (measured: V6 1,560,650; V9 945,000; V8 756,000; V3 236,544; V7 109,760; V4 87,120; V5 72,576; V10 52,488; V1 15,552; V2 2,366).
findings.userImpact: The ranking table the operator uses to pick which formula to port into frontend/lib/trade-logic.js is an in-sample fit contest, so the most flexible family wins by construction and its reported error understates what a user sees on a trade the calibration never saw. The regularization sweep that exists to control this is decided by the metric it is supposed to trade off. Practically: at ~583M pure-Python predict() calls the script produced no output in 8+ minutes on this machine before I terminated it — it was sized for 13 points and the grids were never reduced when the dataset grew to 152.

findings.title: stamp_tiers_on_players misaligns tier IDs whenever any row lacks a position
findings.evidence: src/scoring/tiering.py:199-200: `tiers = detect_tiers(rows, ...)` then `by_id = {id(rows[i]): tiers[i].tier_id for i in range(len(tiers))}`. But detect_tiers returns a FILTERED list — :186 `return [result_map[id(r)] for r in rows if isinstance(r, dict) and id(r) in result_map]` — and rows with no pos/position never enter result_map (:139-141). So len(tiers) < len(rows) whenever any row lacks a position, and the positional zip at :200 pairs tiers[i] with rows[i] rather than with the row that produced it. Worked through: rows = [A(no pos), B(QB), C(QB)] yields tiers = [tierB, tierC], so A is stamped with B's tier, B with C's tier, and C is stamped with nothing. tests/scoring/test_tiering.py exercises detect_tiers at :22, :30, :38, :45 but never calls stamp_tiers_on_players.
findings.userImpact: Currently unexposed — stamp_tiers_on_players has no caller outside scripts/refit_tier_thresholds.py and the feature flag is NO_GATE/OFF (src/api/feature_flags.py:72). But its docstring advertises it as 'Safe to call from the contract builder when the positional_tiers feature flag is on', which is the exact call that would trip it, and the live board does carry rows with no position (the 2026-08-04 export has an unsupported-position 'Brandon Knight' row).
